output: A study looked at two ways to use steroids to help people with a condition called primary sclerosing cholangitis. In one study, they gave some patients a steroid called hydrocortisone through their bile ducts. But this didn't work better than giving them a saline solution. In fact, it seemed to cause more problems like pancreatitis and infections. Because these problems happened more often, the study was stopped early. Another study compared another steroid, budesonide, to a different one, prednisone. They found that patients had higher levels of a substance called bilirubin when they took prednisone. However, there wasn't enough information to say if either steroid helped or hurt the condition overall. So, right now, there's no clear evidence about whether taking steroids by mouth helps people with this condition. Using steroids directly in the bile duct seems to cause serious side effects.

output: This study looked at two groups of people to see if taking certain vitamins could help their blood flow better. In one group of 133 people, those who took folic acid or a form called 5-MTHF had slightly better blood flow to their legs than those who didn't take anything. This was seen in both cases, but it wasn't very strong - just a little bit better. Another small group of 18 people didn't show any difference in blood flow whether they took a special vitamin pill or not. There were no serious problems reported. While these results suggest that these vitamins might help, we don't have enough information yet to tell everyone to start taking them. More studies are needed to know for sure.

output: This research looked at five different ways to do a procedure called amniocentesis or CVS, which helps doctors check if a baby might have problems before birth. They studied 1049 women who had these procedures. Three studies looked at adding medicine into a muscle, using a special medicine spray, or picking where to put the needle for a later time. Two studies looked at giving a different medicine to help relax the body before the procedure. None of these changes showed that they helped more than usual. Also, studies on another medicine and a special way to move the needle did not show any benefits either. The information we have isn't strong enough to change how doctors usually do these procedures. So, doctors should keep doing what they normally do. But if doctors do new studies that are done very well and have lots of people in them, it could help us know better how to do these procedures.

output: A review looked at five studies done in the UK to see if changing how long doctors spend with each patient affects things like the time spent in appointments, the number of tests ordered, the number of medicines given, and how happy patients feel. The studies weren't perfect because some didn't pick their own groups fairly, and there weren't many people in them. Because the studies weren't very good, we're not sure if changing doctor visits would make much difference. We also don't know if it would save money or use more money. Right now, we don't have enough information to decide if changing doctor visit times is a good idea. But if doctors do more studies that are better, we might learn more about this in the future. More studies are needed to look at how these changes affect health and costs.

output: This research looked at whether giving zinc to children helps prevent them from getting sick with pneumonia. They checked six studies that involved 5193 children. The studies found that giving zinc made pneumonia happen less often by about 13%. Also, it made pneumonia less common among these children by about 41%. But when they looked at different ways of checking if a child has pneumonia, zinc didn't seem to help much. Giving zinc seemed to work better when doctors could see something unusual in the lungs, like when a chest X-ray shows trouble breathing. However, zinc didn’t seem to help when doctors just looked for signs of fast breathing and a bit of chest indrawing. Overall, zinc seems to help reduce the chances of children getting pneumonia, but more research is needed to be sure.

We don't know if this treatment helps more than having surgery. We need bigger studies with lots of people over a long time to find out if it works. It's also important to see if it makes breathing easier and helps with how people feel overall.

output: This study looked at six different groups of people who had foot sores on their feet because they have diabetes. They wanted to know if special bandages called foam dressings help these sores heal faster than regular bandages or other types of special bandages. Two studies showed that foam dressings didn't seem to help the sores heal any better than regular bandages. Another two studies found that foam dressings didn't heal the sores any faster than another type of special bandage. One study also found no difference between foam dressings and another type of special bandage. The problem is that all the studies were small and didn't follow the people long enough to see if the dressings really helped. So far, there's not enough good evidence to say that foam dressings work better than other types of dressings for healing foot sores in people with diabetes. But it might be worth considering which type of dressing might work best based on things like how much the dressing costs and how well it handles the extra fluid that comes out of the sores.

output: In a study looking at two ways to prevent pregnancy, researchers found that a special piece of material called a sponge was less effective than another method called a diaphragm. In one big study done in the USA, 17 out of every 100 women who used the sponge had a baby after 12 months, compared to only 13 out of 100 using the diaphragm. In a smaller study in the UK, this difference was even bigger—24 out of 100 women using the sponge had a baby, while only 11 out of 100 using the diaphragm did. Also, more women stopped using the sponge because it made them uncomfortable, while fewer stopped using the diaphragm. The sponge also caused more allergic reactions, but the diaphragm sometimes caused discomfort too. Since then, no new studies have been found. More research is needed to see if the sponge might help stop some sicknesses spread by sex or cause other problems.

output: A study looked at fifteen different medical treatments for a type of treatment called IVF (in-vitro fertilization). Out of these, only three were considered good enough to look at closely. These three studies compared four different ways to prepare a woman's body before trying to get pregnant using her eggs. One study found that fewer baby eggs were collected when using a longer treatment plan compared to other plans. Another study showed that more hormones were given during this longer treatment plan. Fewer women had their treatment cancelled because of problems when using the longer treatment plan. However, none of the studies found that any of these treatments led to more miscarriages or babies growing in the wrong place. Because there wasn't enough information from good studies, doctors don't know which treatment works best for preparing a woman's body before IVF. They need more studies to find out.

This study looked at different medicines called TCAs and SSRIs that doctors sometimes use to help people feel better when they're sad or depressed. They checked if these medicines work better than a sugar pill. There were 1364 people who took the medicine and 919 who took the sugar pill. Most of the studies only lasted for about 6 to 8 weeks.

The results showed that people who took TCAs were about 24% more likely to get better than those who took the sugar pill. For SSRIs, it was about 28% more likely. This means that out of every 100 people taking TCAs, about 9 would need to take the medicine to see some improvement. For SSRIs, about 7 people would need to take them to see improvement.

However, there were also some side effects that made people stop taking the medicine. For TCAs, about 4 to 30 people out of every 100 would have to stop because of side effects. For SSRIs, about 20 to 90 people out of every 100 would stop because of side effects.

So, both TCAs and SSRIs seem to be helpful for treating depression in regular doctor visits. But people might need to try a few different ones before finding one that works best for them.

output: This research looked at five studies about giving something called oral immunoglobulin to babies to help prevent a condition called NEC. Three of these studies had enough information to be included. In total, they studied 2095 babies. The studies didn't find that giving oral immunoglobulin helped reduce the chances of babies getting NEC, suspected NEC, needing surgery because of NEC, or dying from NEC. The studies also didn't find that giving just oral immunoglobulin A helped prevent NEC. Overall, based on the information we have, we don't think giving oral immunoglobulin helps prevent NEC in babies. There haven't been any other studies that only looked at giving oral immunoglobulin A to see if it helps prevent NEC.

output: A group looked at 30 ways doctors use to score how well something heals after an illness called ulcerative colitis (UC). They found out that only 11 of these ways have been checked to see if they work correctly. Eight ways had their own scores checked by the same doctor, but we're not sure how well different doctors agree on these scores. Three ways were checked to make sure they cover everything they should. Two ways were checked to see if they match up with other tests. Six ways were checked to see if they give useful information. Two ways were checked to see if they can show changes over time. The Nancy Index and the Robarts Index have been checked the most. They've been tested for several things like if they work correctly, if they cover everything, if they measure what they should, and if they match up with other tests. But no way has been fully checked yet. To find the best way to know when something is fully healed, more checking is needed. Finding this best way will help doctors better understand healing in people with UC.

Another study gave magnesium through their veins. But all the studies had some problems that made it hard to trust the results fully.

The studies didn't measure everything they wanted to measure, so we couldn't know if magnesium helps or hurts when someone stops drinking too much alcohol. Only one study checked if people had less shaking or confusion after taking magnesium. This study also looked at how strong someone's hands were. They found that people who took magnesium didn't get stronger hands than those who didn't take it. Also, there weren't any big problems with side effects in either group.

Overall, we don't have enough good information to say if magnesium helps or hurts when someone stops drinking too much alcohol. The studies weren't perfect, so we can't be very sure about what they found.

output: A study looked at 519 men who took a special medicine called B-sitosterols for 4 to 26 weeks. Some men got a type of B-sitosterol that didn't have sugar attached, while others got a form that had all the sugar attached. Both types helped men feel better when they went to the bathroom. They could go faster and had less leftover water in their bladder after peeing. One group that got a specific kind of B-sitosterol called WA184 also saw their pee flow get better. But B-sitosterols didn't make the prostate smaller. About 7.8% of men in each group stopped taking the medicine because of side effects. The study shows that B-sitosterols can help with bathroom problems, but we don't know if it works well over time or if it stops other health issues from happening. More research is needed to find out.

output: A few small studies looked at using a medicine called azathioprine to help people with asthma who also have other breathing problems. These studies had only about 23 people each, which isn't very many. The studies didn't find that the medicine helped people breathe better or feel less wheezy. One study did show that the medicine might make something called SGaw better, but it's not clear if this is important enough for people to use. Because the studies weren't done well and had too few people, we can't say for sure if the medicine works or not. We also couldn't find any new studies since last checking in 2010. Right now, there's no good proof that azathioprine helps people with asthma breathe better by taking less of another medicine called steroids. To know if it really works, we need big studies that follow people for a long time.

output: This study looked at different ways to help people who have a condition called Body Dysmorphic Disorder (BDD). They checked if medicines or talking therapies work better. Four small studies showed that medicines like fluoxetine helped more than a sugar pill. Also, two types of talking therapies called Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) seemed to help a lot too. One study found that CBT worked even better than another type of therapy. The medicines and CBT made the symptoms of BDD much better. But, only a few studies were done, so we need more to know for sure if they really work. We also need to see if they work in different groups of people, like teenagers, and with other medicines and types of therapy. More research is needed to fully understand how well these treatments work.

output: A group of doctors looked at many studies about helping women with a type of cancer called cervical cancer. They wanted to find ways to stop their blood from coming out of their vagina when they have this illness. The doctors checked 1522 different studies, but most of them didn't fit what they were looking for. They found 22 studies that seemed close, but these studies weren't done in a way that lets us know if one treatment is better than another. The doctors couldn't find any new studies since their last look at this topic. Because there aren't enough good studies, doctors will choose treatments based on what's available where the person lives. In places where it's hard to get advanced treatments, doctors might use radiotherapy, which is like using special lights to help. But they don't know if this works better than other treatments. So, the doctors think more studies are needed to see which treatment might work best for stopping blood from coming out of the vagina in women with this kind of cancer.

output: A review looked at 2079 studies about using games to teach people who work in hospitals. Out of these, only 8 studies were really good enough to look at closely. One study used a game like "Family Feud" to teach about stopping infections. It found that the people who played the game learned more than those who didn't play it. But another study compared a game called "Snakes and Ladders" to regular teaching methods for learning about preventing strokes. Both groups learned about the same amount right away and three months later. The game made people enjoy learning more. The review couldn't say if games help teach better because there wasn't enough good information. More studies are needed to find out if games really help people learn and do their jobs better.

The study found that babies who used the breathing machine for longer periods had a slightly higher chance of having air leak out of their lungs, but it wasn't clear if this happened more often. They also found that babies who used the breathing machine for longer periods had a tiny bit higher chance of dying before leaving the hospital, which might be due to other factors. The researchers think these results may not apply to today's babies because the babies in the study didn't get some new treatments like special medicines before birth or special breathing support after birth. Also, most of the babies in the study only had one health problem, and the study didn't look at babies with different kinds of lung problems. But the doctors noticed that babies with lungs that don't work well had a higher chance of having air leaks and dying when they used the breathing machine for longer periods. So, for babies whose lungs don't work very well, doctors should try to keep them on the breathing machine for shorter times.

output: A study looked at how well the Mini-Cog test works to find signs of memory problems. They checked this in three groups of people, with a total of 1620 people in all. The Mini-Cog was very good at finding memory problems when used in these groups, with sensitivities (how often it correctly finds problems) of 0.99, 0.76, and 0.99. However, it wasn't always as good at telling who doesn’t have memory problems (specificity), with values of 0.93, 0.89, and 0.83. The studies had some differences that made it hard to combine their results. All the studies had some problems that might have affected the results. Because there aren’t many studies like this and they had some issues, we can’t give clear advice about using the Mini-Cog to check for memory problems in regular communities. More studies need to be done to see if the Mini-Cog is useful and accurate in places where lots of people live.

output: In a review of fourteen studies, the length of time people took molindone varied from just ten days up to over three months. The studies didn't show enough information to decide if molindone works better than a sugar pill for treating mental health problems. When compared to other medicines used to treat these problems, molindone didn't seem to work any differently. However, molindone caused people to gain more weight than the other medicines did. The studies weren't very big or well-designed, so we can't be completely sure about these findings. Molindone might help with mental health problems, but it doesn't seem to work differently from other medicines. It causes people to lose less weight, but it makes them gain more weight. Overall, the evidence isn't strong because the studies were small and didn't look at many different things. At the moment, there's no clear sign that molindone has a special kind of effect that's different from other medicines.

output: This study looked at 660 people who had a type of stroke called an acute ischaemic stroke. Eight different studies were reviewed, but most of them weren't very good. The studies followed the people for less than a month. Two of the studies showed that fewer people died or needed help with daily activities in the group that got something called sanchi compared to the group that didn't get it. Another study said people in the sanchi group did better on tests measuring their ability to move around. When all the studies together were looked at, it seemed like sanchi might help people recover from their stroke more. But there weren't many people in the studies, and the studies weren't perfect, so we can't be totally sure if sanchi really helps. We need more studies to know for sure if sanchi is good for people with this kind of stroke.

output: A study looked at 519 people who had depression. They found three studies that were done well and three that weren't as well done. These studies all tried different ways to help people with depression, but they used different ways to measure if the treatments worked. Some of these studies showed that family therapy might help people feel less depressed and have better relationships with their families. But because the studies were different and not all agreed, we can't say for sure that family therapy works better than other treatments. We need more studies to figure out if family therapy really helps people with depression. For now, doctors usually recommend other types of talk therapy that have been shown to work well. More research is needed to see exactly how family therapy compares to other treatments.

output: This study looked at three groups of people who have schizophrenia. They took part in two out of seven tests because some of the tests didn't work well. The test they did measure showed that people taking chlorpromazine or metiapine didn't seem to get better faster. Also, both groups had about the same number of people getting something called "parkinsonism" after eight weeks. But there wasn't enough good information to know if one medicine worked better than the other for things like feeling better mentally, going back to the hospital, or how much it costs to take care of them. Chlorpromazine has been used for a long time to help people with schizophrenia, but this study couldn't find strong proof that metiapine works differently. It seems that figuring out which medicine might work better isn't very important right now, so researchers may not do more studies comparing these two medicines.

More studies are needed, especially for children and in places where it might be harder to get medicines.

output:
This study looked at nine different studies to see if talking to doctors over the phone instead of going to their office helps people feel better. Five of these studies used something called a randomized controlled trial (RCT), which means they tried to make sure everyone was treated fairly. One study used a different kind of test, and three used something called an interrupted time series (ITS) study. 

Six of the studies compared talking to a doctor over the phone to just getting normal care. Four of those studies said fewer people went to the doctor’s office, but two said more people came back later. Three studies looked at whether talking to a nurse or other healthcare worker over the phone helped. Two of those studies compared nurses to doctors, and one compared health assistants to doctors or nurses.

Seven out of the nine studies looked at whether people went to the hospital’s emergency room less often when they talked to a doctor over the phone. Most of the time, this happened. But one study found that when nurses talked to people over the phone, more people went to the emergency room.

Two studies also looked at whether anyone died, and neither group had more deaths than the other.

Overall, it seems like talking to a doctor over the phone might help people go to the doctor’s office less often. But we still need more research to be sure, especially about how it affects things like using the hospital, costs, and how people feel about it.

output: In a study looking at 38 different groups of kids, researchers found that when children, their parents, or both learned about asthma, they went to the emergency room less often and stayed in the hospital less than those who didn't learn. They also had fewer doctor visits. This happened whether the learning was done for children only, their parents only, or both. The results showed this worked better than not learning. But the study couldn’t tell if learning helped kids feel better over a longer time or if it helped them breathe better. Also, the study didn’t have enough information to know which kind of learning program works best or how long it should last. So while learning about asthma seems to help kids avoid going to the emergency room, more research is needed to fully understand its effects.

output: This research looked at 33 studies with 5110 patients to see if a treatment called TFU works. Most of these studies weren't very good at showing clear results. TFU was used in lots of different people, but it was done in many different ways. Different studies looked at different things, so it's hard to compare them all. Because the studies weren't always done well, we can't be sure about what TFU does. Some studies said it helped, but others didn't. We don't know if TFU really helps or not because the studies were mixed up and not all done the same way. While TFU didn't seem to cause any bad side effects, the studies didn't show that it worked better than other treatments. So, we can't say for sure that TFU is a helpful treatment. We need more good studies to figure this out.

output: This review looked at ten studies with 33,179 people to see if taking vitamin A helps prevent a common illness called acute lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI). Eight studies didn't find vitamin A helped prevent these infections. One study found it did make more people get sick. Two other studies said vitamin A made more people have coughs and fevers. Three studies found no difference. Two studies found vitamin A helped prevent these infections in kids who weren't eating well, but it made more kids sick in healthy kids. This is surprising because we thought vitamin A would help everyone. So, we shouldn't give vitamin A to all children to prevent these infections. It seems to work better in kids who aren't eating well, but even then, it doesn't always help. Lower doses of vitamin A might work just as well with fewer side effects.

This study looked at three small tests done on 110 healthy children. These kids were brothers or sisters of people who got chicken pox. The tests weren't all the same - some used different vaccines, some followed the children for shorter times, and some measured different things. Because the tests were different and not very good, we can't put their results together easily.

Two of the three tests showed that the vaccine didn't work very well. About 23% of kids who got the vaccine got chicken pox, but only 78% of those who didn't get the vaccine got it. Most of the kids who got chicken pox from the vaccine had only a few spots, which wasn't very serious.

In the tests, most kids got medicine called PEP soon after they might have gotten chicken pox. But not enough kids got the vaccine later to know if that works. None of the tests told us about any bad side effects from the vaccine.

The tests suggest that giving the chicken pox vaccine to kids within three days after they're around someone with chicken pox helps stop them from getting sick. But we don't know if it works for older kids or grown-ups. We also don't know much about whether the vaccine is safe for these groups.

output: A study looked at 159 papers to find out if a medicine called beclomethasone could help kids with asthma grow normally. They found 3 studies that matched their rules. In these studies, kids who took beclomethasone for 7 to 12 months grew about 1.54 cm less than those who didn't take the medicine. This happened in all 3 studies. When they added up all the information, they found that kids taking beclomethasone grew about 1.54 cm less each year. But they don't know if this difference in growth will last forever. It might just mean that kids catch up to their normal growth once they stop taking the medicine. The studies only lasted for a few months, so we're not sure if the growth difference stays or goes away. We also don't know if other medicines that work on asthma but aren't as strong affect growth differently. If your doctor thinks you need to take beclomethasone to keep your asthma under control, they should use the smallest amount that works well for you and watch your growth closely.

A few studies looked at ways to help reduce the use of physical restraints for older people living in nursing homes. These studies tried different methods like giving extra help to nurses or teaching them better ways to care for residents. Some studies looked at people living in nursing homes, while others looked at those living in group homes. But none of the studies were done in communities outside of these places.

The studies had some problems, so we can't be sure about their results. One study found that using physical restraints went down a little bit in the group that got extra help. But the other three studies found that using restraints went up more in the groups that got extra help. Another study found that using restraints didn't change much in the group that got extra help, but it actually went up in the group that didn't get extra help.

Overall, there isn't enough good evidence to show that teaching nurses new ways to care for residents helps prevent or reduce the use of physical restraints for older people in long-term care. More research is needed to find out what really works.

The study found that the babies who got the salbutamol medicine had less trouble breathing than those in the other two groups. However, the cool mist didn't help them breathe better. So, doctors still don’t have enough proof to decide whether to use cool mist or the salbutamol medicine for treating bronchiolitis in very young children.

They found that starting food earlier didn't seem to make a big difference in how many people died. But it did seem to help a little bit in making fewer people disabled. 

Seven other trials compared two types of feeding: one where food is given through a vein directly into the body (parenteral), and another where food is given through the mouth and goes down the stomach (enteral). Again, starting food earlier didn't seem to make a big difference in how many people died. But it did seem to help a little bit in making fewer people disabled.

One trial compared giving food through the stomach versus the small intestine. In this case, there were no deaths, so we couldn't tell if starting food earlier made a difference.

Overall, the studies suggest that starting to feed people earlier might help them survive and stay healthier. But more studies are needed to know for sure. These studies should look at both how well people do and whether they live longer.

The study also checked if these medicines might cause the germs to become stronger over time, but they didn’t find any evidence that this happened.

So, using medicine both inside and on the skin seems to be the best way to help sick adults in the hospital stay healthier and have a better chance of surviving their illness. Using medicine just on the skin helps with infections, but it doesn’t seem to improve survival chances.

This study looked at five groups of people who had some kind of surgery or procedure that caused them pain after it was done. Each group got a different medicine to help with their pain. Some people got a medicine called fenoprofen, which comes in different strengths - like very weak, weak, medium, strong, and super strong. Other people got a medicine called zomepirac, another medicine called morphine, and some got a sugar pill that doesn't have any medicine in it.

The study found that when people took the strongest form of fenoprofen (200 mg), they were more likely to feel much better within 4 to 6 hours than those who took the sugar pill. This means that out of every 2.3 people who took the strong medicine, only 1 person needed extra medicine to feel better. But the study didn't have enough information to know if weaker forms of fenoprofen would work as well, or if other medicines worked better.

The study also found that people who took the strongest form of fenoprofen didn't have more bad side effects than those who took the sugar pill. No one in the study had serious problems from taking the medicine.

So, based on this small amount of information, it seems that the strongest form of fenoprofen can help people feel much better from pain after surgery or procedures. But we don't know if weaker forms of the medicine work as well, or if other medicines might be better.

In a study looking at different types of needles used by doctors during surgeries, researchers found that using blunt needles instead of sharp ones helped reduce something called "glove perforations." A glove perforation happens when a needle goes through the glove a doctor wears while operating. 

The study looked at several types of surgeries, like closing up tummy wounds, making baby deliveries, fixing holes in women's vaginas, and replacing hips. On average, doctors who used sharp needles had one hole in their gloves after about three operations. But those who used blunt needles had fewer holes in their gloves—about one hole in every six operations.

Blunt needles also seemed to lower the chance of doctors getting hurt by needles. They reported fewer times where they got pricked by a needle. However, using blunt needles was a bit harder for the doctors to do.

Overall, there's strong proof (high quality) that blunt needles help keep doctors and their helpers safer from getting blood or body fluids on their hands. This finding seems very likely to stay true even if more research is done.

In this review, we looked at some studies about treating a condition called BL. We found 13 studies that had enough information to look at, but only 10 of them gave us good details to understand clearly. Many of these studies didn't tell us everything we needed to know about how they were done, which made it hard to judge if they were done well.

Eight studies tried to get people better quickly, and the chances of living longer didn’t seem different between the groups. But we weren’t sure because the studies weren’t big enough or done in a way that lets us be very confident.

Five studies tried to keep people healthy after they got better quickly. In two out of three studies, people who had less intense treatments lived just as long, but we’re not sure if this is true for everyone.

The newer studies seem to prefer less intense treatments. But we don’t have strong proof that one type of treatment is better than another. The studies were small and might have some mistakes in them.

Overall, while there’s a trend towards using less intense treatments, we can’t say for sure which ones work best. More research is needed to find out.

output: This research looked at 18 studies with 2521 people to see if some special medicines called Chinese herbal remedies could help prevent or treat the flu. But most of these studies weren't very good at showing how well the treatments worked. Three studies said that a medicine called Ganmao capsules might work better than another medicine called amantadine for making flu symptoms go away faster. Another study found that a medicine called E Shu You didn't seem to work any better than another medicine called ribavirin. Some people had side effects from taking the medicines, but it wasn't clear how common they were. Many of the herbal medicines seemed to work about the same as the regular medicines used to fight the flu. Not many of them were shown to work better. None of the studies had serious problems with the medicines. But because the studies weren't perfect, we don't know for sure if these herbal medicines really work. We need more studies with lots of people and clearer information to learn more.

In a study looking at different treatments for a condition called extracranial internal carotid artery dissection, we didn't find any big studies where people were randomly picked to get one treatment or another. We looked at 36 smaller studies that compared two types of medicines: ones that help stop blood clots (antiplatelets) and ones that prevent blood clots from getting bigger (anticoagulants).

When we compared how well these medicines worked, we found that they didn’t seem to make much difference in whether someone died or had a stroke. The studies showed that people might be a little less likely to have a stroke if they took anticoagulants, but this wasn’t very clear because the numbers weren’t very large. 

There were some small differences seen, but they weren’t strong enough to be sure. Anticoagulant medicines caused more bleeding inside the head (symptomatic intracranial haemorrhages) and outside the head (major extracranial haemorrhages), but again, the numbers were too small to be confident about this.

Because there were no big studies comparing these medicines to each other or to nothing at all, we don’t have enough information to say which medicine should always be used first. The studies also didn’t clearly show that one type of medicine was better than the other. So, right now, there’s not enough proof to recommend one type of medicine over the other for treating this condition.

This study looked at how doctors give treatments called chemotherapy and radiation to help prevent cancer coming back or spreading after it has been treated locally. They studied three groups of women who had these treatments. They found that giving both treatments together didn't make a big difference in how long the women lived or how likely they were to get their cancer back or spread it to other parts of the body. 

However, when doctors gave radiation first and then chemotherapy, more women got something called anaemia, which means they felt tired and weak. Also, more women got a condition where tiny blood vessels become bigger and more visible on the skin. And some women's skin became darker. 

Women themselves didn't notice that their skin looked worse after getting both treatments together, but doctors did. Giving radiation first also made it slightly more likely that women would get a type of infection called neutropenic sepsis, which is when bacteria enters the bloodstream and causes a serious illness. But other problems like hair loss or mouth sores didn't happen more often.

Overall, the study suggests that whether you give the radiation first or the chemotherapy first doesn't seem to make a big difference in how well the treatments work to stop the cancer from coming back or spreading. This is based on three studies that were done very carefully.

A study looked at giving a medicine called vancomycin to some very small babies who were born early to see if it would help prevent a sickness called sepsis. Sepsis is when the body gets sick from germs. The study found that giving vancomycin did reduce the number of babies getting this sickness. However, it didn't seem to make a difference in how long the babies stayed in the hospital or if they had any bad side effects from the medicine. Also, the study couldn't tell if the medicine might cause more germs to become resistant to it. 

While giving vancomycin might help keep babies healthy, the study wasn't able to show that it definitely does. The study also couldn't prove that giving the medicine doesn't increase the chance of developing germs that are resistant to it. Because of this, the study couldn't say for sure if the medicine has many good benefits for the babies. 

So, based on this information, doctors don't think it's necessary to give vancomycin to all very small babies as a regular way to prevent sepsis. More research is needed before we know if it's helpful.

This study looked at three small groups of people with type 2 diabetes who took sweet potatoes or a sugar-free pill. The study lasted from 6 weeks to 5 months. Two out of the three groups had the same trial leader. The researchers weren't sure if they did a good job making sure their study was fair. 

All three groups took either sweet potatoes or a sugar-free pill. At the end of the study, the group that ate sweet potatoes had slightly lower numbers for something called HbA1c, which is a measure of blood sugar levels over time. This number went down by about 0.3%. But it's not clear if this really means anything because the study wasn't perfect.

The study didn't look at whether eating sweet potatoes made people feel better or if it helped them live longer. It also didn't check if sweet potatoes cost less than other things people might take for diabetes.

While the study showed some promise, there isn't enough information yet to know if sweet potatoes really help people with diabetes. To learn more, doctors will need to do more studies. These could be bigger groups of people, or they could compare different types of sweet potatoes. They'll also need to make sure all the sweet potatoes taste the same and work the same way in the body.

output: A study looked at two ways to fix a problem called urethral stricture in grown men who had trouble urinating. In one study, they compared two surgeries: one where they widened the urethra using a special tool (urethrotomy) and another where they repaired the damaged part of the urethra (urethroplasty). They followed 210 men for three years. Neither surgery worked better; both caused some men to need more surgeries later on. Another study looked at men who got injured in their pelvis and had a stricture after the injury. In the first six months, more men needed another surgery if they had urethrotomy instead of urethroplasty. But after two years, fewer men needed more surgeries overall if they had urethroplasty. The studies didn't have enough information to know which surgery works better. More studies are needed to help doctors decide which surgery might be best for fixing this problem.

This study looked at different ways to do a quick test called a blood sample on babies. They compared two methods: using a needle to take blood (called venepuncture) and pricking the baby's heel (called heel lance). Six studies with a total of 478 babies were reviewed. 

The studies found that babies had less pain when their blood was taken using a needle instead of pricking their heel. This was true even when the babies got a special tasteless liquid before the blood test. 

When the babies got this tasteless liquid, they still had less pain when their blood was taken using a needle. But if the babies also got the tasteless liquid, they had even less pain when their blood was taken using a needle. 

The studies also found that fewer babies needed to have their skin pricked again if their blood was taken using a needle. For every three babies, one would need to have their skin pricked less often if their blood was taken using a needle.

A skilled person doing the blood test seemed to be the best way to do it. Adding the tasteless liquid helped make the blood test less painful. However, more studies are needed to confirm these findings, especially in places where many people do the blood tests.

In a study looking at removing stents early versus later after kidney transplants, five groups of people were studied. Most of these groups had low or unclear chances of being biased, meaning they followed the right methods. They looked at whether removing the stents sooner or later affected two things: how often people got a bladder infection (UTI) and how often they got something called MUC.

The study found that removing the stents sooner didn't seem to lower the chance of getting MUC. But it did seem to lower the chance of getting a bladder infection. This happened more often when a special type of stent called a BI stent was used. Using another type of stent called an externalized PU stent didn't help prevent bladder infections.

However, the study wasn't very sure about whether removing the stents sooner might make it more likely for people to get MUC. Also, the study didn't have enough information to tell us about how much money it costs or how it affects people's quality of life.

So, it seems that removing the stents sooner might help prevent bladder infections, especially with the BI stent. But we're not very sure about whether it increases the chance of MUC. And we don't know much about the costs or quality of life.

Two studies looked at night splints for a condition called Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1A. They found that wearing a night splint didn't make a difference compared to not wearing one. Another study tested a medicine called prednisone for boys with a muscle disease called Duchenne muscular dystrophy. The study found that taking the medicine helped them move their feet better, but it didn’t help their ankles bend more. A third study looked at surgery to fix foot problems in boys with Duchenne muscular dystrophy. The surgery helped their ankles bend more at first, but after a while, their ankles started to get tight again. None of these treatments seemed to work well for making ankles bend more in either condition. More research is needed to find better ways to help with these foot problems.

output: This study looked at eight studies with about 10,000 people. They tried different medicines called statins to see if they could help prevent another stroke or heart problem. The medicine called statin didn't seem to stop strokes from happening more often, but it did seem to help a little bit in people who already had had a stroke or something called a TIA before. Statins also seemed to help a bit in stopping other problems like heart attacks. But they didn’t find strong proof that statins helped prevent strokes from coming back. Some studies showed that statins might help reduce serious problems like heart attacks, especially in people who have had a stroke or TIA in the past. It’s not clear if statins should be given right away after a stroke or later. However, since statins seem to help people who already have heart disease, doctors think that people who have had a stroke or TIA, even if they haven’t had heart disease before, should probably take statins.

The studies that looked at CBT weren't very long, so we don't know if it works as well over a longer period. Overall, CBT seems to be helpful for short-term treatment of anxiety, but we need more research to decide if it's the best choice for everyone.

This research looked at how doctors and scientists write their papers. They found that when editors do extra work to make sure papers are clear and correct, it helps. But not all the studies agreed on this. Some said better editing made papers easier to read and follow, while others said it didn't always help. Editing also seems to catch more mistakes in parts of papers called abstracts and references. 

Some studies showed that giving authors instructions helped them be more careful about things like getting permission to use someone else's work. But other studies didn't find this worked. Structuring papers to make them clearer usually makes them longer. 

The studies also found that many papers don't cite or quote correctly. This happens in about 38 out of every 100 citations and 20 out of every 100 quotes. Not many studies have looked closely at whether making papers better through editing really works.

So, while there isn't a lot of strong proof, it seems that the extra work editors do can make papers clearer and less likely to have mistakes. But we need more studies to know for sure if this is true.

In this review, we looked at some studies about how doctors treat people who have trouble breathing really badly. We didn't find any new studies to add to our list. There were six studies in total, each with 1297 patients. In five of these studies, the way doctors treated the patients seemed very fair and honest. In one study, we weren't sure if it was fair or not.

The studies showed that when doctors use a special kind of breathing treatment called "lung-protective ventilation," patients had a slightly lower chance of dying within 28 days. They also had a lower chance of dying while they were in the hospital. But we're not sure if this treatment helps patients live longer after they leave the hospital. 

There wasn't enough information to know if this treatment helps patients feel better overall or if it has other long-term effects. Some of the studies were different because they followed patients for different amounts of time or used a higher pressure when treating patients without the special treatment. This made it hard to compare all the studies and figure out if the treatment works.

So, we know that using lower amounts of air to breathe into the lungs seems to help patients survive for a short time, but we don't know yet if it helps them live longer. Because of the differences between the studies, we can't be completely sure if this treatment works or not.

This research looked at two studies that tested whether giving thyroid medicine to very small babies who were having trouble breathing helped them get better. The studies gave different amounts of thyroid medicine to some of the babies and didn't give it to others. But there were some problems with how these studies were done, like not making sure which babies got which treatment fairly, and not knowing if the people measuring the babies' health knew which group they were in.

Both studies did not find that giving thyroid medicine made the babies healthier or less likely to die. When scientists combined the results of both studies, they still did not see any clear benefit from the medicine. They also did not find that the medicine helped the babies need less help breathing, stay on breathing machines for shorter times, have less lung problems, or have fewer other health issues. The studies did not look at how well the babies did later when they grew up.

Overall, there is no strong evidence from these studies that giving thyroid medicine helps very small babies who are having trouble breathing.

However, more people in these groups had side effects like kidney or blood problems, which made them stop taking the medicine more often. Overall, D-penicillamine seems to help with the symptoms of rheumatoid arthritis, but it might cause more health issues than other medicines used to treat this condition. We're not sure if it helps with how well people can move around or how much damage the arthritis causes to their joints over time.

Overall, this suggests that the vaccine might help make malaria less serious, but it only works against certain types of malaria. More research is needed to fully understand how well it works.

This study looked at 11 different studies involving 2246 people with a heart condition called atrial fibrillation (AF). These studies tested different ways to help these people take their medicine regularly, like using special tools to check if they're taking their medicine correctly, or giving them extra information about their condition. 

The studies didn't find strong proof that helping people track their medicine (self-monitoring) made it easier for them to keep taking their medicine regularly. But they did find that giving people extra information (education) seemed to make them less worried about their health (lowered anxiety) and less sad (depression), compared to just getting regular care. 

Decision-making tools (decision aids) didn't seem to help people make better decisions about their medicine. 

Overall, the researchers couldn't be sure about whether these extra steps helped people take their medicine more regularly. They think we need more studies to figure out if these methods work and why some might help while others don't. It's also important to look into how these changes might affect people's feelings over time because having a long-term health condition can be tough on a person's mental health.

output: This study looked at treatments for a stuffy nose called acute sinusitis. It checked if a medicine called INCS helped more than a sugar pill. They found four studies with 1943 people who had this stuffy nose. The studies were done carefully, like a game where doctors didn't know who got which treatment. But they also need to think about whether the medicine will really help each person before deciding to give it.

output: A group of researchers looked through many medical papers to find information about how doctors talk to women who have been diagnosed with breast cancer. They found 2847 papers in total, but after checking, they only had 27 papers to look at closely. Six of those papers were actually the same study done by different people over several years. After removing duplicates, they had 23 papers left to consider. But none of these papers had the kind of study called a "randomized trial" that doctors use to see if a new way of talking really works better than the old way. This means they couldn't figure out if a certain way of telling someone they have breast cancer helps or hurts. The researchers think it might be hard to do a fair test because it's not right to make someone wait to hear their diagnosis just so they can be part of a study. They suggest looking at how doctors talk to women during their first visit, when they're deciding on treatment, instead. This might give them better information about what works best.

In a recent study from 2009 to 2010, researchers looked at 53 different studies to see if helping families could make a difference for people with schizophrenia. They found that family support might help prevent people from having more bad times when they're sick (we call this a "relapse"). This happened in 2981 cases where families got extra help. It's like if you had a friend who helped you stay healthy; they might help your friend stay well too.

Family support might also keep people from needing to go to the hospital more often (481 cases) and might make them take their medicine better (695 cases). But it didn't seem to change whether families left the place where they get help.

Family support seemed to help families work better together and made things less stressful for everyone. The study showed that family support might be helpful, but the researchers aren't completely sure because some of the studies weren't done very well. If the studies were done better, we would be even more confident about these findings. So, family support might be good for people with schizophrenia, but we need more information to be really sure.

However, because only two experiments were done, we need more information to be sure about these findings. More research would help us know if molar bands really are better.

output: In a study looking at six different groups of people, researchers tried to see if sending emails instead of regular letters helped more with getting important check-ups and if it made it easier for people to understand their health. They looked at two groups: one where people got emails instead of regular mail, and another where people got emails instead of just what they usually get. For checking up on health, like getting tests done, there wasn't much difference between using emails or regular mail. Also, people didn't seem to find it harder or easier to understand things when they got emails. But the study couldn't tell us if emails made people feel better overall. There wasn't enough good information to know if emails help with preventing diseases or promoting good health. The study also didn't look at how doctors used emails or if there were any bad side effects. To learn more, we need better studies that use the newest ways of sending emails and consider all the complexities involved.

In a study looking at whether a certain medicine called statins helps people with a condition called Alzheimer’s disease, researchers looked at four groups of people. These people all had Alzheimer’s disease and were taking another medicine to help them. The study compared how well these people did on tests measuring their memory and thinking skills before and after starting the statin medicine. They also checked if the statin caused any side effects.

The results showed that the statin medicine didn’t seem to help people do better on these memory and thinking tests. In fact, it might even make things a little worse, but this wasn’t very clear because the numbers weren’t strong enough to be sure. The study also checked if the statin caused more side effects than a sugar pill, but again, the results weren’t strong enough to tell.

None of the studies found any evidence that statins helped with other parts of Alzheimer’s disease like behavior or daily activities. The researchers thought the studies were done fairly and the results were reliable.

However, the studies didn’t look at whether statins could help people with another condition called Vascular Dementia. Based on the information from these studies, which included some big ones, it seems that statins don’t help with the main measures used to see if someone with Alzheimer’s is getting better.

output: A study looked at two ways doctors close up the skin after a cesarean birth: using special metal clips called staples or using stitches that the body can absorb later. The study found that using staples did not cause more infections around the cut than using the absorbable stitches. But, the staples sometimes caused the skin to pull apart, which needed to be fixed again. This happened more often with staples than with the other type of stitch. The study wasn't sure if this was because of the type of cut made or just because the staples were taken out too soon. Both types of closing worked well overall, but staples might need to be taken out sooner than the stitches. So, doctors still don't know which way is best to close the skin after a cesarean.

This study looked at 11 studies with a total of 38,742 people. Eight studies compared Blood Pressure Lowering Drugs (BPLDs) to nothing or a placebo, and three studies compared different levels of lowering blood pressure. The studies had mixed quality, but overall, the results suggest that BPLDs might help reduce the chance of having another stroke. For example, they found that people who took BPLDs were about 19% less likely to have another stroke compared to those who didn't take them. This finding comes from 8 studies with 35,110 people, which is considered moderate-quality evidence. They also found that people taking BPLDs were about 10% less likely to have other serious health problems related to their blood pressure. 

The researchers noticed that people who used a type of medicine called ACE inhibitors or a diuretic were especially likely to benefit from BPLDs. This happened in 7 out of 10 cases when looking at this group. However, the study couldn't say for sure if lower blood pressure is better than higher blood pressure after someone has a stroke or a mini-stroke. The best way to lower blood pressure after these events seems to involve using ACE inhibitors or diuretics. More research is needed to find out the best blood pressure level to aim for after a stroke or mini-stroke.

output: This study looked at 56 different studies involving 4068 people to see if exercise helps with feeling tired after having cancer. Most of these people had breast cancer. The researchers compared people who did exercise to those who didn't and found that the people who exercised felt less tired overall. This happened whether they started exercising before or after their treatment for cancer. They saw that aerobic exercises, which are activities like walking or running, helped reduce tiredness. But other types of exercise, like lifting weights, didn't seem to help as much. The study shows that aerobic exercise can be helpful for people with cancer who feel tired, especially those with solid tumors like those in the breast or prostate. However, more research is needed to figure out the best kind, how hard to work out, and when to start exercising to get the most benefit.

This study looked at two groups of 447 women who needed special medicine to prevent something called RhD alloimmunization. Both groups got the same amount of medicine during their pregnancy, around 1500 IU (300 micrograms) of Rhophylac, during the 28th week. Neither group had any problems with RhD alloimmunization because it didn't happen often enough to tell if one way of giving the medicine worked better than the other.

In one group, the medicine was given through a needle in the skin (IM), and in the other group, it was given into a vein (IV). After seven days, the medicine levels were a little different between the two ways, but by two to three weeks later, they were about the same. Also, none of the women in the study developed antibodies against the RhD antigen.

The study found that giving the medicine through a vein or under the skin works equally well. But since there weren't many women in the study and the numbers were small, we don't have enough information to know for sure if one way is better than the other. The doctors still need to decide based on what medicines are available, how much medicine needs to be given, and what the patients prefer.

This study looked at 1896 patients who were part of ten different studies comparing a special kind of hospital unit called a Non-Intensive Care Unit (NLU) to regular hospital units. The studies didn't show that the NLU made people die more often while they were in the hospital. But when the studies were of good quality, it seemed like the NLU might make people die a little bit less often after they left the hospital.

The NLU helped people go home sooner than usual, which was good. It also helped people get better faster before leaving the hospital. However, people stayed in the NLU a bit longer than usual, which could have been because they were getting better more slowly.

The NLU also helped people go back to the hospital less quickly after they left. This was a positive thing.

In some studies, people who went to the NLU had lower costs for their hospital stay. In other studies, people had higher costs. So it's not clear if the NLU saves money or costs more.

Overall, the NLU seems to help people get better and go home sooner, but it might take them a bit longer to recover. We need more research to know for sure if the NLU is really better for patients.

output: A study looked at four different treatments for people with a type of sickle cell disease called painful crises. Two of these treatments, Niprisan and Ciklavit, were tested in small groups of people. One treatment called Niprisan seemed to help reduce the number of very painful sickle cell crises over six months. It didn't seem to make the sickness worse or change how much the person's blood cells were broken down. No serious side effects were seen. Another treatment, Ciklavit, might also help with pain, but it could slightly lower the amount of healthy blood cells. Both treatments seemed safe, but more studies are needed to know if they really work well. Right now, we think these plant-based medicines might help with pain, but we need more tests to confirm this. We also need more studies to see if they're safe for everyone who has sickle cell disease.

The medicines methylprednisolone, trimetazidine, and dextrose seemed to help keep the liver from getting hurt during the operation. But the study only had a few small groups of people, which means we can't be totally sure about these findings. 

Because of these issues, we can't say for certain that these medicines work. We need more studies with bigger groups of people to be really confident. Until then, doctors shouldn't start using these medicines on patients. They should wait for better studies to show if these medicines truly help.

These people were split into two groups: one group took their bandages off after 12 hours and could take a bath normally right away, while the other group kept their bandages on for at least 48 hours before taking a bath. The study wanted to see if letting people bathe sooner after their skin cuts healed would make them less likely to get infections at the cut site. But the study didn't find a clear difference between the two groups. About 8.5% of people in each group got infections. Because the numbers were close and the study wasn't perfect, we can't say for sure whether letting people bathe sooner helps or hurts their chances of getting infections. More studies are needed to figure this out.

This study looked at 17 different studies involving 22 comparisons of treatments for women with advanced breast cancer. In 20 of these studies, they checked if the treatment helped the cancer shrink over time. In 14 of the studies, they also tracked how long it took for the cancer to get worse. They followed about 2100 women who were part of the studies. 

The studies didn't find a big difference in how long the women lived or how long it took for their cancer to get worse. But they did find that adding a new medicine to the usual treatment made the cancer shrink a little bit more often. This happened in 14 out of 22 times the new medicine was added. However, when the new medicine was added, the women had more side effects like hair loss, feeling sick, and having low white blood cells.

So, while adding a new medicine might help the cancer shrink a bit more, it doesn't seem to make the cancer last longer or get worse slower. And because there were more side effects, doctors need to think carefully before deciding to use this new medicine.

output: A review looked at fifteen studies involving 1043 people who have Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (CFS). These studies compared a type of therapy called Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) with regular care that doesn't focus specifically on CFS. The results showed that CBT helped reduce feelings of tiredness more than regular care did. About 40 out of every 100 people who got CBT felt much better after the treatment ended, while about 26 out of every 100 who got regular care felt better. However, when looking at how well CBT worked after some time had passed, the results weren't always clear. Only a few studies compared CBT to other types of therapy, and even fewer compared CBT to other treatments. CBT seems to help reduce tiredness more than other types of therapy. But we don't know if it works better than other treatments combined. We need more studies to learn more about the best ways to treat CFS.

output: This research looked at two types of dialysis treatments: APD (Automated Peritoneal Dialysis) and CAPD (Continuous Ambulatory Peritoneal Dialysis). They studied 139 people who used these treatments. The study found that APD didn't seem to help people live longer or have fewer problems like infections or leaks in their tubes. It also didn’t make it easier for people to go back to work or have more free time. However, some studies showed that people using APD might have fewer times when they get sick and spend more time doing things they enjoy. The research suggests that APD might be better for younger people who are still working or studying, but more studies are needed to confirm this. We need bigger studies to compare both treatments and see which one works better overall, including how well they keep people’s kidneys healthy.

output: In a study looking at different ways to help heal foot sores in people with diabetes, researchers looked at four types of casts. They found that some people had fewer sores heal faster when they used casts that couldn't be taken off easily. Five out of seven studies showed that these hard-to-remove casts helped more sores heal compared to casts that could be taken on and off. Two studies also found that using these hard-to-remove casts along with a special procedure called Achilles tendon lengthening helped even more sores heal. The evidence suggests that hard-to-remove casts are better at helping sores heal than regular casts or just putting dressings on them. However, there wasn't strong enough proof to say that other things like special felt materials or surgery to remove sores worked better. So, for now, doctors might recommend using hard-to-remove casts to help heal foot sores in people with diabetes.

output: This research looked at some studies done in different places like Australia, Singapore, and the USA to see if putting red-light cameras at traffic lights helps make roads safer. They found that out of all the studies, only one that tried really hard to account for things like people driving more carefully after seeing the cameras (called adjusting for regression to the mean) showed that there were fewer accidents overall. Other studies that didn't try as hard to do this also saw fewer accidents, but it wasn't always clear if the cameras were really the reason. Some studies found that fewer people ran red lights too. But most of these studies didn't try very hard to rule out other reasons why accidents might go down. So while red-light cameras seem to help keep people safer, we need more studies to be sure. It's important to have bigger and better studies to get a clearer picture.

output: This study looked at four groups of women with a condition called PCOS. Each group got medicine called statins for 6 or 12 weeks. The medicine was either simvastatin or atorvastatin. The study found that statins did not help make periods more regular, help eggs come out by themselves, make hair less noticeable, or clear up spots. But statins did help lower a hormone called testosterone. They also helped lower bad cholesterol, but didn't change good cholesterol or another measure of heart health. Statins didn't affect how much a person weighs or other things like blood sugar. No one in the study had serious problems from taking the medicine. While statins seem to help with some parts of PCOS, they don't seem to fix all the problems like making periods regular or clearing up skin. More studies with bigger groups of people would be needed to know if statins really work better than other treatments.

output: A study looked at a medicine called opioids (a special kind of painkiller) compared to a sugar pill to see if they help with a condition called Restless Legs Syndrome (RLS). After 12 weeks, people who took the medicine had fewer RLS symptoms and felt better overall. They also slept better and felt less sleepy during the day. However, more people taking the medicine had some side effects like feeling sick in their tummy, being very tired, and headaches. While this study suggests the medicine might work well, it's just one study, so we don't know for sure if it's safe for everyone. The results are based on a small number of people who didn't finish the study, which makes the information a bit uncertain.

It also seemed like these cuts might hurt less. But the study wasn't perfect, and some of the findings might not apply to everyone. Other parts of the recovery, like when you feel pain and if your body has problems, didn’t show much difference. The cuts might look nicer too. So, even though it looks good, doctors still decide based on their own experience which cut to use.

More studies are needed to see if these special medicines really help with chemotherapy side effects and if they're safe to use.

output: In a study looking at two ways to find a tooth called a maxillary canine that's stuck behind another tooth, researchers looked at 146 people who had the procedure done. Two out of the three studies they looked at might not have been completely fair in their results. They found that both methods seemed to work about the same way. But there wasn't enough good information to know if one method was better than the other for things like how the tooth looks after the surgery, how much pain someone feels, or how well their gums heal. There were some small problems with the surgeries, like one tooth getting a little infection or feeling sore when the gold chain was put in place. Because the studies weren't perfect, the researchers think the results aren't very strong. But they're hopeful that new studies now underway might help make the results clearer and stronger.

output: A review looked at different studies about how to talk to people who might get sick with a rare brain disease called CJD or vCJD. But no studies exactly matched the way the review was looking for. Instead, the researchers looked at many other studies that talked about how well people understood information about their risk of getting these diseases. They found that it's important to have a long-term plan for talking to people, making sure they understand and feel supported. They also found that if people don't understand or are scared, it can make things worse, like making it harder for them to get help when they need it. However, there isn't enough strong proof to know exactly what works best for talking to people about their risk of these diseases. So, while this information can help make decisions about how to communicate better, more studies would be needed to be really sure.

- Parents were happier with the care.

This study looked at 390,769 people to see if eating certain plant compounds called flavonoids might help prevent colon cancer. Eight different studies were reviewed. Some of these studies followed people over time to see what happened to them, while others compared people who got colon cancer to those who didn’t. 

The studies that followed people over time found mixed results. They couldn't be sure if eating more flavonoids helped or hurt colon cancer. Two other types of studies also showed mixed results. 

Some specific flavonoids like isoflavones, flavonols, flavones, and flavanones did not seem to have much effect on preventing colon cancer. But some other flavonoids like flavan-3-ols, which include epicatechin, seemed to lower the risk of colon cancer. Another type of flavonoid called procyanidins and phytoestrogens also seemed to lower the risk of colon cancer. However, there wasn't enough evidence to show that eating more anthocyanins would help prevent colon cancer.

Overall, the evidence isn't strong enough to say whether eating flavonoids helps prevent colon cancer. It's hard to know exactly how much flavonoids people eat because they're found in many foods. More research is needed to understand better how flavonoids might affect colon cancer.

output: In a study looking at different medicines for helping people stop using heroin, researchers looked at 2467 people who took part in 23 different studies. They found that methadone, which is one medicine used, didn't seem to work better or worse than other medicines in helping people finish their treatment. When comparing methadone to other medicines like some painkillers or anxiety medicines, people often felt more pain and had to stop taking the medicine sooner. The studies showed that slowly reducing the dose of methadone while giving them another type of medicine helped make stopping feel less painful. But most people still ended up using heroin again. The information isn't always easy to compare because the ways the studies measured success were different.

output: This study looked at different ways doctors do heart procedures called angioplasty and stenting. They found that using a special arm method (transradial approach) might be better than another common way (transfemoral approach). When doctors used the special arm method, they saw fewer bad things happen right after the procedure, like when the heart stops working (cardiac death) and when people die from other causes (all-cause mortality). But they also saw more bleeding and problems at the place where the doctor put the needle into the arm. The special arm method didn't work as well as the old way at first, but it seemed safer overall. This special arm method might help prevent some serious problems after the procedure. However, we don't know if it will keep being better over a longer time, because that information wasn't available in this study.

output: A review of medical studies found that there are no direct comparisons between giving more or less food to very sick premature babies with a condition called CLD/BPD. But two studies did give us some clues. One study showed that feeding these babies a special formula with extra protein and minerals helped them grow better up to three months after starting the special formula. Another study looked at how much formula babies drank, but made sure they got the same amount of calories either way. This study found that the babies couldn't drink enough to meet their goals and there was no difference in how they grew, how well their lungs worked, swelling in their bodies, or how much water they needed. So far, there aren't any studies that compare giving more food to these babies to see if it helps them. More research is needed to find out if giving more food, especially in the form of thicker formulas or extra fluids, might help these babies grow better and stay healthier. Researchers also need to look at whether giving more of different types of food, like carbohydrates, proteins, or fats, could be helpful.

This study looked at 23 trials with 1806 women who had problems controlling their urine. In these trials, 717 women used special cones to help. The studies were small and sometimes hard to understand because they used different ways to measure success. Some people dropped out of the studies, which made it harder to know if the cones really worked. Seven studies only had short reports about their findings.

The study found that using the cones helped less than nothing helping, but it wasn't clear if this was true. It also didn't show that the cones worked better than squeezing muscles (PFMT) or using electricity (electrostimulation). There wasn't enough information to tell if using cones with squeezing muscles worked better than just using cones or just squeezing muscles.

Only a few studies looked at how well people felt after using the cones, and none looked at how much money it cost. Some studies only included women who had trouble holding their urine, while others needed women who had a specific type of problem called urodynamic stress incontinence.

Overall, the study suggests that using cones might be better than doing nothing to help with leaking urine, but we need more big, good-quality studies to be sure. Until then, doctors can offer cones as one way to help, if the woman likes them. But more research is needed before we can say for sure.

output:
This review looked at five studies with 1,726 patients to see if a special medicine mix helped people live longer or if it made their cancer grow slower. The mix didn't seem to help people live longer, but it did seem to make their cancer grow more slowly. This finding might be because only one study looked at this before. The evidence isn’t very strong because some studies didn’t follow good rules when they did their research.

The mix also seemed to cause less severe side effects like hair loss and diarrhea, but more severe side effects like low blood cells called neutrophils. We’re not sure how reliable these findings are because the studies weren’t perfect.

Overall, the mix of medicines doesn’t seem to give people with advanced or spread-out colon cancer a better chance of living longer. But it does seem to help their cancer grow more slowly. To know for sure, we need more studies with lots of people in each group to see if the mix really works better than just using the medicine alone.

output: In a study looking at 29 groups of people with a serious illness called pancreatic cancer, researchers compared two ways to help them feel better: using plastic tubes (stents) or having surgery. Using plastic tubes was linked to fewer problems during treatment, but it made it more likely that the tubes would get blocked again before the person died. However, plastic tubes cost less and helped people feel better more often. Metal tubes were found to be better at keeping the tubes open longer without getting blocked. But there wasn't enough information to know if metal tubes were better overall. Some types of plastic tubes didn't work as well as others. Adding a special valve to some plastic tubes helped keep them open longer. At the moment, doctors use metal tubes because they seem to work better. But for people who might not live very long, the metal tubes might not stay open as long as the plastic ones. More studies are needed to figure out which type of tube works best for each person.
