This study looked at different medicines put inside the vagina to help stop babies from being born. They checked 22 studies that involved 12,400 people in different parts of the world. Some of these studies used a medicine called LNG, which comes in different amounts. The studies looked at whether these medicines worked well to stop babies from being born, if they caused problems, and if people liked using them.

The medicine called LNG seemed to work pretty well and was safe. When they added up all the studies together, they found that for every 100 women who used it for a year, about 5 to 7 of them got pregnant. This is much better than when women don't use any birth control at all.

Other medicines also seemed to work, but there weren't as many studies about them. The most common problem was that some women's periods didn't come regularly. But the studies didn't find a clear link between how often the medicine was taken or how much was taken and the changes in periods.

Most women said they liked using this method, even though their periods sometimes changed. The studies showed good results, but they had some problems. Many of the studies were done a long time ago and didn't give us all the information we need. So while the results look promising, we need more recent and detailed studies to be sure it works and is safe. If it does work well, doctors might change how they talk about this method to women.

output: This research looked at two medicines, chlorpromazine and piperacetazine, to see if they help people with a mental illness called schizophrenia. They found 12 studies about these medicines, but only 5 were good enough to use. These studies were done a long time ago, in the 1970s. They didn't find much difference between the two medicines in how well they worked. Both medicines seemed to cause similar problems, like feeling sick or having trouble moving normally. But the studies weren't very good, so we can't be sure. There wasn't enough information about other important things, like how the medicines might affect the cost of care. Because the studies were not very strong, we can't say for sure which medicine is better. Right now, doctors and people with schizophrenia who need these medicines don't have good information to decide which one to take. More studies are needed to learn more.

output: This study looked at four different ways to help people take their medicine correctly when they're sick. Some of these ways worked better than others. One way, where nurses visited people's homes, helped them remember to take their medicine more often. But it didn't seem to make their sickness go away faster. Another way, where caregivers kept track of the medicine, also made people remember to take it more often, but not enough to be sure it really works. A third way, where kids got support from other kids who were also sick, didn't help them remember to take their medicine better, but it did help keep their sickness under control. Finally, another way, where kids took a special kind of medicine, also didn't help them remember to take it better, but it did help keep their sickness under control better. So, while some ways to help people take their medicine work, we need more studies to know which ones really help. We also need to find out why some ways work better at keeping sickness under control.

output: This review looked at 34 studies involving 2169 people who had blepharitis, which is a condition that makes your eyelids itchy and red. In 1661 people with a front part of their eyelids being affected, and 508 people with the back part, researchers found that putting medicine on the eyes helped make them feel better and got rid of some of the germs around the eyelids. Cleaning your eyelids can also help with the itchiness. But for other ways to treat blepharitis like taking medicine by mouth or using creams, the studies weren't clear enough to know if they really work. There isn’t strong proof that any of these treatments cure blepharitis. Some things you buy in stores aren’t proven to work either. More research is needed to see which treatments actually help. Researchers should try different treatments and compare them fairly, and they should follow people for at least a year to see if the treatments work over time. They should use special tests to measure how well the treatments work.

This study looked at different ways to fix broken bones in the hip area, especially for older people. They tested two types of metal rods: the Gamma nail and the sliding hip screw (SHS). The Gamma nail seemed to cause more problems like broken bones and needing to do surgery again. But it didn't make much difference in other things like infections or how long someone stayed in the hospital.

Another type of rod called the intramedullary hip screw (IMHS) also had more problems fixing the bone properly. But when it came to other issues like infections or how well someone could move after the surgery, there wasn't much difference between the Gamma nail and the SHS.

For some types of broken bones, using a special rod called a proximal femoral nail (PFN) didn't seem to cause more problems than the SHS. But for other types of broken bones, using a special rod called an intramedullary nail seemed to cause fewer problems with the bone not healing correctly.

Overall, the SHS seems to be better for fixing these hip fractures because it has fewer problems overall. But we need more studies to know if newer types of intramedullary nails might have fewer problems too. And for some types of broken bones, using an intramedullary nail might be better than using a plate, but we need more studies to be sure about this.

The study found that a special kind of exercise called modified constraint-induced movement therapy (mCIMT) seemed to help people move their arms better and less stiff for up to six months. Another type of exercise using a special splint for the elbow also helped keep the elbow joints from getting too tight, but only for about 14 weeks. output:
This research looked at six studies involving 142 children with a condition called hemophilia. These studies compared two ways of treating hemophilia: giving medicine regularly (prophylaxis) or only when they had a bleed (on-demand).

Two studies found that giving medicine regularly helped prevent bleeds, especially in the joints. They saw fewer joint bleeds in children who got regular medicine. But the studies weren't able to compare how well different types of regular medicine worked.

Three studies looked at hemophilia A, and one found that regular medicine reduced joint bleeds. Another study didn't find a clear difference between two types of regular medicine. One study looked at hemophilia B and found that getting medicine every week was better than every other week for preventing joint bleeds.

The studies also found that regular medicine might cause more problems like infections and something called an "inhibitor," which makes it harder to get the medicine working properly.

There's strong proof from these studies that regular medicine helps keep the joints healthy in children with hemophilia. But there isn't enough proof from studies to show that regular medicine stops bleeds and other problems in adults who already have damaged joints.

More studies are needed to figure out the best type of regular medicine and to see if it works well in adults.

output: This research looked at seven studies involving 766 women who were in labor. Four studies used a special liquid injected into the skin, two used it under the skin, and one used both. All the studies talked about pain in the lower back during labor. The studies were mostly done well, but some had small groups of women, didn't have complete information, or might not have been fair to compare the treatments. They all said that the women who got the special liquid had less pain compared to those who got something else. But because the way they measured pain wasn't always the same, they couldn't combine all the results to get a clearer picture. None of the studies looked at whether the women had better or worse births, how their babies did later, or if the women liked the pain relief. Some women said they wanted the same pain relief again, but others didn't. There were no serious problems reported. The studies showed that the special liquid didn't seem to help much with pain or make any big differences in how the babies were born or how the mothers felt overall. More studies need to be done to know if this liquid really helps with labor pain.

output: This study looked at different ways to help people who have trouble controlling their bowels. They checked 21 studies with a total of 1525 people. Half of these studies did a good job making sure everyone got the right treatment. Two small studies showed that using special tools called biofeedback and doing exercises helped more than just doing exercises alone. Another small study said adding biofeedback to another tool called electrical stimulation worked even better. When they looked at all the studies together, they found that adding electrical stimulation to biofeedback helped people control their bowels better than just using biofeedback. One study also said that a tool called sacral nerve stimulation worked better than just doing exercises or using biofeedback. But there wasn't enough information about other types of biofeedback or exercises. Some studies suggested that a type of biofeedback called rectal volume discrimination training might work better than a fake version. However, we don't know for sure if these treatments really work because there weren't many studies and some of them didn't follow the best methods. More studies need to be done to find out if these treatments are really helpful and safe.

This study looked at seven research projects comparing how well people do when they have either higher or lower levels of a gas called PEEP in their breathing machines. In five of these studies, the researchers kept the amount of air breathed in the same for both groups, but in the other two, they changed the amount slightly. Some of the studies had problems that might affect how reliable their results are, while others were done very carefully.

The main part of the study looked at how many people died before they left the hospital. When they compared the higher PEEP group to the lower PEEP group, they didn't see a big difference in who lived longer. They also checked if there were more problems with the breathing machines, like getting hurt, and again, there wasn't much difference.

This study looked at eight different studies about finding broken bones in the back, especially when people go to the hospital or doctor because they hurt their backs. Most of these studies had some problems, like not always doing things fairly or not telling us everything they did. 

In the hospital, about 6.5% to 11% of people who went there had broken bones in their back. In regular doctor visits, it was much lower, around 0.7% to 4.5%. They checked lots of different signs that might mean someone has a broken back, but only a few signs showed up in more than one study. 

They found that three signs in regular doctor visits could help tell if someone has a broken back, but the information wasn't very clear. One sign in the hospital was helpful too. When they put together several signs, they could better guess if someone has a broken back. But the signs alone aren't very good at guessing right all the time.

The study suggests that using a few signs together might help find broken backs, but it's not very strong evidence. Also, even when they use signs together, they still get some wrong guesses. This means that if doctors act on these signs without thinking carefully, it could lead to extra costs and other problems for patients. More research is needed to figure out which signs work best and how to report them clearly.

output: This research looked at some studies that tried to help Native American kids stop smoking and using something called smokeless tobacco. Two studies were big enough to count, and they both tried special programs that fit with Native American culture. These programs taught kids about healthy choices. But after a long time, the studies didn't show that these programs helped kids stop smoking or using smokeless tobacco better than usual care. One program did seem to work a little bit at first, but it didn't last. The studies weren't perfect, but they were pretty good overall. Because there aren't many studies like this, we don't know if these kinds of programs really work for Native American kids. We need more studies to find out. Many Native American kids start smoking earlier than other kids and continue smoking more often. This means they get sick from smoking more than other kids. To help, we need strong studies to see if these programs can help prevent kids from starting to smoke and to close the gap between how healthy Native American kids are compared to other kids.

output: This review looked at 32 studies to see if different types of special liquids help make babies from eggs. But the studies were done differently, so we couldn't combine the results. Only a few studies told us if the babies were born or if they became pregnant. In those studies, some said the special liquids didn’t make a difference, while others said one type might help more. But the studies that said it might help weren’t very strong. Some studies talked about whether the babies had problems during birth or after birth, but they didn’t find any differences. Many of the studies didn’t tell us where they got their money or how they did their work. Overall, we don’t have enough good information to say which liquid helps make babies better. We need more studies that do a good job comparing different liquids and follow up with the babies to know more.

This research looked at ten studies that tested if taking special good bacteria (probiotics) along with other medicines (antifungals) helps people get better faster. The studies had lots of people in them, about 1656 total. None of the studies were paid for by the companies that make the medicine. 

The studies showed that probiotics helped people feel better quickly (short-term cure) and also helped their bodies fight the bad fungus (mycological cure) more often than just using the antifungal medicine alone. They also helped stop the fungus from coming back in the first month after treatment (relapse rate).

But, it didn't help people stay better longer. It didn't make them feel better for a longer time after the treatment was over. And it didn't make them less likely to need extra medicine later on.

Taking probiotics did not cause more serious side effects. But we don't know if it causes any minor side effects because there weren't enough studies to find out.

We need more studies to be sure about all of this. These studies were not perfect, so we're not very confident in the results. More research is needed with better methods and bigger groups of people to learn more.

A study looked at how soon after tooth removal people get dental implants. They found that getting the implants right away didn't make much difference in how well they worked or how happy people were with them. However, after five years, people who got their implants right away thought it took less time to use them. The implants also looked better in their mouth. But there were more problems like infections in the gums for those who got their implants right away. 

The study had some limitations though. It wasn't very big and some parts weren't done very well. So while it suggests that getting implants right away might look better and be quicker, we don't have enough good information to know if it's better overall. We also don't know if putting in extra bone before the implant helps or if one way of doing it is better than another. More studies are needed to answer these questions.

The researchers aren't sure if everyone who started the study was counted or if some people didn't want to finish. Because they don't know everything about who was in the study, the scientists think the results might not be completely accurate.

But the study wasn't big enough to tell us if meditation helped people live longer or feel less tired or anxious. It also didn't look at how well people slept or if meditation caused any problems.

Because the study was small and not very detailed, we can't be sure about the results. More studies would help us understand if meditation really helps people with this kind of sickness. Right now, we don't have enough information to say for sure if meditation works or not.

This research looked at 37 studies that involved 3110 people who had a brain injury. Nine of these studies were new ones done since the last time this information was checked (in 2009). Five studies that were checked before were removed but then brought back because they were important. The studies included both grown-ups and kids who had brain injuries. Most of the studies started giving special medicine right away when the person got to the hospital or after a surgery called a craniotomy. All the treatments lasted at least 24 hours.

The studies looked at how many people died, if they were in a coma, or if they had serious problems like not being able to move much. But the results weren't always the same from one study to another. Some said the treatment helped, while others said it didn’t. Because the studies weren't all done the same way, we couldn't put them all together to see if the treatment really works better.

The researchers thought the studies weren't very good and couldn't tell if some studies might have been biased. They gave the evidence about whether the treatment helps or not a low grade. This means they're not sure if the treatment actually works or not.

There haven't been enough good studies to know if the treatment helps people with brain injuries. More research needs to be done, but it has to be done carefully to get better results.

This means we don't have enough good information to say if paracetamol should be used by itself or with other medicines for cancer pain. It's not clear if paracetamol makes a big difference in how people feel or if it has any effect at all.

This study looked at eleven different programs that try to help people stop smoking. These programs were in different places and had different ways of working. Some of these programs reported changes in how many people smoke less. Two big programs in California and Massachusetts saw more people stop smoking compared to other places in the country. Other smaller programs also seemed to help some people stop smoking. 

Four out of eight studies that looked at whether people stopped smoking or cut down found that the programs helped. But in one study, it wasn't clear if the program helped because they didn't separate quitting from just cutting down. And one program that didn't seem to help overall still made a difference for smokers and former smokers.

The study found that when states or communities do lots of TV and radio ads about not smoking, it can help people stop smoking. But the results aren't always the same. It's hard to know exactly why some programs work better than others because they're all a bit different. One big program in Massachusetts kept helping people stop smoking for eight years. Another in California worked well while the program was running and then after it ended. Programs in some areas also helped people stop smoking.

Overall, the evidence suggests that these kinds of programs can be helpful, but we need more studies to be sure. The programs seem to work best when they last for a long time and are done right. It's not clear if they work better for certain groups of people like older or younger people, or if they work better for people who have different backgrounds.

This review looked at seven studies with a total of 422 people who had schizophrenia. These studies compared a medicine called trifluoperazine with another type of medicine used to treat schizophrenia. The studies weren't always done in a way that makes them very reliable, but they didn't find that trifluoperazine worked better or worse than the other medicine. 

Both medicines seemed to work equally well, but people taking trifluoperazine had more side effects like movement problems. They also left the studies more often because of these side effects. 

The studies weren't very big or long, and some parts weren't described clearly. So while we know trifluoperazine doesn't seem to be better, we can't be sure it's definitely worse either. More studies would help us understand better if trifluoperazine is a good choice for treating schizophrenia.

This study looked at eleven studies that lasted at least a week. These studies involved about 950 people who had mostly moderate to severe pain. The studies compared different types of medicines called NSAIDs, which are often used to treat pain. Some studies also compared NSAIDs with other medicines like opioids, which are stronger painkillers. But none of the studies compared NSAIDs directly with each other or with opioids.

The studies weren't perfect because many didn't do a good job hiding which medicine people were getting, and some didn't follow all their participants to see if they finished the study. Because of this, we don't know how reliable the results are. The best we can say is that the evidence is very uncertain.

None of the studies showed that people's pain went down by at least half or that they felt much better. However, in four out of eleven studies, people's pain got much better after one or two weeks. This happened in 415 people in total, and the pain got so much better that it wasn't as bad as just having a mild ache.

Some people did have side effects like feeling thirsty, not wanting to eat, feeling sleepy, or having stomach problems. Many people stopped taking the medicine because it didn't work well or because of these side effects.

Sadly, there were two serious problems that might have been caused by the medicines, but it's hard to be sure. Also, 22 people died during the studies, but it's not clear if the medicines caused these deaths.

Overall, there isn't strong proof that NSAIDs help people with cancer pain get better. But some people did seem to feel a lot better after taking them for a few weeks. More research is needed to know if NSAIDs really work for everyone with cancer pain.

One study looked at women who had had diabetes before, and it didn't find that taking a special medicine called combined oestrogen and progestogen made a difference in things like miscarriages, stillbirths, or babies born too early. However, this special medicine might slightly increase the chance of the mother getting a certain type of cancer later in life. The other study looked at women who used a technique called IVF to help them get pregnant. This study also didn't find that the special medicine helped prevent miscarriages. Because of this, we don't have enough information from these studies to know if the special medicine helps prevent miscarriages. We think more research is needed to answer this question.

This study looked at different ways to help people with a condition called Bullous Pemphigoid (BP). They studied 10 groups of people, each with about 100 participants. Most of these groups didn't have a special sugar pill to compare against, so we're not sure if the treatments really worked better.

One group found that giving extra medicine called plasma exchange along with a steroid called prednisone helped control BP better after just one month. But after six months, another group didn't see this difference.

The study also found that different amounts of a steroid called prednisolone didn't make much difference. Adding other medicines like azathioprine or mycophenolate mofetil didn't seem to work better either. Some traditional Chinese medicines didn't help either.

In some cases, using stronger steroid creams was helpful, but it might cause more problems. Using weaker creams was safe and helped control BP too. Doctors think starting with a small amount of a steroid called prednisolone might be enough to control BP and avoid side effects.

Adding other medicines like azathioprine or mycophenolate mofetil, or using a combination of tetracycline and nicotinamide, might be useful, but more research is needed to know for sure.

This research looked at whether getting special help with teeth cleaning, called professional oral care, helps prevent lung infections called pneumonia in older people living in nursing homes. They studied four groups of people, but the studies weren't perfect. 

They couldn't tell if the special teeth cleaning helped prevent pneumonia overall because the studies didn't show a clear difference. They also couldn't say for sure if it helped prevent the first time someone got pneumonia. But they did find some low-quality evidence suggesting that special teeth cleaning might help keep older people alive longer if they do get pneumonia.

There wasn't enough good quality evidence to know if special teeth cleaning helps prevent all kinds of sicknesses. One study showed there were fewer problems like mouth sores, but it's not clear if these are good or bad. None of the studies looked at whether regular teeth cleaning would work better than doing nothing.

The research team thinks that while it seems like special teeth cleaning might help, more studies are needed to be really sure. They also don't have strong proof about which specific ways of cleaning teeth are best. More research is needed to figure out the best way to keep older people's teeth clean and healthy.

This study looked at ten trials involving 1658 people to see if a special breathing technique called "open lung ventilation" helped people with a condition called ARDS. Five of these trials were done very carefully, while the other five were a bit less so. In six of the trials, doctors used a special technique to help open up parts of the lungs before giving regular breathing support. 

The results showed that this special breathing technique did help reduce deaths in the ICU by about 17%, which means it slightly lowered the chance of dying in the ICU. However, it didn't seem to affect how many people died within 28 days or how many died in the hospital overall. 

There was also no clear difference in how often people got hurt by too much pressure in their lungs. But because there were some differences between the groups in how they were treated, it's hard to know for sure if the special breathing technique really made a difference.

Overall, the evidence isn't very strong because the trials had some differences that could have affected the results. So we can't be completely certain about whether this technique helps or not. The information is considered to be of low quality.

output:
A study looked at two ways to help people with a blocked part of their colon: putting a special tube (called a stent) inside the colon or having an operation right away. They studied 207 people who had these treatments. 

The operation seemed to work better because it helped people feel better faster—about 3.5 days compared to about 1 day with the stent. But using the stent didn't make people die more often. About 2 out of every 100 people died in both groups after 30 days. 

Using the stent also caused some problems like the tube breaking or moving around, but these happened in about 5 out of every 100 tries. The operation also caused some problems, but not more than the stent. About 45 out of every 100 people had problems after the operation, and about 39 out of every 100 people had problems with the stent.

Both ways took people to the hospital for about the same amount of time—around 11 days for the stent and 17 days for the operation. The operation also took a little longer to do—about 144 minutes compared to about 114 minutes for the stent. And people lost less blood when they had the operation—about 50 milliliters compared to about 350 milliliters with the stent.

Overall, the operation seemed to work a bit better, but both ways were pretty safe. The stent might be easier on people by making them go home sooner and needing less time in the hospital. But we need more studies to know if this is true for everyone.

This study looked at different ways to put a tube into a child's artery using a tool called ultrasound. They tested it against two other methods: feeling the area with your hands (palpation) and listening to the sound waves (Doppler auditory assistance).

They did five studies, each testing ultrasound in different ways. Some studies weren't very clear about how they planned their tests, which might have affected the results. But overall, the studies showed that using ultrasound helps doctors put the tube in better the first time and causes fewer problems like swelling around the tube.

Two out of the five studies told them how often things went wrong, and those studies showed ultrasound helped too. But because there were only a few studies and not many children in them, we can't be totally sure about these findings. So, we think there's a good chance that ultrasound works better, but we're not completely certain yet.

The studies also found that using ultrasound made it easier to put the tube in again if it didn't go in the first time. This happened more often in younger children than in older ones. The studies also said that if the doctors who used ultrasound were really good at it, they might do even better.

Overall, the evidence suggests that ultrasound helps make putting the tube in easier and safer, especially for younger children. But we need more studies to be really sure.

This research looked at different ways of putting an IUD (a small device put inside a woman's uterus to help prevent pregnancy) into her body. They studied 7,119 women who got IUDs. Some of these studies said that putting the IUD right away might make it come out more often than if you wait a little bit. But other studies didn't find this happened. 

One study found that putting in a special kind of IUD called Copper 7 right away might cause it to come out more often than waiting. Another study found that putting in a different type of IUD called Levonorgestrel-Releasing Intrauterine System or CuT380A right away might also make it come out more often. 

Another study found that a newer type of IUD called Nova T might make it harder for women to keep their periods, which could mean they're having trouble getting pregnant. 

Some studies also looked at putting in an IUD right after a woman has an abortion. They found that putting in an IUD right away might make it happen more often, but by six months later, more women were using the IUD when they put it in right away. 

Overall, the evidence isn't very strong about whether putting in an IUD right away or waiting makes a big difference. The studies had some problems that made it hard to know for sure. So while there are some hints that putting in an IUD right away might have some risks, we need more research to be really sure.

More studies need to look at different kinds of exercises and how often people do them, and make sure the people in the studies have similar levels of the condition. Right now, there isn't enough good information to know if exercising helps people with CVI.

This research looked at 471 people with a condition called AsPD who were trying to stop using drugs like cocaine. They tried different ways to help these people, but not all the ways worked equally well. Some ways helped people stay away from drugs better than others, but they didn't always help with other things like being aggressive or having fewer bad things happen to them.

Two ways that seemed to work were:
- Talking to a therapist about their feelings and problems, along with regular support, which helped some people stay away from drugs.
- Getting rewards for staying clean, along with regular support, also helped some people stay away from drugs.

But these ways didn't always help with other things like being aggressive or having fewer bad things happen. The research found that there wasn't enough good information to know if any of these ways really help people with AsPD. Also, very few studies looked at whether these ways helped with things like being aggressive or having fewer bad things happen.

The best ways found were for people who were already using drugs and wanted to stop. But none of the ways helped with being more antisocial. More research is needed to find better ways to help people with this condition.

This research looked at a type of medicine called glucocorticoids that might help women get pregnant using a process called IVF. They studied four groups of women, but some information wasn't clear enough to use. In total, 416 women took part in the studies. Two studies had problems explaining how they picked which women got which medicine, but the other two did a good job.

The studies didn't find strong proof that taking this medicine helps women have more babies. If a woman has a 15% chance of having a baby when she doesn't take the medicine, it's not clear if taking the medicine will make that chance go up or down. The same goes for the chance of getting pregnant, where the medicine might make that chance go up or stay the same.

There wasn't enough information to know if the medicine causes more than usual problems like twins or miscarriages. Also, the studies didn't look at whether the medicine caused side effects. Overall, the research suggests that while the medicine might help some women get pregnant, it probably doesn't significantly increase their chances of having a baby. More studies are needed to learn more about this.

output: This study looked at 15,936 people over 75 years old who had high blood pressure. They wanted to see if lowering their blood pressure could help prevent memory problems. Four studies were done, but they didn't find a clear difference between those who took medicine to lower their blood pressure and those who took a sugar pill. The studies also showed that people's blood pressure went down when they took the medicine, but it wasn't enough to make a big difference in preventing memory problems. Some people had to stop taking the medicine because of side effects, but the same thing happened with the sugar pill group too. The studies had some problems because many people in the control groups (who didn't get the medicine) were already getting medicine for their high blood pressure anyway. Because of these issues, we can't say for sure that lowering blood pressure helps prevent memory problems in older people with high blood pressure. To get clearer answers, researchers might need to look at all the patients' information instead of just the groups they were comparing.

This research looked at two studies involving 97 women who had a type of cancer called ovarian cancer that didn't respond well to certain treatments. One study compared a medicine called leuprorelin to another medicine called treosulfan. The other study compared leuprorelin to a sugar pill. Both studies had some problems because they used different kinds of controls. 

The studies didn't find much difference in how long people lived longer (overall survival) or how long they survived without their cancer getting worse (progression-free survival) when using leuprorelin or treosulfan. This means it's hard to know if one is better than the other based on these studies. 

Both medicines caused hair loss and tiredness, but it wasn't clear if leuprorelin caused more of these side effects. Other serious side effects like sickness, feeling sick, or having trouble with nerves weren't clearly seen to be different between the medicines. 

The studies also didn't report on how well people felt (quality of life) or how long they lived after starting the medicine. They only talked about the side effects for the medicine being studied, not the sugar pill. 

Overall, the studies don't give us enough information to decide if leuprorelin or treosulfan work better for this type of ovarian cancer. We can't be sure about the benefits or risks because the studies aren't very strong.

output: A study looked at 16,154 people with a lung condition called COPD who used a medicine called ICS for more than six months. The study found that using ICS didn't help slow down how badly their breathing got worse over time. But it did help stop them from getting sick more often. Using ICS also helped keep their breathing better over time. However, some people had a sore throat or a fungal infection in their mouth while taking the medicine. Also, there were more cases of pneumonia in people taking ICS compared to those not taking it. Overall, the study suggests that while ICS might help COPD patients feel better and have fewer coughing spells, they need to be aware of these possible side effects. Patients and doctors should think about both the good and bad parts before deciding if this medicine is right for someone with COPD.

This review looked at 11 studies about using antibiotics for colds and stuffy noses. Six studies talked about colds, involving up to 1047 people, and five studies talked about stuffy noses, involving up to 791 people. One study just told us about bad side effects, and one study didn't give enough information to include it in the main findings.

The studies were mixed. Antibiotics didn’t seem to help people get over their colds faster or keep their stuffy noses for shorter times. In fact, sometimes they might make people feel worse. For adults, taking antibiotics seemed to make them feel even worse. But for kids, it didn’t seem to make them feel any different.

For stuffy noses, antibiotics didn’t seem to work either. Some studies showed that antibiotics might actually make the stuffiness last longer. And in all the studies, antibiotics caused more bad side effects.

Overall, the review suggests that antibiotics don’t help with colds or stuffy noses. It also shows that antibiotics can cause problems. Because of this, doctors shouldn’t usually prescribe antibiotics for these conditions.

This research looked at ways to help babies born too early who have high levels of potassium in their blood. There were three small studies that tried different treatments. Only one study had enough information to look at how much urine the babies made. None of the studies did a good job hiding which treatment group the babies were in, so it might have been hard for the doctors to know if the treatments really worked.

In one study, using sugar and medicine called insulin seemed to lower the chance of the baby having a serious brain injury. But this wasn't proven very well because the study was small and not very good.

Another study found that breathing in medicine called albuterol helped lower potassium levels in the blood. But again, the study wasn't very big or well done.

The researchers couldn't find any studies about other medicines that might help. They also didn't find any serious problems with the treatments they looked at.

Because these studies were small and not very good, the researchers can't make strong suggestions about which treatment works best. However, they think that giving sugar and medicine called insulin might be better than putting medicine in the baby's bottom. And they think that breathing in albuterol might also work, but more studies need to be done to be sure.

Overall, there isn't enough good information to tell doctors exactly what to do for these babies, but some treatments seem to work better than others.

This study looked at 21,379 people with diabetes who had heart problems before. They wanted to know if taking certain medicines called ADP receptor antagonists helped prevent heart attacks and strokes. Three studies compared these medicines to another medicine called aspirin. Five studies compared different types of these medicines to see which worked best.

All the studies were done well, but they didn't have enough information to tell if the medicines helped prevent all kinds of bad health problems. One study found that taking a medicine called ticlopidine wasn’t better than taking nothing at preventing all causes of death or heart attacks. Another study found that taking a medicine called clopidogrel might slightly lower the chance of having a stroke, but it wasn’t clear if this happened often enough to be useful.

The studies also didn’t give much information about other things like whether these medicines caused side effects, or how much they cost. So, doctors don’t have strong proof about whether these medicines should be used to help people with diabetes and heart problems. More studies are needed to learn more about how well these medicines work for people with diabetes.

More studies need to be done to see if letting mom and baby stay together really helps more babies get breast milk.

We looked at 394 studies and found information from 9 clinical trials that studied people with a type of eye problem called retinitis pigmentosa (RP). These trials included 866 people, mostly young adults, who had different types of RP. Some trials looked at just vitamin A, some just DHA, and some both together. But we couldn't see the full details of how they did their studies, which made it hard to know if they followed good rules.

None of the studies showed that taking vitamin A or DHA helped stop the eyesight getting worse. Also, none of the studies found that taking these vitamins caused any bad side effects.

The studies didn't show that taking vitamin A and DHA helped people's eyesight stay better over time. However, some of the studies found that taking DHA might make the light-sensing part of the eye work better in some people, but this wasn't seen in other studies.

Based on these three studies, we don't think taking vitamin A and DHA helps people with RP keep their eyesight better. Future studies should look more closely at whether taking these vitamins might help some people, especially those who haven't taken them before. They should also use more people in their studies to make sure they can see any possible benefits clearly.

This study looked at different medicines used to help people with asthma. They compared two medicines: salmeterol and salbutamol. The study involved 62,815 people with asthma, including some children. In six studies, they couldn't find information about very serious problems that might happen. For everyone, there wasn't enough proof that salmeterol caused more serious health issues. But in some studies, it seemed like salmeterol might cause more serious problems than salbutamol. 

For all people with asthma, there was a slight chance that salmeterol might lead to more serious health problems. This chance was a bit higher than usual, but not by much. For every 188 people taking salmeterol, one more person had a serious problem over 28 weeks. 

The study didn't find strong evidence that salmeterol causes more serious problems in children compared to adults. It also didn't find strong evidence that salmeterol causes more asthma-related deaths in children. However, it did find that salmeterol might slightly increase the risk of dying from asthma in people who don't use a medicine called an inhaled corticosteroid. 

The study found that salmeterol might increase the risk of asthma-related deaths in people who don't take inhaled corticosteroids. But it's hard to know if this happens because the numbers aren't very clear. The study also found that salmeterol might increase the risk of serious health problems in people who don't take inhaled corticosteroids. 

Overall, the study suggests that salmeterol might cause more serious health problems, especially in people who don't take inhaled corticosteroids. But the exact risks for children are still unclear because not many children were studied.

A review of four studies with 494 participants looked at whether giving different amounts of a medicine called warfarin helps people reach a target blood clotting level called INR faster after they start taking the medicine. Three studies with 383 participants found that giving 10 milligrams of warfarin worked better than 5 milligrams for people who were not in the hospital. This means that more people reached the target INR level within 5 days when they got the 10-milligram dose. However, there was some disagreement between the studies about this. One study also found that giving 5 milligrams of warfarin helped more people reach the target INR level, but only for people who were not in the hospital. 

The studies did not find that either dose made a big difference in preventing blood clots coming back or in causing serious bleeding. They also did not find that either dose made a difference in how long people stayed in the hospital. 

Overall, there is some uncertainty about which dose of warfarin works best for reaching the target INR level quickly. This is because the studies had different groups of people and followed them for different lengths of time. More research would be helpful to clarify which dose might work best.

This study looked at fourteen different trials involving 1,724 people who had ear problems called CSOM. The way they defined CSOM and how bad it was could be different in each trial. Some trials also included other ear problems. The way the studies were done wasn't always very good.

Topical quinolone antibiotics (a type of medicine put directly into the ear) worked better than nothing at getting rid of fluid in the ear after one week. But when we looked at all the data together, there wasn't much difference between quinolone and other types of antibiotics (without steroid help) after one week or three weeks. There was a small hint that quinolone might work better after two weeks, but this wasn't proven because it could have been just one trial making a difference.

Topical quinolone antibiotics also worked better at curing CSOM than antiseptics (cleaning agents put in the ear). But when comparing quinolone to other types of antibiotics without steroids, the results weren't as clear. We need more studies to figure out if these other antibiotics work as well or better.

The studies didn't give us strong information about whether quinolone antibiotics are safer than other treatments. They did show that topical quinolone antibiotics can get rid of fluid in the ear better than nothing or antiseptics. However, we don't know yet if they cause fewer side effects or if they're safer overall.

More studies are needed to see if quinolone antibiotics are better than other types of antibiotics without steroids, especially over longer periods of time. We also need to look at whether they cause fewer problems like hearing loss or other issues.

This research looked at different ways to help people feel better after a type of surgery called robotic radical prostatectomy. This surgery helps men who have a problem with their prostate gland. The study included 170 men, most of whom were older adults. They were divided into two groups: one group got one kind of medicine to help them sleep during the surgery, and the other group got another kind. 

The study found that there wasn't much difference in how much pain the men felt after the surgery, whether they used propofol or the other medicine. But it did find that using propofol helped stop some sicknesses that can happen after surgery, like feeling sick to your stomach, for about six hours. Propofol also seemed to help keep the pressure inside the eyes lower than when the other medicine was used. 

However, we're not sure if this means less eye problems during the surgery. Also, the study only had a few men, so the results might not apply to everyone. The information isn't very strong because the study was small and didn't explain everything clearly. There's not much other information available about which medicine works best for these kinds of surgeries. A new study is starting that will look at more people, including women, and will try to answer these questions better.

Overall, the medicines seem to help most children with breathing problems and big adenoids, but we need more time to know if they work well over a longer period.

In total, we looked at 12 studies with 461 patients. All of these studies were considered to have some uncertainty about their results.

Two small studies compared a procedure called LASB to a sugar pill. They found that LASB didn’t seem to help reduce pain in the short term. One study that lasted longer found that LASB might help reduce pain after a year, but the results weren’t clear. Another study showed that adding LASB to physical therapy didn’t make much difference in pain relief.

Eight smaller studies compared LASB to other treatments. Most of these studies found that LASB didn’t provide better pain relief than the other treatments. One study found that guided LASB wasn’t different from unguided LASB in terms of pain relief.

Overall, there were some small benefits seen, but most of the studies didn’t show strong evidence that LASB helps with pain. The studies also found that LASB isn’t very harmful, but there just isn’t enough good-quality information to say if it works well or not.

output: The research looked at whether women who walk around and sit up during labor had different experiences compared to those who stay in bed. The results suggest that women who stand up and move around during the early part of labor (first stage) had their labor last about 1 hour and 22 minutes shorter than those who stayed in bed. They were also less likely to need a cesarean section and less likely to get an epidural, which is when doctors give medicine to help them feel less pain during labor. Their babies were less likely to need special care after birth too. However, the study found no difference in how long it took for the baby to come out or in how the mom and baby did afterwards. Some of the studies had problems, so we can't be completely sure these results apply to everyone. But overall, the evidence shows that moving around during labor can help make things easier for both mom and baby. So, if you're in low-risk labor, it's good to talk to your doctor about the benefits of standing up and moving around. Your doctor can help you find comfortable positions to use during labor.

output: A study looked at different ways to help people feel better when they have wrist problems. They checked on 884 people who had these problems. The study found that wearing a special wrist brace helped people feel less pain and be more active after four weeks. Another way that worked was using ultrasound, a kind of light energy, for two weeks. But it didn't work right away, it took seven weeks to see some improvement. After six months, the ultrasound still helped. Some medicines like steroids and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (like ibuprofen) also helped people feel better after two weeks. But other medicines like diuretics (water pills) and vitamin B6 didn’t seem to help much. Yoga and a special type of wrist movement called carpal bone mobilization also helped reduce pain. For people with diabetes, getting steroid and insulin shots helped their wrist pain go down. Using special keyboards at work didn’t seem to help much either. There wasn’t enough information about other treatments like magnets, lasers, or chiropractic care. So far, taking steroids, using a brace, ultrasound, yoga, and special wrist movements seem to work well in the short term. But we need more studies to know if these treatments last a long time and if one is better than another.

output:
A study looked at two types of treatments called ERT and HRT to see if they help keep the brain healthy in older women who have gone through menopause. They studied 16 women out of 24 who got the treatments. The study didn't find that either treatment helped prevent problems with thinking skills after taking them for five and four years, respectively. Some studies showed that the treatments might make thinking skills worse instead of better. The studies also found that the treatments didn’t seem to work well over time. 

The results suggest that ERT and HRT don’t help keep older women’s brains healthy when they take these treatments for a short time or longer. However, we don’t know if different groups of women might get different results. We also don’t know if the type of menopause, the way the treatments are given, or the amount of treatment makes a difference. More research is needed to answer these questions. For now, doctors can’t recommend ERT or HRT to help keep older women’s brains healthy because the current evidence isn’t strong enough.

This study looked at seven trials with 1369 people to see if giving a medicine longer helped more people get better. Most of these studies weren't very good at showing they were fair. Some studies used one way to decide who was a "slow responder" and others used another way. But none of the studies looked at the main things they wanted to know about.

The study found that when people took the medicine for 72 weeks instead of 48 weeks, more people stayed healthy without the virus coming back. This happened whether the study used one way or the other to decide who was a slow responder. Also, fewer people got sick again during the time they were taking the medicine.

However, the study didn't find that this worked for everyone. It also didn't look at how many people died or if there were more side effects from taking the medicine longer. The study wasn't perfect because some important information wasn't shared.

Because the study wasn't perfect, we can't be sure if giving the medicine longer really helps everyone. We need more studies to know if this should be a new rule for treating people with a certain kind of infection.

output: A study looked at whether getting special pictures of the brain right after surgery helps people live longer when they have a type of brain tumor called glioblastoma. This study only looked at 125 people who had surgery for this type of tumor. Most of these people had their tumors removed as much as possible and then got radiation and a medicine called temozolomide. The study found that getting these pictures soon after surgery didn't seem to make a big difference in how long people lived, either one year or two years after the diagnosis. The study wasn't perfect because it might have some problems. There's not much information about whether getting these pictures sooner costs more money or if it works better. The study suggests that doctors use these pictures mostly because they check if there's still any tumor left, which can help them do another operation if needed. More research is needed to find out the best time to get these pictures for people with glioblastoma. Also, studies with children who have this type of tumor might help figure out the best times to get these pictures for grown-ups too.

In a study looking at different ways to spot schizophrenia, researchers looked at 21 studies with 6253 people. Most of the studies weren't very detailed about how they did their work. 

The test called FRS was used in 20 out of the 21 studies. It helped tell schizophrenia apart from other illnesses. When it worked well, it correctly identified people with schizophrenia about 75% to 95% of the time. But when it didn't work perfectly, it sometimes said some people had schizophrenia when they really didn't. This happened in about 5 to 19 out of every 100 people who got the test. 

When doctors used FRS to decide who needed more help, they sometimes made mistakes. They might think someone had schizophrenia when they really didn't, or they might miss someone who actually did have schizophrenia. This could mean those people might not get the help they need right away, or they might be sent home too soon. 

But even though FRS isn't perfect, it's still a good tool for doctors to use. It helps them quickly see who might need extra attention. As new tests come along, we hope they'll do even better. For now, FRS is a simple way to help doctors make decisions about who needs more help.

We split the studies into two groups: one group with patients who had major surgeries, and another group with other patients who were in the ICU. For the ICU patients, using a special tool called PAC didn't seem to make a big difference in how many people died. It also didn't change how long they stayed in the ICU or in the hospital.

For the patients who had major surgeries, using PAC didn't seem to lower their chances of dying either. Five out of eight studies looked at whether preparing patients before surgery (called "pre-operative optimization") helped, but it didn't seem to make a difference.

This research looked at two ways to help women get pregnant using a special kind of medicine called IVF. They studied 788 women in total, with the biggest study including 396 women. They wanted to know if one way (natural cycle IVF) worked as well as another way (standard IVF).

For getting pregnant, there wasn't enough clear proof that natural cycle IVF was better than standard IVF. For some things like having a baby after a few tries, it seemed like natural cycle IVF might be a bit less successful. But for other things like having a healthy baby, there wasn't enough information to tell which way was better.

There was also some uncertainty about whether natural cycle IVF caused a condition called OHSS, which can make you feel sick. And while natural cycle IVF didn't seem to cause more twins, it didn't show a clear advantage in other areas either.

One study found that fewer eggs were retrieved when using natural cycle IVF. However, we don't know if this means it's worse overall because the study isn't finished yet.

The researchers think more studies are needed to see if natural cycle IVF is a good option. They suggest comparing it to standard IVF in future studies to find out which works best. These studies should look at many different things like how many treatments are needed to get pregnant, how much it costs, and any side effects.

output: This study looked at three small groups of women to see if a medicine called prostaglandin helped them after they gave birth. The medicine comes in two types: one called sulprostone and the other called misoprostol. Both were given to help the placenta come out after birth. But the study found that the medicine didn't work better than a sugar pill (placebo) to reduce the need for doctors to remove the placenta by hand, or to stop heavy bleeding after birth. It also didn't seem to help much with the amount of blood lost or how long it took for the placenta to come out. However, more women in the medicine group had a feeling called shivering after the medicine. The study wasn't very good, so we can't be sure if the medicine really helps or not. There's not enough strong proof yet to change how doctors treat this problem. We need bigger and better studies to know if the medicine works or not.

output:
This study looked at two groups of dental practices to see if giving dentists extra money to do more work would make them do more or less. They studied 503 dental practices with 821 dentists and 4771 patients. But the way the studies were done wasn't perfect, so we can't be sure about the results. 

One study tried to find out if giving dentists extra money to do more work made them do more check-ups and cleanings. It did show that when dentists got extra money, they did more check-ups. But this happened only in some parts of Scotland, so it might not work the same way in other places. The study didn't look at whether patients got better or worse because of the extra check-ups.

The other study compared two ways of paying dentists: one where they get paid for each visit and another where they get a fixed amount of money no matter how many visits they have. This study found that dentists who got the fixed amount of money did fewer fillings and tooth extractions, but they gave more advice to help prevent cavities. They also saw fewer patients overall. But the study couldn't tell us if these changes helped or hurt the patients.

Overall, the studies aren't very strong, so we can't be totally sure what happens when dentists get extra money. More research is needed to understand if this affects how much care patients get and if it's good or bad for them.

output: This research looked at three studies that involved 285 premature babies. These studies found that giving arginine to these babies might help them avoid a serious condition called NEC, which can be dangerous. The studies suggest that arginine could reduce the chance of developing NEC by about half. This means that out of every six babies given arginine, one fewer baby would develop NEC. However, the studies were small, so we need more research to be sure if this works for all babies. Giving arginine didn't seem to cause any bad side effects like low blood pressure or changes in blood sugar levels. But we don't have enough information yet to tell doctors to give arginine to all premature babies. More studies are needed to confirm if arginine helps prevent NEC and to see if it affects other health problems later in life.

This study looked at 12 different groups of people who had heart problems. These people had either simple or complicated blockages in their arteries. The researchers tried a new treatment called PTCRA, which uses a special balloon and wire mesh tube to open up the blocked arteries. They also tried a regular balloon treatment called PTCA.

For simple blockages, the new treatment didn't seem to help more than the regular treatment. But for complicated blockages, the new treatment didn't work better either. It might even make some things worse, like causing spasms in the artery, making holes in it, or blocking it temporarily.

The new treatment didn't cause more serious problems like heart attacks or needing emergency surgery. However, it caused more minor problems like spasms, small holes, and temporary blockages. 

The study found that if the regular treatment works, the new treatment doesn't offer much extra benefit. There isn't enough information yet to know if the new treatment should always be used after the regular treatment fails. But sometimes, when other treatments don't work, the new treatment might still help.

output: This study looked at one trial involving 120 families and 143 children. The trial used day care centers but some kids in the control group (the group that didn't get day care) still got day care services. The study tried to see if day care helped kids learn better or if it made them more or less likely to have problems growing up. They tested things like how well kids could think and how they were doing socially. They also checked if moms had jobs and how much money the families had. But the study couldn't tell us if day care helped or hurt these things. The study wasn't very good because some kids in the control group got day care anyway. There isn't enough good information to give clear advice about whether day care helps or hurts kids' development. More studies are needed to find out, especially ones that don't have extra things happening that aren't usual in regular day care. These studies could help us understand why day care might work or not work.

This research looked at 15 studies involving 1098 people who had received transplants. Six studies compared getting medicine before they got a problem with a dummy pill or waiting until they got sick before taking medicine. Eight studies compared getting medicine before they got sick with taking medicine regularly to stop the virus. One study compared taking the medicine by mouth with taking it through a vein.

The studies weren't perfect, but most of them followed the rules well. They didn't lose many people from their studies, and they didn’t try to trick the people taking part about which medicine they were getting. Only one study made sure that the people doing the tests didn’t know which group the people in the study were in.

When comparing the medicine to a dummy pill or regular treatment, the medicine helped prevent a condition called CMV disease better. It also helped prevent another condition called leucopenia, which means having fewer white blood cells. But it didn’t help prevent other problems like needing new organs or getting sick from other things.

When comparing the medicine to regular medicine to stop the virus, the studies didn’t show much difference. The studies had some problems because they were different from each other, so we can’t be sure if one is better than the other.

Not many studies have looked at this before, and the medicine seems to work better than regular medicine to prevent CMV disease. But more studies are needed to see if one type of medicine is really better than the other for preventing CMV disease and other problems after a transplant.

This study looked at twelve trials involving 1,856 women. Eight trials compared getting progestogen treatment with not getting any treatment, and four compared just getting progestogen with not getting any treatment at all. The trials happened in different places like India, Jordan, the UK, and the US. Some women had already had several miscarriages, while others had only had a couple.

The studies found that for most of them, women who got progestogen had fewer miscarriages than those who didn't get it. This seems to be true whether the women had had a few miscarriages or many. However, the way they gave the progestogen and how long they gave it varied from trial to trial.

Most of the studies were done well, but some parts weren't perfect. When they looked at all the women together, they found that progestogen might help prevent miscarriages. But when they looked at just the women who had had miscarriages before, they couldn't tell if progestogen made a difference.

Progestogen also seemed to slightly increase the chance of having a baby survive until full term. But the evidence for this wasn't very strong, so we're not sure if it really helps.

There wasn't enough information to know if progestogen affects things like morning sickness, depression, or problems with babies after birth. Also, the studies didn't look at how much babies weighed at birth or if they had any health problems.

Overall, for women who have had miscarriages before, taking progestogen might help prevent another miscarriage in their next pregnancy. But more research is needed to be sure.

So right now, doctors don't have enough proof to change how they treat women with sickle cell anemia during pregnancy. More studies are needed to learn more.

This review looked at twenty studies with 2337 people to see if getting some extra help about their illness helped them take their medicine better and stay well longer. Most of the studies compared getting extra help (called brief psychoeducation) with just getting regular information. 

People who got extra help were less likely to stop taking their medicine right away (short term), but they didn't do much better at keeping up with doctor visits (medium and long term). However, they had fewer problems coming back to the doctor later (medium term).

The extra help seemed to make it less likely that people would have more problems with their illness (medium term). Some studies showed that people who got extra help did better overall, felt better quicker, and had less anxiety and depression. They also did better in helping with their daily activities and didn't have as much trouble with their social life.

While most of the studies weren't perfect, the results suggest that getting extra help might be good for people's health. But we need more big, well-done studies to know for sure if this works and how best to do it.

This research looked at different ways to help women who have heavy bleeding after giving birth. They studied ten groups of women in total, with 4052 women participating. Some groups got a medicine called misoprostol along with other medicines to stop bleeding, while others just got other medicines. The study found that adding misoprostol didn't make it better for things like the mother dying or getting very sick. It also didn't help the mother need to stay in the hospital's special care unit or have her uterus removed. However, some women in the misoprostol group lost even more blood than before. Also, more women in the misoprostol group felt sick, like throwing up or having chills.

Two groups were tested with another medicine called oxytocin. These groups didn't have much difference, but women who took oxytocin lost less blood overall. Oxytocin caused fewer side effects than misoprostol.

The study also looked at using estrogen and a medicine called tranexamic acid, but these weren't enough to draw clear conclusions. Another study tried a different method to stop bleeding, but it wasn't big enough to know if it helped.

The researchers think that oxytocin works better than misoprostol for treating heavy bleeding after birth. If oxytocin doesn't work, they suggest trying tranexamic acid or other methods that haven't been tested yet. More research is needed to find the best way to help women whose bleeding doesn't stop with the usual treatments.

This study looked at 39 different medical tests on 4216 people to see if using special liquids called antimicrobial lock solutions helps prevent problems with central venous catheters (CVCs) used for dialysis. Out of these tests, 27 studies had enough information to compare. Most of the tests didn't have many problems being fair in their comparisons.

The tests found that using antimicrobial lock solutions probably lowers the chance of something called catheter-related infection (CRI) by about 38%, which means it's likely to happen less often. But they're not sure if it makes much difference in preventing blood clots around the catheter.

When they looked at different types of antimicrobial lock solutions, they found that:

- Antibiotic lock solutions probably lower the chance of CRI by about 30%.
- Non-antibiotic lock solutions probably lower CRI by about 60% for tunnelled CVCs, but don't seem to help much for non-tunnelled CVCs.
- Both antibiotic and non-antibiotic lock solutions probably lower the chance of CRI by about 76%.

However, when they checked if these solutions also helped prevent blood clots, they weren't sure. They think antibiotic lock solutions probably make little or no difference, while non-antibiotic lock solutions probably make little or no difference too.

Overall, the doctors aren't very confident in these results because there wasn't enough good-quality evidence. They think more studies are needed to know if these special liquids really work and are safe.

This research looked at different ways to lower a person's potassium levels when it gets too high, which can be dangerous. We checked seven studies with 241 people to see if they worked, but the studies weren't all done the same way, so we couldn't combine them easily. Some studies didn't tell us enough about how they did things.

The studies showed that a medicine called salbutamol, which is usually used to help breathing problems, can lower potassium levels. When given through a nebulizer (a machine that turns the medicine into a mist you breathe in), it works quickly, starting to lower potassium levels within an hour. When given as a spray (metered-dose inhaler), it also lowers potassium levels, though not as fast. 

Salbutamol seems to work as well as another medicine called insulin-dextrose, but better than another medicine called bicarbonate. It's also better than a medicine called aminophylline. But none of these medicines were compared to other medicines like IV calcium or potassium-binding resins, which haven't been studied much.

Overall, the research shows that salbutamol is one of the best medicines to lower potassium levels, especially when given through a nebulizer. However, we don't have strong proof that other medicines work as well or better. More studies are needed to know if these medicines really help prevent bad health problems.

This study looked at different ways to help pregnant women who use drugs. They checked 14 studies with 1298 women and their babies. Nine studies looked at helping moms with just talk therapy, and five studied special programs for moms. But not many studies looked at how well the babies did.

The studies weren't always done in the best way to make sure they were fair. Some didn't tell us enough about how they picked people for the studies or kept them honest about what was happening. 

They found that moms using talk therapy or special programs didn't have more or less preemies (babies born too early) than those who didn't get these therapies. They also didn't have more problems during birth or babies born smaller. But moms using these therapies stayed in the hospital for shorter times after giving birth.

For the babies, the studies showed that those whose moms got talk therapy or special programs spent fewer days in the hospital after birth. But there wasn't much difference in how well the babies did overall.

The studies weren't very good at looking at how the therapies affected mom's health or whether the babies had long-term problems. So while these therapies might help with some things, we don't know for sure how they affect mom's health or the baby's health over time.

Overall, the evidence isn't strong enough to say these therapies work better than others. More studies are needed to learn more about these treatments and how they can help pregnant women who use drugs.

output: This study looked at 38 research studies involving 1828 people. These studies tested whether taking a certain type of sugar called non-absorbable disaccharides helps prevent a condition called hepatic encephalopathy, which can happen to people with liver problems. The studies found that taking this sugar might help lower the chances of dying, especially when the studies were done fairly (low risk of bias). When all the studies were looked at together, it seemed like taking the sugar helped reduce the risk of death by about 41%, though more studies would be needed to be sure. It also appeared to help with other health issues related to liver problems, like stopping the brain from acting funny and reducing bad things happening to the liver. However, the sugar didn't seem to make much difference in how well people felt or in minor side effects. The researchers think there's good evidence that this sugar might help, but they're not completely sure because some parts of the studies weren't done very well. Overall, these studies suggest that taking this sugar might be helpful for people with liver problems, but more research is needed to confirm this.

This study looked at 13 different groups of people who took a medicine called fibrates. These medicines were given to about 16,000 people in total. Most of these people had heart or blood vessel problems before. The study found that taking fibrates seemed to help prevent some serious health problems like strokes and heart attacks. It also helped lower the chances of dying from heart-related issues. However, fibrates didn't seem to help people live longer overall. 

The study found that fibrates worked better than a sugar pill for preventing heart attacks. But they didn't seem to help with all-cause deaths or strokes. This might be because one type of fibrates called clofibrate was taken off the market because it wasn't safe enough. 

Without using clofibrate, fibrates still helped prevent heart attacks. But the study couldn't be sure if fibrates would work as well in people who have had strokes before or when they're already taking another medicine called statins.

Overall, the evidence suggests that fibrates can be helpful for people who have had heart or blood vessel problems in the past. But more research is needed to see if they work as well in other situations.

This study looked at some research papers to see if certain treatments could help people with chest pain. They found that after starting the treatment, people reported less chest pain for the first three months. They also had more days without chest pain during that time. But after three to twelve months, the treatment didn't seem to work anymore. 

The treatments used in the studies weren't always kept secret from the people getting them, which might have affected the results. Also, it's hard to know if the treatments really helped because some of the studies couldn't be sure they were fair to both groups. 

Overall, the studies showed that these types of treatments might help for a short time, but we need more research to be sure. It seems like talking therapies, especially ones based on thinking differently about problems, might be helpful. Hypnosis might also work. But we don't know for sure yet because the studies had some problems and there weren't many people in each study. More research is needed to find out if these treatments really work over longer periods of time.

This review looked at 42 studies involving 11,399 patients, including some from earlier research done in 2010. Out of those studies, 19 were part of the original review and 23 were new ones. Some studies were removed because they had problems with their data or didn't have enough information. 

The review found that people who got a type of fluid called HES (which stands for Hydroxyethyl Starch) needed dialysis (a treatment to clean blood) more often than those who got other types of fluids. They also found that more people developed kidney failure in the HES group compared to others. 

However, when looking at another way to measure kidney damage (using something called RIFLE criteria), the results were mixed. Sometimes HES seemed to cause more kidney damage, but other times it didn’t. This might be because how much HES is given matters. Giving too much HES could lead to more kidney problems.

Overall, the studies showed that HES increases the risk of needing dialysis and developing kidney failure. But the exact amount of HES that’s safe hasn’t been figured out yet. The researchers think that using HES fluids might be risky in most cases and that other types of fluids should be used instead. More research is needed to find out exactly how much HES is safe to use.
