In this study, researchers looked at 11 studies involving 9,839 people who had moderate to severe COPD. Most of these studies included people who didn't have recent flare-ups of their breathing problems. One big study funded by drug companies included people who did have recent flare-ups, and it had the most participants, making up 37% of all the people studied. Because many of the studies were paid for by drug companies, there might be some bias in the results. 

The studies followed people for between 6 and 52 weeks. When comparing the group taking LAMA plus LABA to the group taking LABA plus ICS, here’s what they found:

- They had fewer flare-ups of breathing problems (about 18% fewer).
- There were about the same number of serious health problems.
- Their breathing improved a little bit, but not enough to notice easily.
- Their lung function improved slightly, which is good.
- They had a lower chance of getting pneumonia.
- Their overall breathing problems got better, especially if they improved by 4 or more points on a special breathing test.

These findings suggest that LAMA plus LABA might be a good choice for treating COPD. However, the evidence isn’t very strong because the studies weren’t perfect. It’s like when you’re trying to guess how many candies are in a jar – the more times you look, the closer you get, but you still might not know exactly right away. This study supports what doctors already thought about using LAMA plus LABA for COPD.

It found that the special device did not seem to help people live longer or shorter than usual. There wasn't enough information to know if it caused more problems.

However, it did find that more people got diagnosed with why they were fainting when they had the special device. This happened in four out of four studies, but the studies weren't exactly the same so we can't be sure it's true every time.

The cost of putting in the special device was a bit higher, but the cost of diagnosing someone without the device was even higher. So, it might be worth considering for some people.

Overall, the study suggests that using the special device to diagnose people who faint isn't better than just doing a regular checkup. More research is needed to see if it helps with things like how people feel and how much it costs.

The studies lasted from 6 weeks to a whole year. Most of the studies followed strict rules to make sure the results were fair.

This research looked at a medicine called latrepirdine to see if it helps people with a memory problem called Alzheimer's disease. They studied 1697 people in total, but only 1243 people had their memory checked and 1034 people had their daily activities checked. Some of the studies weren't done very well, so we can't be sure about all the results.

The medicine seemed to help improve how doctors and caregivers think about the person's condition after 26 weeks. But when they looked at other ways to measure thinking and doing things, like using special tests, they couldn't tell if the medicine helped much or not. The results were a bit unclear because the studies didn't always agree.

The medicine did seem to help with some behaviors, like mood swings, which is good news. But it didn't seem to help with thinking or doing everyday tasks. 

Overall, the evidence isn't very strong, but it doesn't show that the medicine causes more problems than regular medicine. More studies are needed to see if latrepirdine really helps with behavior issues in people with Alzheimer's.

The study looked at how well a medicine called PEP helps prevent HIV after someone gets hurt by a needle that might have HIV. They found that if there was a lot of bleeding or if the person who got hurt was very sick, they were more likely to get HIV. But even when they took the medicine, some people didn't take it properly, and others still got sick.

There weren't many studies done, just one big study and a few smaller ones. This one big study showed that people who got hurt were less likely to take the medicine than those who didn't get hurt. Also, taking the medicine wasn't always easy because some people had bad side effects like feeling sick.

Doctors think that giving people PEP right away after getting hurt might help, but they're not sure because there haven't been big studies to prove it. They know that giving people three medicines together isn't as good as giving them one or two. And they don't know if giving people more than one kind of medicine works better.

Doctors suggest that healthcare workers get special training about the medicine and what to expect. They also tell workers that this medicine doesn't work perfectly and can't stop everyone from getting sick. Because it's hard to do big studies, doctors are looking for ways to learn more about how well PEP works and what might cause problems.

In this study, researchers looked at different ways to give medicine to numb hands, wrists, forearms, and elbows during surgery. They studied 22 different studies with a total of 2193 people who had these surgeries. Most of the studies did a good job, but some parts weren't perfect.

The studies found that giving medicine in more places at once (multiple injections) worked better than just one or two places. This was true whether they used special tools to find the nerves or not. More places gave less chance of the medicine not working well (primary anaesthesia failure), and it also helped keep the hands moving better after the surgery.

They also found that giving medicine in more places at once made the pain from the tourniquet (the thing that squeezes the arm to stop blood flow) go away faster. But there wasn't enough information to know if this made the surgery safer or if it caused more problems.

Overall, the studies show that giving medicine in more places at once works better for keeping hands numb during surgery. But we don't have enough information to say if it makes the surgery safer or causes more problems.

This study looked at 50 studies involving 45,285 people. Most of these studies compared people taking a medicine called statins to those not taking any medicine. Three studies compared two different statin medicines. The studies had some problems, but seven of them were done better and followed strict rules.

In this study, researchers looked at four groups of people who had strokes and were trying to drive again. They trained these people using different methods like driving simulators and exercises to improve their driving skills. However, the studies were small and didn’t all follow the same rules, so the researchers couldn’t combine them into one big study. Most of the studies did a good job to make sure they weren’t biased, but some parts were a bit tricky to know if they were fair.

The studies showed that people who took part in the driving training did better at recognizing road signs than those who didn’t train. But when it came to actually driving on the road, there wasn’t much improvement seen right away or even six months later. The researchers also noticed that some people dropped out of the studies before they were finished, which might have affected the results.

While the training seemed to help with recognizing road signs, the researchers aren’t sure if it helps people drive safely on the road. They don’t have enough information to say if driving training works well for everyone who has had a stroke. Some people did see improvements in their driving skills, but others didn’t. The researchers think that maybe different types of training might work better for different people. Overall, while the training helped with some aspects of driving, it’s not clear if it makes a big difference in helping people drive safely after having a stroke.

A review looked at 11 studies with 855 people to see if a special head move called the Epley maneuver works better when you add something extra. Nine of these studies used the Epley maneuver with extra steps. They found that adding these extra steps did help more people get better. Specifically, 88.7% of people who got the extra steps had their problem go away, compared to 78.2% of those who only did the regular Epley maneuver. This means that about every 10 people who get the extra steps will have their problem go away, which might sound like a small difference but can make a big difference for some people.

The extra steps didn't cause any serious problems, but they did make some people feel a little stiff in their neck or dizzy. Most people don't have these problems though. It's also important to know that the regular Epley maneuver already helps about 80% of people with a common problem called Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV), so adding the extra steps isn't necessary for everyone.

There wasn't enough information to say whether another step or a special vibration on the ear area would help. Both of these other things didn't cause any problems either.

The review suggests that while the extra steps do help a bit, the regular Epley maneuver is still very good at helping most people. So, doctors can talk to their patients about whether the extra steps are worth trying, especially if the patient feels uncomfortable with them. Some people might still get better without the extra steps, and the extra steps don't seem to cause any major problems. More studies are needed to learn more about this.

output: This study looked at giving extra protein in the milk of preterm babies. They studied 204 preterm babies in six research studies. The results showed that babies who got extra protein in their milk grew faster in the hospital. They gained more weight, were taller, and had bigger heads than babies who didn't get extra protein. But there wasn't much difference in how thick their skin folds were. Babies who got extra protein stayed in the hospital a little longer and had slightly higher levels of a substance called blood urea nitrogen. There wasn't enough information to know if this extra protein caused problems like feeding difficulties or a condition called necrotizing enterocolitis. Also, we don't know if it affects how they grow up later or their heart and metabolism. The study couldn't tell us if this extra protein helped or hurt because there weren't many babies in the studies, and the information isn't very strong. We also don't know if this works in places where it's harder to get resources. Future studies should look at different amounts of protein and see if it helps with staying in the hospital longer and if it's safe, and also check if it affects how they grow up and their heart and metabolism.

This study looked at how moms feel about getting vaccines for their kids. They reviewed 38 studies from places where people have lots of money. Most of these studies talked about the MMR vaccine, which helps protect against measles, mumps, and rubella.

Parents wanted more information about vaccines than they were getting. They thought this lack of information made them worried and feel bad about their choices. Parents also said they wanted information that showed both the good parts and the not-so-good parts of vaccines. They wanted this information to be easy to understand and to fit their own situations. 

Parents liked when the information was given close to the time of the shot and at different places, like outside of regular doctor visits. They also thought doctors and nurses were good sources of information. But sometimes, if doctors didn't explain things well or had bad feelings with parents, it could make parents decide not to get shots.

Parents had trouble knowing which information to trust and often found it hard to get unbiased information. Parents who were less sure about vaccines wanted even more information.

The studies showed that giving parents information before their appointments and tailoring it to their needs helped. But none of the studies looked at how to deal with scary news stories or how parents think doctors might not be honest.

Overall, we're pretty sure about these findings. But we need more studies in places where people don't have as much money to learn more. This will help us better understand how to give parents the right information so they can make good choices about vaccines.

A study looked at eight trials to see if getting regular check-ups could help stop breast cancer from being deadly. But when they carefully checked the results, they found that the check-ups didn't seem to make a big difference in reducing deaths from breast cancer. 

Some of the trials showed that the check-ups might actually make things worse. They found that more women had to have their breasts removed, even though this wasn't always necessary. Also, more women got radiation treatments, which can have side effects. 

The researchers think that for every 2000 women who get regular check-ups for 10 years, one woman might live longer because of the check-ups, but 10 other women who didn't need the check-ups might still get their breasts removed or have other treatments that aren't needed. Plus, many women might feel worried and anxious about the check-ups.

To help people understand the risks and benefits better, the researchers wrote a leaflet that explains the information clearly. However, because doctors have gotten better at treating breast cancer and more people know about it now, the check-ups might not work as well as they did in the old studies. New studies also suggest that some women might get extra treatment that isn't really needed. So, it's important for people to talk to their doctor about the pros and cons of getting regular check-ups.

This research looked at four studies that tested whether using a medicine called corticosteroids helps people with a type of eye infection called bacterial keratitis. The studies involved a total of about 600 people. Some of these studies were done before, and others were new ones found recently. All the studies compared people who got the corticosteroid medicine to those who didn't get it. They followed the people for different amounts of time, from a few weeks to a year.

The studies found that neither group had better vision or fewer problems overall. One study found that it took longer for the eye to heal in the group that got the corticosteroid, but another study didn't see this difference. None of the studies found that the corticosteroid caused more problems like high eye pressure.

The studies weren't perfect because some people couldn't be tracked down over time, and not enough people were in each group to really know if the corticosteroid made a big difference. Also, the way they measured things wasn't always the same across all the studies.

Overall, the research doesn't give us strong proof that using corticosteroids helps with bacterial keratitis. It might be because the studies weren't big enough to show a clear difference. So, we don't have enough information to say for sure if corticosteroids work better than not using them.

This study looked at three small groups of people who had a type of broken leg called a distal tibial metaphyseal fracture. These people were split into two groups: one group had their leg fixed with a special nail inside the bone, and the other group had metal plates put on their leg. The study found that overall, there wasn't much difference between the two methods. 

The results showed that using the nail might slightly reduce the need for extra surgeries or physical therapy if something goes wrong, but it's hard to know if this makes a big difference. Also, the nail didn't seem to cause more problems like wounds or bones not healing properly compared to the plates. 

There wasn't enough good information to say which method is definitely better. The study found that both methods work similarly, but the results weren't clear enough to make a strong decision. More studies are needed to learn more about which method might be better for some people.

Overall, the evidence isn't very strong, so we can't be sure if these methods really work. More research is needed to know for sure.

output: This research looked at how doctors ask questions to find out if people get bad side effects from medicine. They compared asking open-ended questions versus using checklists or rating scales. Some studies talked to people directly. Overall, the research found that asking more detailed questions led to finding more bad side effects. But it wasn't always clear if the extra details helped find more serious side effects. One study said that asking people open questions might miss some very serious side effects. Another study found that interviewing people worked better for some very serious side effects. But overall, there wasn't enough information to know exactly how well each method works. The studies had different ways of doing things, so it's hard to compare them. The researchers think that how doctors ask questions can affect what side effects they find. They suggest that future studies should use clearer ways to describe side effects and how they were found. This could help make sure all side effects are caught and shared properly.

This research looked at 15 studies involving 721 people who had pain from different kinds of cancers. All the studies were done on grown-ups, not kids. The studies were mostly done well, but many of them had some problems. Some didn't have enough people in them, and others had trouble keeping track of missing information or when people left the study. Most of the studies gave people either codeine (a medicine) or a mix of codeine and another medicine called paracetamol. Some studies also gave people a pretend medicine to compare it to. Most of the studies gave people just one dose of the medicine, but some gave them medicine for longer periods of time.

The studies showed that codeine or codeine mixed with paracetamol helped people feel less pain than when they took nothing. But the studies weren't perfect, so we're not sure how much better it really is. Some studies said people felt much better, while others said it wasn't much different. Codeine caused some side effects like feeling sick to your stomach, throwing up, and having a hard bowel movement. It also made some people sleepy or dizzy. Not many people stopped taking the medicine, but sometimes the cancer got worse and caused death.

Overall, codeine seems to help with pain, but it might cause some uncomfortable side effects. We don't know if it works as well over a long time or if it's safe for everyone. There isn't much information about how it works or if it helps kids. More studies would be needed to learn more.

In this study, researchers looked at 15 studies involving 561 patients who had braces put on their teeth. These studies came from different places like Europe, India, China, South Korea, and the United States. Most of the patients were teenagers or young adults, but some studies included people up to 54 years old. The studies mostly had equal numbers of boys and girls, but seven studies had more girls than boys.

The researchers compared two ways of putting braces on teeth: one way uses surgery to hold the braces in place (surgical anchorage), and the other way uses regular methods (conventional anchorage). They found that the surgery method helps keep the braces in place better. For every 100 patients, the surgery method helped keep the braces in place about 1.68 millimeters tighter than the regular method. This finding is pretty sure because it's based on many studies, but there was a bit of disagreement among the studies, so we need to be careful about this.

The surgery method didn't make the treatment last any longer than the regular method. But again, the studies weren’t very clear about this.

The studies also didn’t have enough information to tell us if one type of surgery was better than another. And they didn’t find any bad side effects from either method.

Overall, the studies show that using surgery to hold braces in place works better than regular methods, especially when tiny metal pins called mini-screws are used. However, we shouldn’t jump to conclusions because the studies weren’t perfect.

This research looked at how changing the thickness of drinks affects people with dementia. But it didn't find many studies that did this. Two main studies were done, both part of the same big study. They looked at whether thicker drinks, like very thick honey or less thick nectar, help people swallow better. One study watched people right away, and another followed them for three months. 

The first study found that thinner drinks helped people swallow better right away, but they had more problems later. The second study found that people who drank very thick drinks had more lung infections over time. But neither study found that drinking thicker drinks caused people to die.

Both studies had some problems being fair to all the people in them. So we don't know for sure if making drinks thicker helps or hurts people with dementia. It might depend on how thick the drink is and how the study tried different drinks. Doctors need to think carefully before recommending thicker drinks. More studies are needed to learn more about this.

In a study looking at different blood pressure goals, researchers found that trying to keep blood pressure very low (less than 120 mmHg) didn't seem to help much overall. They looked at 7314 people and followed them for about 4 and a half years. One group tried to keep their blood pressure lower, but they had to take more medicine to do so. This group had a slightly lower chance of having a stroke, which is good. But when it came to living longer, there wasn't a clear answer - some studies said it might be better, others said it might be worse. Also, trying to keep blood pressure very low seemed to cause more serious health problems like kidney damage. 

For people with diabetes, another study looked at whether keeping blood pressure lower (less than 80 mmHg) was better than the usual goal (less than 90 mmHg). Again, there wasn't a clear answer. Some studies said it might be better, but others said it might not make a difference. The studies also showed that trying to keep blood pressure very low could lead to more serious health issues.

Overall, the current research doesn't strongly support aiming for very low blood pressure goals for most people with high blood pressure and diabetes. More studies are needed to find out if very low blood pressure goals are really better. These studies should look at things like how many people live longer and how many have serious health problems.

This study looked at 12 trials involving 3285 healthy women who did not have a high risk of heavy bleeding after giving birth. These women had either a planned cesarean section (C-section) or gave birth naturally. All the women got medicine to help stop bleeding, which is what doctors usually do. The studies were mostly done well, but some parts might have been a little biased.

The results showed that women who got a special medicine called TA (which stands for something) lost less blood compared to those who didn't get it. Specifically, they lost less than 400 mL, 500 mL, or 1000 mL of blood. This happened whether the women had a C-section or gave birth naturally. Women who had a C-section lost less blood overall when they got TA.

TA helped reduce the amount of blood lost by about 77.79 mL, which is a lot less than if they didn't get it. It also made it less likely that they would need extra blood or other treatments. However, some women did feel sick sometimes, like having a stomach ache or feeling dizzy.

While TA seemed to help with bleeding, we're not sure if it affects things like death or very serious health problems. We just don't know enough yet. But we do know that TA helps prevent heavy bleeding after birth, especially for women who are not at high risk of it. More research is needed to see if it has any serious side effects or if it works better for women who are at higher risk.

This study looked at how well a medicine called cerivastatin works to lower bad cholesterol in people. They gave it in different amounts to 12,877 people, most of whom already had high cholesterol or heart problems. After taking the medicine for 3 to 12 weeks, they saw that it helped lower bad cholesterol by 11% to 40%, total cholesterol by 8% to 28%, and triglycerides by 9% to 21%. The doctors think this information is very reliable.

The study found that the more cerivastatin you take, the more it lowers these types of cholesterol. It was much better at lowering cholesterol than other medicines like fluvastatin, atorvastatin, and rosuvastatin. However, cerivastatin didn't seem to help raise good cholesterol (HDL).

Some people got sick while taking the medicine, but not more often than when they took a sugar pill instead. The medicine worked best when taken in higher doses, and its effects were consistent across the doses tested.

While the study showed that cerivastatin was very effective at lowering cholesterol, it wasn't able to tell us how common side effects might be because the studies were short and some didn't report all the side effects.

This research looked at 10 studies involving 1015 people to see if adding special nutrients called omega-3 fatty acids and antioxidants to a feeding formula could help people who have a lung problem called ARDS. The studies were mixed and didn't always follow the same rules, so it's hard to be sure about their results. 

For the main goal, which was to see if these nutrients helped people live longer, the studies didn't show a clear answer. Some said yes, some said no, and others said it might not make much difference. This means we're not very sure about this part.

However, when it comes to other goals like making people stay in the ICU or on a breathing machine for shorter times, or helping them breathe better, the studies weren't clear either. There wasn't enough good information to say for sure if these nutrients helped or not.

The researchers also weren't very sure about whether these nutrients caused more problems like heart or stomach issues. They think there might be a small chance that these nutrients could cause more of these problems, but it's not clear.

In summary, while these nutrients might not help people live longer, we don't know for sure if they help with staying in the hospital or breathing better. More research would be needed to find out.

This research looked at two types of airway tools used to help people breathe after surgery. They studied 829 people who got one of these tools. Some studies didn't have enough information to tell if the tools worked differently. 

The main thing they found was that it took longer to get the tool in place when using the ProSeal Laryngeal Mask Airway (pLMA). But the Classic Laryngeal Mask Airway (cLMA) let doctors put the tool in faster. 

Using the pLMA also made it harder for air to escape through the mouth, which might be good for keeping air pressure steady. But the cLMA had less air escaping, which could mean it's easier to use.

Overall, the studies weren't very clear about whether the tools work better. There weren't many cases where the tools failed to work properly. So we can't say for sure if one tool is better than the other. But the pLMA seems to make a better seal, which might be helpful. The cLMA might be easier to put in, but that might not matter much in real life.

output: In a study looking at different ways to help people with anorexia nervosa, researchers looked at 10 trials with 599 people who had the illness. They found that some types of talk therapy seemed to work better than usual care given by doctors who don’t specialize in eating disorders. One type of therapy called focal psychodynamic therapy helped more people get better than usual care. But another type of therapy called cognitive analytic therapy didn’t seem to help more people get better. The studies weren’t perfect because they couldn’t always tell if the treatments really worked or if people dropped out of the studies. Also, many of the studies had too few people to give clear answers. Overall, the evidence isn’t strong enough to say which type of therapy works best. More studies with bigger groups over longer periods would be helpful to know better.

output: This research looked at seven studies involving a total of 406 people. Some of these people had leg cramps during pregnancy, and others had cramps that happened for no clear reason. The studies compared taking magnesium to not taking it. For people with cramps that happen for no clear reason, which often affect older adults, there wasn't much difference between taking magnesium and not taking it. The studies didn't show that magnesium helps reduce the number of cramps or make them less intense. There wasn't enough information to know if magnesium helps with pregnancy-related leg cramps. The studies weren't able to tell us if magnesium causes any problems. Overall, the evidence suggests that magnesium might not help prevent cramps in older adults. However, more research is needed to see if it helps with cramps during pregnancy. There's not enough information about using magnesium for other types of cramps. More studies are needed to learn more about magnesium and cramps.

A study looked at whether taking a medicine called prednisone helps people with a condition better than just not taking any medicine. But this study didn't measure the main thing they wanted to see. It had some problems being fair, so we're not sure how good the results are.

In another study, doctors gave two different types of prednisone to 40 people over a year. One group got a higher dose once every month, while the other got a lower dose every day. They didn't find much difference between the two groups in terms of getting better or feeling better after a year. Some people in both groups got worse, though.

The study that gave monthly high-dose prednisone didn't have many side effects, except that fewer people had trouble sleeping. Also, fewer people got a moon-like look on their face. But the study wasn't big enough to be very sure about these differences.

Overall, we're not very confident about whether prednisone works better than nothing. But doctors often use it anyway because there's some evidence it might help. Long-term use of prednisone can cause serious health problems.

For high-dose monthly prednisone, the study showed it might work about the same as daily prednisolone, but it might cause fewer side effects like moon face and trouble sleeping. More research is needed to figure out who will do best with which type.

This review looked at different ways to help people keep their teeth healthy. It checked 19 studies with 4232 people who took part. The studies tried many different things like one-on-one visits with a dentist or using special toothpaste. They looked at how well these helped with things like having red gums, having less sticky stuff on teeth called plaque, and getting cavities.

For one type of visit where a person works with a dentist, there wasn't much clear proof that it helps. Some studies said it might help a little bit, but others didn't find any difference. For another type of visit where a person does things themselves, there wasn't enough good proof either. And for visits where a person gets extra help, there wasn't enough good proof to know if they work better.

Overall, we don't have strong enough proof to say which way of helping people keep their teeth healthy is best. More studies need to be done to figure out the best way. These new studies should be careful to use the lessons learned from this review.

This study looked at eight trials involving 291 people, mostly teenagers and young adults, who had cystic fibrosis (CF). The trials compared a regular amount of a medicine called rhGH to no medicine at all. In one trial, they also compared a normal dose of rhGH to a higher dose. The studies lasted from 6 months to a whole year.

The results showed that rhGH helped make people taller and heavier, but didn't make them gain more weight or muscle. It also seemed to help with breathing problems, but only a little bit. The medicine didn't cause diabetes, but it might slightly lower blood sugar levels. 

There wasn't much information about how the medicine affected how people felt or if it caused other health issues. The studies were too short to tell if the benefits would last longer. Also, we don't know if the medicine costs more than not taking it. 

Overall, rhGH seems to be helpful for making people taller and heavier, but it doesn't seem to help with breathing problems or make people feel better. More long-term studies are needed before doctors can decide if rhGH should be used routinely for CF.

The balloons had medicine called paclitaxel on them. Two of the three trials were paid for by companies that make these balloons. The trials checked if the special balloons helped more than regular balloons. They looked at whether the arteries stayed open and if people got better over time. The results showed that the special balloons didn't cause more people to need their leg cut off. But they did seem to keep the arteries open better for up to 2 years. However, the information isn't very strong because there weren't many people in the studies and some things about the way the studies were done might have made the results less reliable. More studies are needed to know for sure if these special balloons really work better.

This study looked at whether adding zinc to common foods could help people who don't get enough zinc. They checked eight different studies, all done in places where many people don’t have enough zinc in their bodies. In some studies, they gave people foods with extra zinc and compared them to people eating the same foods without extra zinc. 

The studies found that people who ate foods with extra zinc had higher levels of zinc in their blood compared to those who didn’t eat the zinc-rich foods. But, there wasn’t much difference in how much people weighed or how well they grew. One study showed that adding zinc to wheat flour didn’t help reduce zinc problems. 

When zinc was added to foods along with other important vitamins and minerals, it didn’t seem to change zinc levels in the blood. Adding zinc to foods didn’t cause any bad effects on other things like iron or copper levels. 

While adding zinc to foods might help raise zinc levels in people, we don’t know if it helps with zinc problems, makes kids grow better, or helps grown-ups do their jobs better. More studies are needed to find out.

This research looked at different ways to help people who had breast cancer feel better mentally and keep their minds sharp. They studied five groups of people who took part in different types of training or activities. But all the studies had some problems, so we can't be totally sure of the results.

The training that used computers to help think faster and remember things worked well. People who did this training felt their thinking skills improved both when measured by doctors and how they felt themselves. 

Another type of training that helps people find ways to do things even if they're having trouble remembering or thinking clearly also helped. This made it easier for people to remember things and feel better about their thoughts.

However, another type of training called meditation didn't seem to help with feeling better physically right away. In fact, some people who meditated felt worse right after the training. And the training that involved doing more exercise didn't seem to help with physical well-being either.

Overall, the evidence isn't very strong because the studies weren't perfect, but it does suggest that these kinds of training might help people with breast cancer feel better mentally and keep their minds sharp. More studies are needed to be really sure, especially ones that compare these treatments to other ways of helping. They studied five groups of people who took part in different types of training or activities. But all the studies had some problems, so we can't be totally sure of the results.

The training that used computers to help think faster and remember things worked well. People who did this training felt their thinking skills improved both when measured by doctors and how they felt themselves. 

Another type of training that helps people find ways to do things even if they're having trouble remembering or thinking clearly also helped. This made it easier for people to remember things and feel better about their thoughts.

More studies are needed to be really sure, especially ones that compare these treatments to other ways of helping. We also need to look at how these treatments affect everyday activities and other types of cancer too.

This research looked at three small studies to see if taking more of a medicine called stavudine helped people better. These studies were done in places where people have good healthcare. They found that taking more of this medicine didn't seem to help people's sicknesses get better any faster. However, some people who took more of the medicine had higher levels of a chemical called lactate in their blood, which can happen even when the sickness isn't getting worse. The studies also showed that taking more of this medicine might make bones weaker and cause people to gain more belly fat. But it didn't seem to cause people to stop taking the medicine because of bad side effects.

The studies were a bit tricky to compare because they weren't exactly alike. Also, most of the people in the studies already had their sickness under control before starting the study. So we can't really tell if taking more of this medicine would work better for people who haven't started taking medicine for their sickness yet.

Because of these issues, doctors think it might be a good idea to do more studies in places where people don't have access to good medicine yet. This could help figure out if taking less of this medicine might be safer and still work well for people who haven't started taking medicine for their sickness.

This review looked at six studies involving 2411 people who had seizures. Most of the studies only looked at people whose seizures started in one part of their brain, but one study included people whose seizures started in different parts too. All the studies were done with adults aged 16 to 80, and they lasted from 7 to 16 weeks.

Two studies were judged to be very good at making sure the results are reliable, while the other four were less clear about this. Some studies didn't tell us exactly how they kept the treatment secret from the people taking it, and some didn't mention all the things they planned to look at before the studies started.

People who got a medicine called brivaracetam along with their usual treatment had more seizures go away by half or more compared to those who just took a sugar pill (placebo). They were also more likely to stop having seizures completely. But people taking the brivaracetam were slightly more likely to stop taking the medicine because of side effects compared to those taking the placebo. 

Brivaracetam helps reduce seizures and can help people stop having them completely. But it makes people want to stop taking the medicine more often because of side effects. This medicine works best for adults with seizures that don't get better with other medicines. More studies are needed to see if it works as well over a longer time and if it helps people of other ages or with different types of seizures.

output: This review looked at fourteen studies about a medicine called dexamethasone. These studies mostly compared different amounts of the medicine given to babies born very early. Some studies found that giving more of the medicine might make it harder for these babies to have a good brain development later. Other studies didn't find much difference when they gave different amounts of the medicine. But there wasn't enough information to know for sure which amount works best. Also, many of the studies had small numbers of babies, so we can't be completely confident in the results. Because of this, doctors can't give clear advice on the best way to use this medicine to help prevent a condition called BPD in very young babies. More research is needed to figure out the best way to use this medicine safely and effectively.

This study looked at two different treatments for a condition called CRVO-ME, which affects the eye. It involved 708 people who had this condition. One study used a medicine called triamcinolone, while the other used something called dexamethasone. Both studies had some problems though. In the triamcinolone study, about 10% of people didn't finish the study, and in the dexamethasone study, around 17% didn't finish. Also, the dexamethasone study only looked at people with both types of blocked veins, not just the type that causes CRVO-ME.

The triamcinolone study showed that people who got the medicine had better vision after eight months. But the study also said that the medicine caused people's vision to get worse over time. The dexamethasone study didn't show that the medicine helped vision either. Both studies had problems like not having enough information or not telling us everything that happened to the people in the study.

Because of these problems, we don't know if the medicine helps or not. The studies weren't very good at showing whether the medicine works or not. There wasn't enough information to be sure about the results. The medicine caused more side effects, like making the eye pressure go up or causing the lens to get cloudy.

So, we don't have enough good information to say if the medicine helps or not. More studies would be needed to find out.

This study looked at ways to help people who have trouble controlling their bladder or bowels, especially when they're in a nursing home or hospital. They tried different creams and special washing methods. But the studies weren't perfect because they had too few people or didn't last long enough. 

Two out of nine studies showed that a special cream might work better than just using soap and water. Another study said a special washing method might work better than just using soap and water. Other studies suggested that putting on creams or lotions might work better than not putting them on. But none of the studies told us if people liked the treatments or if there were any bad side effects.

Overall, there's not much good information about what works best. Soap and water don't seem to help much. Putting on creams or lotions does seem to help more than not putting them on. But the creams need to be the right kind and used the right way.

More studies are needed to confirm these findings and make sure they work everywhere. Also, it would be helpful to have everyone use the same kinds of creams and follow the same steps when washing. This will make it easier to compare the results from different studies. The information we have is based on studies done up to September 28, 2016.

This study looked at twelve trials to see if a medicine called IVIg works better than another medicine called plasma exchange (PE) for people who have a very serious illness. In five trials where we could compare the results, there wasn't enough difference to say which medicine worked better. But in three smaller trials with children, IVIg seemed to help them get better faster than just being taken care of. One trial with 21 children showed that IVIg helped them get better faster than just being watched closely. Another trial with 249 people found that combining IVIg with PE didn’t seem to give extra benefits. IVIg was also easier to give completely than PE. 

The study also found that IVIg helps children recover faster than just being taken care of, but it’s not clear if it helps adults. For children, IVIg seems to help them get better faster than just being watched, but we need more research to know for sure. We also need to find out if giving IVIg before or after PE makes a difference. More research is needed to learn about how to use IVIg safely and effectively in different situations.

This research looked at different tests used to find a type of malaria called P. falciparum. They found 74 studies that were important for their review. These studies tested for different parts of the malaria parasite, which they called HRP-2 and pLDH.

When these tests were compared to looking at blood under a microscope, which is considered the best way to diagnose malaria, the tests worked pretty well. For tests that look for HRP-2, they found that these tests correctly identified about 95 out of every 100 infected people (that's very good), but sometimes they might say someone has malaria when they don't (false positives), happening about 5 out of every 100 times. For tests that look for pLDH, they found that these tests correctly identified about 98 out of every 100 infected people (also very good), but they almost never said someone has malaria when they don't (very few false positives).

Overall, the tests that look for HRP-2 were a bit better at finding malaria, but they also had a higher chance of saying someone has malaria when they don't. The tests that look for pLDH were better at not saying someone has malaria when they don't, but they weren't quite as good at finding malaria.

These tests are very helpful because they can be used instead of or along with looking at blood under a microscope to find malaria. However, the HRP-2 tests might work a little better, but they're not as good at making sure they're right all the time. The HRP-2 part of the malaria parasite doesn't go away even after it's treated, so these tests can't tell if the treatment worked.

This study looked at 15 different groups of people who had a stuffy nose and sinus problems. In all, 3057 people took part in these studies. The researchers found that without taking antibiotics, about half of the people got better after one week and three-quarters got better after two weeks. But antibiotics helped even more people get better faster, about 5 out of every 100 people. This means that more people would get better quickly if they took antibiotics instead of nothing, but it also meant that more people might have some side effects like feeling sick.

The study found that antibiotics worked best when doctors could see fluid or blockages in the sinuses using a special X-ray called CT scan. They also helped pus go away faster. However, more people had side effects from the antibiotics than from not taking them.

The study showed that while antibiotics might help make people feel better faster, they also made more people have other side effects. There was just one case where someone got a serious problem from the antibiotics, which happened in one person out of 3057 who took them.

Overall, the study suggests that antibiotics don't seem to be very helpful for most people with a stuffy nose and sinus problems. The benefits aren't big enough to outweigh the risks of side effects. Also, the study didn't look at children, people with weak immune systems, or people with very bad sinus problems. So, for most people, doctors probably won't prescribe antibiotics for their stuffy nose and sinus problems.

output: This research looked at 24,704 medical papers to find out about treatments for kids with certain health conditions called cerebral palsy (CP) and osteogenesis imperfecta (OI). They found nine studies with 379 children in total. The studies looked at different medicines to help with pain, like a medicine called intrathecal baclofen (ITB) and another called botulinum toxin A (BoNT-A). For CP, both ITB studies showed that the medicine helped reduce pain compared to regular care. But for OI, the studies didn't show much difference in pain relief. Most of the side effects were from the way the medicine was given, not the medicine itself. One study had some serious side effects, but it wasn't clear if they happened because of the treatment. The studies weren't very big, so we don't know for sure if these medicines work well for all kids. More studies with bigger groups of kids would be needed to learn more about which medicines might help with pain better. Right now, we don't have enough good information to say for sure which medicines work best.

This research looked at four studies that compared a treatment called G-CSF plus plerixafor to G-CSF plus a placebo. But two of the studies stopped early because they couldn't find enough people to join. The other two studies had 600 people each who had either a type of blood cancer called multiple myeloma or another type called non-Hodgkin lymphoma.

In both groups, the treatment didn't seem to make people live longer after 12 months. But when it came to getting stem cells ready for a transplant, the group that got plerixafor seemed to do better. They were more likely to get the stem cells they needed. This happened in both types of blood cancers studied.

The studies also found that the group that got plerixafor had fewer problems getting ready for the transplant. But this wasn't true for all the problems they looked at.

The studies showed that using plerixafor might help more people get their stem cells ready faster. But the studies weren't big enough to tell if it helps people live longer or if it causes more problems. Some other studies that didn't finish were done by the same company that makes plerixafor. These studies haven't been shared yet, so we don't know if they would show different results. This means there might be some information missing that could affect what we think about plerixafor.

output: This research looked at different ways to check on asthma, either in person or over the phone. Six studies with a total of 2100 people were studied. Some people had their asthma checked in person, while others had it checked over the phone. The studies showed that about 21 out of every 1000 people who had their asthma checked in person had an asthma attack that needed medicine, compared to about 36 out of every 1000 people who had their asthma checked over the phone. But since the numbers were so small, it's hard to tell if one way is better than the other. The studies also found that people didn't have more asthma attacks when they had their check-ups over the phone. The research couldn't say for sure if checking asthma over the phone was safer than seeing a doctor in person. Some studies showed that more people got checked over the phone, but it wasn't clear if this helped them with their asthma. Overall, the research suggests that there isn't much difference between having a check-up in person or over the phone for asthma. More research is needed to know for sure.

A study looked at two medicines called clioquinol and PBT2 to see if they help people with Alzheimer’s disease. For clioquinol, they gave it to 36 people and compared it to a sugar pill. After 36 weeks, the medicine didn’t seem to make their thinking better than the sugar pill. Some people did have problems with their eyesight while taking the medicine, but these went away when they stopped taking it. 

For PBT2, they gave it to 78 people with early Alzheimer’s disease. They found that PBT2 helped with some thinking skills like remembering things and doing puzzles. But it didn’t improve other thinking skills or memory. Also, PBT2 seemed safe to take. 

The researchers think PBT2 might help people with Alzheimer’s, but they need to do bigger studies to know for sure. They’re worried that the first study wasn’t done very well, so they’re not sure if clioquinol helps. They also stopped testing clioquinol because the results weren’t clear. The study of PBT2 showed it was safe, but more research is needed to show if it really works to help people with Alzheimer’s.

In a study looking at different birth control methods and their effects on breastfeeding and baby growth, researchers looked at 11 trials. These trials included 1482 women who used various types of birth control. Some of these trials were done a long time ago, before 1985, and some more recently, from 2005 to 2014.

The studies didn't always give clear numbers about how much breastfeeding or milk production changed. But some older studies suggested that birth control pills might make it harder for women to breastfeed. One study found that women using a type of birth control called a COC had shorter breastfeeding periods than those who didn't use any birth control. Another study found that women using a different kind of birth control called an LNG-IUS had fewer babies breastfeeding at 75 days, but this wasn't true for all babies.

For breast milk volume, some older studies said there was less milk for women using birth control pills compared to those not using any. However, other studies didn't find a difference in milk volume.

This research looked at different ways to help people recover better after they break their hips, especially if they have problems remembering things. They studied seven groups of people, each group had about 79 people. Some groups got extra help right after they left the hospital, while others got it both in the hospital and at home. Another group got special help from doctors who know a lot about older people's health instead of regular doctors.

The researchers didn't find strong proof that any of these extra help methods work better than normal care. They weren't sure because the studies weren't perfect and some people in the groups started out differently. The studies were too small to tell us for sure if the extra help made a big difference.

They did find that people who got extra help in the hospital might have fewer problems called "delirium" which is when you get confused. They also found that people who got extra help from geriatricians (special doctors for older people) might spend less time in the hospital. But again, the proof isn't very strong.

Overall, the evidence isn't very good. It's like trying to guess what color shirt someone is wearing when you can only see them through a foggy window. More research is needed to figure out the best ways to help people with hip fractures who have memory problems.

output: This study looked at 72 different experiments involving 2470 people. These studies added 35 new ones to the old ones. The experiments had some problems because it wasn't always clear if the treatments worked better. The main finding was that virtual reality didn't seem to help with moving your arms better, but it did help with doing everyday tasks like getting dressed or eating. When people got extra virtual reality sessions as part of their regular care, they did better at these tasks. But it didn't help them walk faster or stay balanced. There weren't enough studies to know if it helped with thinking or feeling better. Most of the time, the virtual reality didn't work better than normal care. Some people might have had a little trouble, but it wasn't serious. The study suggests that using virtual reality might help if you get more time with it as part of your treatment. It also seems that custom-made virtual reality games might work better than store-bought ones. But we need more studies to be sure.

This study looked at 28 studies that involved 6851 patients to see if a treatment called remote ischaemic preconditioning helped reduce something called serum creatinine levels after surgery. Most of these studies seemed to be done fairly well, but it's not completely clear how reliable the results are. The treatment didn't seem to make much difference in lowering creatinine levels on days one, two, and three after surgery. However, there was a small chance that it might cause more serious problems, though not enough studies showed this clearly. 

The treatment did not seem to increase the need for dialysis, shorten the time someone stays in the hospital, or increase the chances of dying. It also didn't seem to affect the chance of getting a condition called acute kidney injury, but it might slightly lower the chance of it. 

Overall, the treatment doesn't appear to cause many problems, but it seems to help a little bit in preventing some damage to the kidneys. But the evidence isn't strong enough to say for sure that it works better than other treatments. So while it looks like it might be helpful, we can't be very confident about that yet.

This study looked at 7 different trials involving 922 people who had a condition called Kawasaki Disease. The trials lasted from 32 to 242 days. The results show that using medicines called corticosteroids helped reduce problems like narrowed arteries in the heart (called coronary artery abnormalities), fever, and the time it took for blood tests to show things were getting better. It also helped people stay in the hospital for fewer days.

The medicine didn't cause any serious bad side effects or deaths. Some groups of people might get more help from the medicine, but we need more studies to know for sure. The information we have is good enough to think that using these medicines helps, but we're not completely certain about everything. 

Overall, the medicine seems to help by reducing heart problems, shortening how long people stay in the hospital, and making their symptoms go away faster. But we don't know if it will help everyone or if it will cause other problems later on. So doctors suggest using these medicines for all kids with Kawasaki Disease until we learn more from future studies.

This study looked at a special kind of treatment called Mobilization and Breathing Exercises (MBR) for people who have back pain that started recently. They checked if MBR helps more than just regular care. They studied nine groups of people in different parts of the world, and each group had about 30 to 350 people. The people in the study were mostly young adults, around 32 to 43 years old.

The study found that people who got MBR had less pain and were able to go back to work faster. They also had fewer days off work. But, the study wasn't perfect because some things might have made the results not as reliable. For example, the people giving the treatment or the people getting it might have known which group they were in, which could have affected the results.

When comparing MBR to other treatments, the study didn't find much difference. It's like saying MBR might be a bit better, but we're not sure because the studies weren't very good quality.

Overall, MBR seems to help people with recent back pain feel better and get back to work faster. But we need more good studies to know for sure if it works better than other treatments. More research is needed to make sure MBR is really helpful for everyone.

This study looked at 17 different studies involving 1639 people who have kidney problems. Some studies focused on people who need special machines to help them filter their blood, while others looked at people who got new kidneys. The studies also looked at different ways of eating, like eating less meat or more fruits and vegetables.

The studies weren't perfect because some parts weren't clear, so we're not sure if the changes in eating really helped. But overall, it seems that changing what you eat might help a little bit. For example, it might help one out of every 3000 people avoid needing a special machine to clean their blood for a year. It also helps keep your blood pressure down and makes your kidneys work better. Eating a special kind of food called a Mediterranean diet might even help lower your bad cholesterol.

While we're not completely sure if eating differently will help everyone, it does seem to make your health feel better and your kidneys work better. More big studies are needed to be really sure about whether eating differently helps people with kidney problems live longer or have fewer health problems.

This research looked at three different medicines—human albumin, HES, and mannitol—to see if they could help prevent a condition called OHSS, which can happen to women who are pregnant. They studied 1867 women who were at high risk of OHSS. 

The results showed that human albumin seemed to help prevent OHSS. If a woman didn't get any treatment, she might have a 12% chance of having OHSS. But if she got human albumin, her chance would be about 9%. However, using human albumin also made it less likely that she would get pregnant. If she had a 40% chance of getting pregnant without any treatment, her chance would drop to about 32%.

HES (another medicine) also seemed to help prevent OHSS. If a woman didn't get any treatment, she might have a 16% chance of having OHSS. But if she got HES, her chance would be about 5%. HES did not seem to affect her chances of getting pregnant.

Mannitol, another medicine, also helped prevent OHSS. If a woman didn't get any treatment, she might have a 52% chance of having OHSS. But if she got mannitol, her chance would be about 29%. Mannitol did not seem to affect her chances of getting pregnant either.

Overall, these medicines seemed to help prevent OHSS, but they might make it harder for a woman to get pregnant. More studies are needed to confirm these findings and to see if these medicines should be used routinely in hospitals. The studies weren't perfect, so we can't be completely sure about everything. But the medicines do seem to help prevent OHSS.

These people were split into two groups - one group got a treatment called TACE followed by another treatment called 3-DCRT, and the other group just got TACE. The study found that after about a year, the group that got both treatments seemed to live longer and their tumours responded better to treatment. But there were some side effects like higher levels of a chemical called bilirubin, which can make someone feel sick. The study wasn't perfect, so we're not sure how well the treatment works overall. More studies are needed to confirm these findings.

output: This study looked at 84 different experiments involving 22,872 people to see if a type of help called MI (which stands for Motivational Interviewing) helps reduce how much alcohol someone drinks. Most of these experiments lasted at least four months to see if the help works over time. The researchers think the evidence is good enough to be considered moderate or low quality. They found that MI might help people drink less alcohol, have fewer days when they drink, and have lower levels of alcohol in their blood after four months. However, it didn't seem to help with things like having more than three drinks in one sitting or driving while drunk. There wasn't enough evidence to show that MI helps with other bad behaviors related to drinking. The studies didn't find any harmful side effects from MI. While some of the results showed a little bit of improvement, the changes were so small that they probably wouldn't make much difference in real life. So, based on this information, it seems that MI doesn't provide meaningful benefits for reducing alcohol use, misuse, or problems related to drinking.

A small study found that a medicine called pegloticase helped get rid of lumps called tophi in some people with a condition called gout. The study had very good methods to make sure it was reliable. 

The study looked at three ways to give the medicine: every two weeks, every month, or not at all. They found that giving the medicine every two weeks worked better at getting rid of the lumps, but it also made more people stop taking the medicine because of side effects. Giving the medicine every month was less effective at getting rid of the lumps, but it caused fewer side effects.

Most people who took the medicine had less pain and felt better overall. But when they gave the medicine every two weeks, more people stopped taking it because of problems like feeling sick during the injection. When they gave it every month, even more people stopped because of similar issues.

The study suggests that the medicine might help get rid of the lumps, but it comes with a lot of side effects, especially from the injections. More studies are needed to look at other ways to treat these lumps, like surgery.

output: This study looked at whether giving more oxygen during surgery helps or hurts patients. They checked 28 studies with 9330 people to see if it made a difference. In most of these studies, the results weren't clear and might have been affected by small problems in how the studies were done. The studies didn't find that giving more oxygen changed how many people died after surgery or how many had problems like infections. However, they did find that in some studies, giving more oxygen seemed to lower the chance of getting an infection at the cut made during surgery. But the evidence wasn't strong enough to say for sure that giving more oxygen is better. Because there are risks involved with giving too much oxygen, and because the studies aren't perfect, we don't know if giving more oxygen is helpful or harmful. More studies need to be done to figure this out, especially ones that are done correctly and have lots of people in them.

output:
This review looked at eleven studies involving 886 people who had wounds that took a long time to heal. The studies were not all very big, and sometimes didn’t give enough information to know if the treatments worked. 

Some studies compared different types of iodine to see if they helped wounds heal faster. They found no clear evidence that iodine helped. Other studies compared zinc oxide dressings to regular dressings. These showed that wounds treated with zinc oxide healed a little faster, but the evidence wasn’t very strong.

One study found that a special cream called sucralfate helped wounds from hemorrhoids heal faster than another cream. This was a bit better than other creams, but the evidence wasn’t very strong. Another study found that using a special liquid called Triclosan after surgery helped wounds heal faster too.

A third study found that using honey-soaked gauze to cover wounds from a type of muscle infection called pyomyositis helped them heal faster. It also made people stay in the hospital less time. But again, the evidence wasn’t very strong.

There was also some evidence that wounds in people with diabetes healed faster when treated with a product called Dermacym. But like before, the evidence wasn’t very strong.

Overall, there isn’t much good evidence about which treatments work best for wounds that take a long time to heal. Most of the studies were small and the evidence was not very strong. More research might help us understand better.

- They drank less alcohol each week.
- They drank less often.
- There was also a small drop in how much alcohol their bodies had after drinking.

The researchers think the small changes might not be important enough to change policies or how colleges handle drinking. This review looked at seven studies involving 696 people to see if taking special medicines called progestogens helps prevent miscarriages. The studies came from different parts of the world, including rich countries like Germany and Italy, and poorer countries like Jordan. Most of the studies had good methods, but some had flaws that made it hard to be completely sure about the results.

The studies showed that taking progestogens probably lowers the chance of having a miscarriage. This happened whether the medicine was taken by mouth or put into the vagina. But taking vaginal progestogens didn't seem to help much more than taking nothing at all.

Progestogens also seemed to slightly lower the chance of having a baby too early, but the evidence for this wasn't very strong. It's not clear if these medicines affect babies born with problems, but the evidence for this isn't very good either.

In general, the review suggests that progestogens might help prevent miscarriages, but they don't seem to make a big difference in preventing babies from being born too soon or having problems after birth. More research would be needed to know for sure.

This study looked at three research studies that tested different ways to help people with inflammatory arthritis keep their jobs. These studies involved 414 people who might lose their jobs because of their condition. Most of the people studied had rheumatoid arthritis, which is a type of arthritis that causes joint pain and swelling. The studies tried to help people keep their jobs by making changes at work or giving them advice and support. Some studies visited workplaces to help, while others just gave advice or education.

The studies had different ways of doing things, and some might not have been done fairly. But the biggest study found that people were less likely to lose their jobs. It's like if you had a lemonade stand, and the study said that lemonade stands lasted longer when someone came to check on them regularly. The other study didn't find a clear difference, but it could be that the results weren't strong enough to see clearly.

One study also looked at how long people stayed home sick from work. It found that people took about 2.42 fewer days off work after getting help. Another study found that people's ability to work improved a little bit after getting help, but the improvement wasn't very big.

None of the studies found that helping people at work caused any problems. The researchers think that these kinds of help might work, but they're not sure because the studies weren't perfect. They need more studies to be really sure.

Overall, this review suggests that helping people with inflammatory arthritis keep their jobs might work, but we need more good studies to know for sure.

More studies would help us know if these ideas work well in everyday life.

output: This study looked at 17 important studies that involved babies born too soon or just a little later. These babies had trouble breathing and weren't getting enough oxygen. Some of these studies gave the babies a special gas called iNO, while others didn't. The studies showed that giving iNO helped the babies breathe better and lowered the chance they would need a machine to help them breathe. It also helped them keep more oxygen in their blood. However, it didn't change how many babies died. About half of the babies who got iNO had clearer lungs. But some studies found that giving iNO to babies who weren't very sick didn't help them get better faster. Giving iNO early seemed to work well, but it didn't make the babies healthier overall. The studies also found that babies who got iNO didn't have different chances of being disabled or having hearing problems later. Overall, the evidence suggests that giving iNO to babies who aren't very sick helps them breathe better, but it doesn't seem to make them healthier in other ways.

This research looked at two studies with a total of 181 people who had different ways to get into their body to do a procedure. In one study, there weren't enough details about how they picked who got which way, so we're not sure if it was done fairly. The other study had more people and followed better rules, making its results more reliable.

Both studies didn't find any extra deaths in either group. They also didn't find any big problems like holes in blood vessels being left behind. There were no infections around the wounds in either group. Neither group had more major problems or bleeding.

The studies didn't look at what happened after six months, but they did find that the percutaneous (through the skin) way took less time to do the procedure. However, the results for some things weren't very clear because there weren't many people in the studies, so we can't be completely sure about those findings.

Overall, the evidence suggests that the two methods are about the same for short-term results. But the results for operating time are clearer and show that the percutaneous method takes less time. Because there aren't many studies, we need more research to be really sure about everything.

There's a new study starting soon that might give us even better information.

This research looked at ways to help people with brain problems called brain metastases. These are like tumors that spread to the brain. The studies tried to see if certain medicines or special programs could help keep their thinking skills from getting worse or make them better.

Six studies were chosen for this review. Three studied ways to stop thinking skills from getting worse, and three studied ways to make thinking skills better. But because the studies used different things, it wasn't possible to combine all the results into one big picture.

Two studies looked at a medicine called memantine. One found that it helped keep thinking skills better over time, but another didn't find a clear difference. Both had few side effects.

Another study looked at a medicine called donepezil. It seemed to help improve thinking skills, but some people got sick from taking it. Again, there were only a few people in these studies, so we can't be sure about the results.

One study looked at a special program to help thinking skills. It didn't show a clear difference, but it did help with one type of thinking test.

None of the studies looked at other ways to help thinking skills besides medicines. Some of the studies had problems because people left the study early, which made it hard to know if the results were true.

Overall, the studies suggest that memantine might help keep thinking skills from getting worse, and donepezil might help improve them. But more research is needed to be really sure. Other ways to help thinking skills aren't very clear right now. More studies are needed to learn more.

This study looked at whether a type of exercise called PFMT helps with a condition called prolapse. Six studies were reviewed, and three of them were new. Some of the studies had problems being sure they were fair, but overall, the results suggest that PFMT might help. 

Four studies showed that women who did PFMT felt better than those who didn't. This happened in three out of four studies. The studies measured how much better people felt in different ways, but they mostly agreed that PFMT helped. 

One study found that PFMT made it easier for women to do their normal activities after surgery. But another study said PFMT didn't make a big difference in how well women could go to the bathroom.

Overall, there's some good news that PFMT might help with prolapse, especially right after doing the exercises. But we need more studies to know if it works over time and if it's worth the effort. We also need to look at other ways to prevent prolapse and see if they work too.

output: This research looked at 12 studies involving 933 people with a condition called Multiple Sclerosis (MS). These studies gave some people extra vitamin D and others a different kind of treatment to see if it helped. After 52 weeks, the extra vitamin D didn't seem to help reduce the number of times people had a flare-up of their MS, or make them less disabled. It also didn't seem to cause more side effects than the regular treatment. Some studies found that vitamin D might help people feel better about their lives, but not all studies agreed. Other studies showed that vitamin D didn't affect how tired people felt. The studies didn't look at other important things like how long it took for a person's MS to get worse, or how many people needed to go to the hospital because of their MS. Overall, the best information we have right now isn't strong enough to say that taking extra vitamin D helps people with MS. But so far, it doesn't seem to hurt either. A few more studies are still being done, and they might give us more information later.

This research looked at 62 studies about a breathing method called the active cycle of breathing technique. Out of these, 19 studies with 440 people were carefully chosen because they followed strict rules. These studies showed that this technique works similarly to other methods like autogenic drainage and airway oscillating devices. 

The studies didn't always do things perfectly, but they mostly told us what happened after using the techniques. They compared it to other treatments like chest physiotherapy. The studies found that this breathing technique doesn’t seem to make a big difference in how well people can breathe, how much mucus they cough up, or how often they get sick. 

However, some studies found that people liked this technique better than others. And when they looked at how well people could exercise and how their lungs worked, they didn’t see much difference. 

Overall, the research isn’t strong enough to say if this technique is better than other ones. But some longer-term studies suggest it might be as good as other treatments. More research is needed to know if this technique helps people with cystic fibrosis feel better and prefer it over other methods.

This study looked at two groups of people with a breathing problem called COPD. One group took a special medicine twice a day, while the other group took a different medicine. There were also some ongoing studies that were planned but not yet finished.

The study had 880 people in total. It lasted for 12 weeks. Both groups got the same medicines, just in different combinations. But the researchers couldn't be sure if the new medicine worked better because they didn't have enough information. Here’s what they found:

- The new medicine didn’t seem to help people live longer.
- It didn’t seem to cause more breathing problems.
- There were fewer cases of pneumonia when people took the new medicine, but none of these were life-threatening.
- The new medicine didn’t seem to cause more serious side effects overall.

The study wasn’t perfect because it was small and didn’t last long enough. Also, there wasn’t much information about other important things like how well people could exercise or how often they needed to use their rescue inhalers.

Overall, the study suggests that the new medicine might work about the same as the older one, but it’s hard to know for sure. More studies are needed to find out if the new medicine really works better or if it causes different side effects. Right now, we don’t have enough good information to say for certain which medicine is better.
