This research looked at different types of arch wires used in teeth straightening. They found three new studies, making a total of twelve studies with 799 people involved. Some of these studies had some problems being fair, while others did not. No studies reported if the arch wires caused the teeth to move back into their old positions.

The researchers compared different types of arch wires like stainless steel, superelastic nickel-titanium (NiTi), and thermoelastic NiTi. They found:

- For stainless steel and superelastic NiTi, they couldn't tell if one type moved teeth faster or if they hurt more.
- For stainless steel and thermoelastic NiTi, they couldn't tell if one type moved teeth faster or if they hurt more.
- For NiTi wires that bend easily and those that don't, they couldn't tell if one type moved teeth faster or if they hurt more.
- For NiTi wires that bend easily and those that bend in a special way, the ones that bend easily moved teeth a little bit faster.
- For superelastic NiTi and thermoelastic NiTi, they couldn't tell if one type moved teeth faster or if they hurt more at the start.

Overall, the studies didn't give clear answers about which type of arch wire works best for moving teeth. They suggest that NiTi wires that bend easily might work better, but more research is needed to know for sure.

output: This study looked at 19 different studies involving 2663 people to see if antibiotics helped treat their illness better. For people with milder to moderate sickness, the studies showed that antibiotics didn't make much difference in how well they got better within about a month. But for people who were very sick, antibiotics seemed to help them get better faster. There wasn't enough information to know if antibiotics made a big difference in how long people stayed in the hospital. Antibiotics didn't seem to help people live longer, but they might help prevent them from getting sicker again. Some studies found that antibiotics could cause side effects, but it wasn't clear if these happened more often than usual. The studies also found that antibiotics didn't seem to cause more infections. More research is needed to find out which sick people might really benefit from taking antibiotics and which ones might not. This way, doctors can give antibiotics only to those who will likely get better and avoid using them for those who won't.

output: This research looked at 11 studies involving 3060 people who had been randomly assigned to different treatments. The studies found that a type of medicine called non-steroidal antiandrogens did not work as well as another treatment called castration. Non-steroidal antiandrogens made it harder for people to live longer, more likely to have their condition get worse faster, and more likely to stop taking the medicine because of side effects. Side effects like breast pain, gynecomastia, and feeling weak were more common with these medicines. But they seemed to reduce other side effects like hot flashes, bleeding, and urinary problems. The studies weren't perfect, so we're not sure if non-steroidal antiandrogens help or hurt in the long run. For people with advanced prostate cancer that hasn't spread yet, more research might help us know better. But for people with advanced prostate cancer that has spread, we think we already know enough. Future studies should be very good and follow people for a long time to get clearer answers.

This research looked at whether certain chemicals in the spinal fluid (called CSF) can help tell if someone with memory problems (MCI) will get Alzheimer's disease or another type of dementia. They studied 1282 people who started with MCI. Over time, 430 of them got Alzheimer's disease and 130 got other types of dementia.

They tested two ways to look at these chemicals:
1. One way checked for a chemical called t-tau. It wasn't very good at telling who would get Alzheimer's disease. When it was 72% sure someone didn't have Alzheimer's, it was only about 75% sure they really didn't.
2. Another way checked for a different chemical called p-tau. This was better. When it was 47.5% sure someone didn't have Alzheimer's, it was about 81% sure they really didn't.

There weren't enough studies to make a big picture of how well these tests work overall. Some of the studies weren't done very well. Also, there isn't much information about how well these tests work for other types of dementia.

Because there aren't many good studies, doctors don't know yet if using these tests helps them decide if someone with memory problems really has Alzheimer's disease. There's also a chance that these tests might sometimes say someone has Alzheimer's when they don't, which could lead to unnecessary treatment.

More research is needed to make these tests clearer and more reliable. Until then, doctors need to be careful when using these tests to diagnose Alzheimer's disease.

This study looked at two ways to help kids who have trouble with their speech, called CAS. It included 26 children aged 4 to 12 who had mild to moderate speech problems. The study compared two different treatments: one called NDP-3 and another called ReST. The children were split into two groups and each group got one of these treatments. The treatments happened in a clinic in Australia, and speech therapists taught them. The study checked how well the kids spoke before and after the treatments, and again one month and four months later. But some kids started talking normally again during those last few months, so we couldn't be sure if the treatments worked for everyone.

The study found that both treatments helped kids speak better, especially on words they were practicing. But it wasn't clear if one treatment was better than the other. The study didn't look at how well kids used their speech in everyday life. There's not much proof yet about which treatment works best for kids with CAS, but more studies might help us know more.

In a review of 38 studies with 1896 people, only one study was done very carefully. Most studies had problems that might have affected their results. The studies looked at ways to help people move better after they had their bones fixed or weren't able to move them much.

Three small studies looked at helping people move after their bones were fixed. Two studies found that letting people do some exercises while wearing a removable brace helped them move their ankles more than when they wore a regular cast. This also meant they had fewer problems like soreness. But there were more small injuries too.

One study found that using a special kind of electricity called neurostimulation might help people move their ankles better in the short term. But there wasn't enough good evidence to know if this works long-term.

During the time when people couldn't move much, starting to put weight on their feet seemed to help them move their ankles a bit better. But there wasn't enough strong evidence to say which type of brace or support was best.

Some small studies found that certain types of electrical treatments might help, but the evidence isn't clear. And there wasn't much evidence about things like stretching or getting massages to help move better.

Overall, the evidence suggests that starting to put weight on your feet and using a removable brace to let you exercise might help you move your ankles better. But there's a chance of having more small injuries. More studies are needed to make sure these ideas work and to find out the best way to help people move better after their bones are fixed.

Some studies showed that using room air instead of carbon dioxide might help save money, but there wasn't enough good information to be sure. Using any of these gases had very few serious problems, but we don't know if they're completely safe. More studies are needed to learn more about these gases and how they affect people having this type of surgery.

This research looked at different ways to help babies and young children grow better, especially in places where people don't have much money. They studied 15 studies, mostly in countries like Bangladesh, India, and Peru. These studies focused on giving extra vitamins and minerals to mothers and children, teaching them about healthy eating, and making sure they get enough food.

Most of these studies weren't perfect, but some did show good results. For example, giving extra zinc to mommies while they're pregnant didn't seem to help their babies be born lighter. But teaching mommies about healthy eating did help their babies be less likely to be born too small. Giving extra vitamins and minerals to kids also didn't seem to make them grow taller. And helping families learn about healthy eating helped their babies be less likely to be born too small.

Overall, these studies suggest that giving extra nutrients might help, but we need more information to know for sure. Also, it's hard to keep track of everyone in these areas because people move around a lot. So, we need more research to find out if these kinds of programs work well in cities where many people live in poor conditions. We also need to look at how different parts of society can work together to improve nutrition.

This research looked at five hundred and sixteen people who had a condition called retinal detachment with something called proliferative vitreoretinopathy (PVR). They tried different materials to help keep the retina in place during a surgery called pars plana vitrectomy. Three studies were done:

- One study in the United States gave some people silicone oil and others sulfur hexafluoride gas.
- Another study also used silicone oil but had two different strengths.
- A third study compared heavy silicone oil to regular silicone oil in nine people.

The studies found that after one year, people who got silicone oil or perfluoropropane gas didn't have much difference in their vision or if their retina stayed attached. But after two years, people who got silicone oil had better vision. Sulfur hexafluoride gas didn't work as well as silicone oil after one year, but it was okay after two years.

The studies weren't perfect. Some didn't check if they had enough people to see differences. One study had many people drop out, so we don't know if the results would be the same if everyone stayed in the study. Also, the researchers couldn't hide which treatment the doctors gave, so that might have affected the results.

Overall, silicone oil seems to be a good choice for most people. If you need this treatment, your doctor will decide which type is best for you based on your specific situation. Heavy silicone oil isn't commonly used, and the studies showed it wasn't better than regular silicone oil.

output: This research looked at three studies involving 492 people who had hip replacement surgery. The studies had some problems in how they were done, so we're not sure about their results. One study compared two groups: one got special instructions and equipment to help them recover, while the other didn't. At 12 months, we're not sure if these extra instructions helped people move better or feel better overall. But there were no problems like the hip coming out of place in either group. Another study looked at whether giving people extra help right after surgery made them feel better about their recovery. It wasn't clear if this extra help made a difference. The last study looked at giving people more help and education after they left the hospital to get back to normal activities. Again, we're not sure if this helped people move better or feel better. Overall, the evidence isn't strong enough to say if these extra steps really help after hip replacement surgery. More studies are needed to find out which types of help might work best and if they make a difference in things like pain, how well people can do daily tasks, and how often they need to go back to the doctor.

This research looked at ways to prevent blood clots called VTE in children who have tubes in their veins (CVCs) to help them get medicine. They studied different medicines like low molecular weight heparin (LMWH), antithrombin (AT), and others. But most of the studies had some problems, and the results weren't always clear.

In total, they looked at 1291 children. Some studies gave extra AT or something called cryoprecipitate and fresh frozen plasma (FFP) to children who didn't have enough of these things. But even with these extra treatments, there wasn't much difference in how many children got blood clots compared to those who didn't get anything special.

The researchers did a few smaller studies where they compared giving AT plus LMWH to just AT. In these studies, fewer children got blood clots when they also got LMWH. But there were no big differences in other bad side effects like bleeding or infections.

Overall, the studies showed that giving extra AT or other treatments didn't seem to make much difference in preventing blood clots in children with CVCs. The researchers couldn't strongly recommend any specific treatment based on this information because there weren't enough children in the studies. More studies are needed to learn more about what works best.

This study looked at different treatments for Bell's palsy, which is a condition where someone loses the ability to move their face muscles. They reviewed 14 studies with 2488 people who had Bell's palsy. Most of the studies were small and some might not have been done very well.

The study found that taking both special medicines (antivirals) and steroids (corticosteroids) did not seem to help more people recover completely from Bell's palsy compared to just using steroids. However, it also didn't seem to hurt. People who took just steroids had a slightly higher chance of getting better than those who took just antivirals, but the difference wasn't very big.

For people with more severe Bell's palsy, the combination of antivirals and steroids didn't seem to help them get better faster than just steroids alone. But it did seem to help prevent some problems that can happen later, like when the face moves in funny ways or when tears don't work right.

Steroids alone seemed to help people get better more often than just antivirals. And the combination of antivirals and steroids seemed to help prevent some problems that can happen later compared to just steroids.

There weren't many side effects from the different treatments, but the study couldn't be sure if the side effects were different because of the medicine or just because of chance. The researchers think they need to do more studies to see if one type of antiviral works better than another.

Overall, the best treatment seems to be just steroids, but the combination of steroids and antivirals might be helpful in some cases. More research is needed to find out the best way to treat Bell's palsy.

This research looked at a treatment called SNS, which uses small electrical signals to help people with problems like leaking stool or having trouble going to the bathroom. They studied this treatment in different ways in six trials and two smaller ones.

In one big trial, 53 people with really bad leaking problems got the SNS treatment. At first, they had fewer times when they leaked than those who just got regular medicine. But after a year, the number of times they leaked was about the same. Some people had a little pain where the treatment was put in their body.

Another trial had 15 people with leaking problems. They also got the SNS treatment. At first, they had fewer times when they leaked compared to another treatment called PTNS. But after a year, the number of times they leaked was about the same.

In some other trials, the SNS treatment didn't seem to help people have more bowel movements, but it could make them feel less pain sometimes.

The studies showed that SNS might help some people with leaking problems, but it didn't work for everyone. Also, some people had small problems like pain or swelling where the treatment was put in. More studies are needed to know if SNS works well and if there are fewer problems with it.

This study looked at 85 different studies to see what healthy pregnant and new moms, along with doctors and nurses, thought about getting prenatal care. They found that where you live—whether rich, middle class, or poor—a lot of people think about prenatal care differently. 

The studies showed that for prenatal care to be helpful, it needs to feel good and be done in a way that makes people feel safe and cared for. This means having friendly, understanding doctors who take the time to talk to you and your baby. It also means having enough money and staff to help you get this care.

The studies also found that how much women like prenatal care depends on things like whether they think pregnancy is a healthy or risky time, and what their culture says about prenatal care. If women have a good experience the first time they go, they're more likely to keep going.

Doctors need to be trained well and paid fairly so they don't try to get extra money from patients. They also need to respect that most pregnancies are normal, but know how to handle any problems that might come up.

Overall, this review helps us understand why some women and families might not want prenatal care, and why others do. It suggests ways to make prenatal care better for everyone. People who run health centers should use this information to improve their services.

This research looked at studies about medicines used to treat heart failure, especially in people who also have kidney problems. Out of 112 studies reviewed, most didn't have good information about how well the medicines worked. Only 26 studies had enough clear information to look at together.

For heart failure overall, we're not sure if some medicines like adenosine A1-receptor antagonists, dopamine, nesiritide, or serelaxin help people live longer or stay out of the hospital. Some medicines like angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors (ACEi) or angiotensin receptor blockers (ARB) might slightly lower the chance of dying, but we're not very confident about this. Beta-blockers seem to help people live longer, but we're not sure if they make it less likely for them to need to go to the hospital for heart problems.

Some medicines like aldosterone antagonists might make it more likely for people to have too much potassium in their blood, which isn't good. But we're not sure about this either. Other medicines like renin inhibitors don't seem to raise the risk of too much potassium.

We're not sure if these medicines affect how well heart failure gets worse or if they improve quality of life. We also don't know if they cause low blood pressure, which can be dangerous.

The medicines that help with heart rhythm problems, digoxin, and some others aren't very clear either. There just weren't enough studies to tell us much about them.

Overall, we don't have enough information to use these medicines safely in people with both heart failure and kidney problems. More studies are needed to learn more about how these medicines work in people with kidney problems.

output: This research looked at a treatment called RIC to see if it helps prevent and treat strokes. They studied seven groups of people in total, with 735 people altogether. The researchers checked if the studies were done fairly and if they followed all the rules. They found that RIC might help stop strokes in some cases, like when arteries in the brain are partly blocked. It also seemed to make strokes less serious when arteries in the neck are fixed. But RIC might make people more likely to die or become dependent after having a stroke caused by a clot in the brain. The results aren't very strong because there weren't many studies, and the ones that did exist had some problems. So while RIC might help in some situations, we're not sure yet because the information isn't very clear.

This research looked at 10 studies that tested different ways to help kids with a skin condition called atopic eczema. Five of these studies were new to this review. All the studies gave kids extra help along with regular treatments. The studies involved 2003 kids in total and 44 kids in one special study about feelings.

Some of the studies weren't perfect, but the biggest and best one showed that kids who got extra help had less of the rash and felt better overall. They had more than 9 out of 10 chances that the extra help worked. 

The study that helped the most kids was for those under 7 years old. They saw big improvements in their quality of life. For kids between 8 and 12 years old, they saw good improvements in 3 out of 5 areas. 

Overall, the review found that giving kids extra education and support can help them feel better and have less of the rash. But the studies didn't always explain exactly how they did the extra help, so it's hard to know if it would work the same way in other places. More studies are needed to see if these methods really work and if they're worth the time and effort.

Most of the studies didn't have many problems in how they were done, but some had issues that made it hard to know for sure if the teaching helped. The studies compared different ways of teaching people to use their inhalers, like having a face-to-face lesson, watching videos, or using special devices to give feedback.

The studies found that teaching people to use their inhalers better worked well right away and also after some time. But it wasn't always clear how much better people did. Sometimes, checking how well people were using their inhalers affected whether they learned more or not. Using a checklist to measure how well people were doing didn't always show a clear difference.

For adults, teaching them to use their inhalers better seemed to help, especially when it was checked within 2 to 26 weeks. This means that 69 out of every 100 people in the group that got extra teaching had good inhaler technique, compared to only 45 out of 100 in the group that didn't get extra teaching. This was a moderate-quality finding, which means we're not very confident about it.

The studies tried different kinds of help like talking about feelings, going to a special program, getting short advice, or having someone talk them into making changes. But they didn't find much difference between these different kinds of help. 

For some comparisons, like talking about feelings and going to a special program, there wasn't enough information to know if one worked better than the other. For others, like getting short advice or talking to someone, it seemed like they might help a little bit, but we're not sure because the studies weren't very good. 

The studies also looked at whether people stopped drinking too much alcohol or stayed in treatment longer. Again, they didn't see big differences between the different kinds of help. 

Overall, the research suggests that none of these different types of help seem to work much better than just checking in or doing nothing special. It's hard to say which might work best because there aren't many good studies. So, we don't have strong proof about which type of help is best.

This research looked at many studies that tried to stop kids from smoking. There were 27 studies in total, but they didn't all do exactly the same thing. Some focused on families, others on schools, and some tried both. They came from places like the USA, Europe, Australia, and India. Many of the studies weren't perfect, so we're not sure how good the results really are. But overall, it seems that helping families together can help kids avoid smoking. 

In most of the studies, researchers followed kids for a while to see if they started smoking. They found that kids who got extra help from their families were less likely to start smoking. About 4,800 kids were part of these studies, and they showed that the chances of kids starting to smoke were lower by about 24%. 

Some studies tried to combine family help with school programs, and those worked too. But not all the studies could be put together to make one big picture. 

The studies mostly used a lot of help from families, but even some studies that used less help still seemed to work. It's not clear if less help would work as well. 

Overall, the best way to help kids avoid smoking seems to be giving them lots of support from their families. This kind of help can make a difference, but we need more studies to know for sure.

This study looked at 12 trials involving 563 people with sickle cell disease, mostly African-American, aged between 6 and 35 years. The trials tested different types of education programs, ranging from one hour to weekly sessions over 8 weeks. Some of the trials lasted until 12 months after the program ended. The studies had some differences, like who they studied and how they did the tests, which made it hard to compare them all perfectly.

The education programs seemed to help people learn more about their condition. Four trials showed that patients learned about 0.87 more points on average, which is a bit better. But when we look at just the best trials, this number becomes 0.67 points. This means patients learned more about their disease. However, caregivers didn't seem to learn much more from the same programs.

The education helped patients remember more about their illness and its signs and symptoms, which might help them take care of themselves better. It also seemed to make caregivers feel less depressed. But there wasn't enough information to know if this helps patients manage their illness better.

The studies weren't perfect. Some didn't report all the results clearly, and some had problems keeping participants involved. Also, the education programs didn't seem to help patients use the health services more often.

Overall, the evidence shows that education programs can help patients learn more about their sickle cell disease and feel less depressed. But the improvements aren't very big, and we need more research to be sure if this helps patients in real life. The studies had some problems that might affect the results, so we need better-designed trials in the future.

This research looked at whether a special kind of fetal heart monitor, called admission CTG, helps during labor for women who don't have any known problems. They reviewed four studies that involved over 13,000 women who were in labor. These studies were done in the UK and Ireland. 

The studies didn't find strong proof that admission CTG helped. On average, women who got admission CTG had a slightly higher chance of needing a cesarean section compared to those who just listened to the baby's heartbeat intermittently. But this difference wasn't big enough to be sure it was real. 

There was also no clear difference in how often babies had problems after birth. Admission CTG didn't seem to make things better or worse for babies. However, women who got admission CTG had more continuous fetal heart monitoring during labor and more fetal blood tests. 

Overall, the studies showed that admission CTG might lead to more cesarean sections without providing extra benefits. The researchers think there's a good chance that admission CTG could increase the need for cesareans by around 20%. 

The studies weren't perfect because they didn't always follow the same rules, and sometimes people knew which group the women were in. Because of these issues, the evidence isn't very strong. 

Based on this information, doctors and nurses should tell women that admission CTG might lead to more cesareans without giving them extra benefits. More research is needed to look at women who show signs of labor before they're officially diagnosed.

This research looked at two types of studies about a medicine called pregabalin for people who have fibromyalgia, which is a condition that causes pain all over the body. They found that people taking pregabalin felt less pain compared to those taking a sugar pill. Specifically:

- About 14% of people taking pregabalin 300 to 600 mg felt their pain reduced by at least half after 12 to 13 weeks, while only about 9% more felt this way compared to those on a sugar pill.
- Around 28% of people taking pregabalin 300 to 600 mg felt their pain reduced by at least a third, which was about 11% more than those on a sugar pill.

The studies showed that pregabalin was safe overall, but some people did experience side effects like feeling dizzy, sleepy, gaining weight, or swelling in their feet. However, these side effects were not very common. Most people taking pregabalin also felt better overall, including having less pain and feeling more able to do daily activities.

The studies found that about 10% of people taking pregabalin had their pain reduced so much that they didn't want to stop taking the medicine. This happened more often with the highest dose of pregabalin (600 mg) compared to when people started taking smaller amounts first and then increased them.

Overall, the research suggests that pregabalin helps reduce pain in fibromyalgia, but it's important to talk to a doctor about the benefits and risks before starting this medicine.

This research looked at three types of medicines called amphetamines to see if they help people with a condition called ADHD. They studied 2521 people, mostly men aged 35 years old, who had ADHD. The studies lasted about 5 weeks.

The researchers found that amphetamines helped reduce the symptoms of ADHD, especially when measured by doctors. Patients also reported feeling better. However, the medicines didn't help people stay on the treatment longer. Many people stopped taking the medicine because of side effects like feeling sick or having trouble sleeping.

Different kinds of amphetamines worked similarly well. Lisdexamfetamine and mixed amphetamine salts seemed to work better than dexamphetamine. But it's hard to know if these results apply to everyone because the studies weren't perfect. Some people might have known which medicine they were getting, and some people dropped out of the studies. Also, the studies were short and only included certain types of people.

Overall, the evidence isn't very strong because the studies weren't done perfectly. So while amphetamines seem to help with ADHD symptoms, we can't be sure they're the best choice for everyone. More research is needed to find out.

This study looked at 57 different studies that involved 34,390 people. These studies tested if digital programs could help people drink less alcohol. Most of the studies had some problems that might have affected their results, but we still think the findings are reliable.

The main finding was that people who used digital programs drank about 23 grams of alcohol less each week (which is about 3 UK units) compared to those who didn't use any programs. This happened even after the studies ended. Other studies also found that people who used these programs had fewer days when they drank alcohol and had fewer heavy drinking sessions.

However, only a few studies compared digital programs to face-to-face programs, and they didn't find a big difference in how much people drank.

Some parts of the digital programs seemed to work better. Things like helping people set goals, solve problems, learn about why they drink too much, and get advice from believable sources helped people drink less alcohol.

The studies found that digital programs worked well overall, but it's hard to know exactly how much they help because some studies had problems. Also, it's possible that the differences seen might not be real, or that other factors might affect the results.

In summary, digital programs seem to help people drink less alcohol, but more research is needed to confirm this. The best parts of these programs are things that help people make plans and solve problems related to drinking. But we don't know if all digital programs will work equally well, and more studies need to look into this.

This research looked at five studies involving 240 children aged 1 to 18 who had mild to moderate sleep-disordered breathing (OSA). The studies were done in special sleep clinics at big hospitals. They compared different treatments: some kids got steroid sprays in one nostril, others took a medicine called montelukast, and some got nothing.

The studies found that kids who got montelukast had fewer times when their breathing stopped or slowed down during sleep. This happened in two out of three studies. But it's not clear if the steroid spray helped much. It might help a little bit, but we're not sure.

Montelukast seemed to make kids' breathing better, but we're not very confident about this. Kids taking montelukast had less trouble getting enough oxygen while sleeping. This happened in two out of three studies too.

The studies showed that these medicines were safe, but not many side effects were seen. No study looked at whether these medicines could stop kids from needing surgery for OSA.

Overall, we don't know if these medicines work very well for treating OSA in children. They might help a little bit, but we need more studies to be sure. We also need to see if these treatments work over a longer time and if they cause any problems. It would be good to look at how these treatments affect things like attention and learning in school. More research is needed to find out if these medicines are helpful and safe for children with OSA.

This review looked at 28 studies involving 788 children and adults who use different ways to clear their lungs. In 18 of these studies, 296 people used a mask, while in 3 studies they used a mouthpiece with nose clips, and in 3 studies it wasn't clear what they used. They compared these methods to others like ACBT, AD, special breathing machines, and exercises. The main thing they checked was how well people could blow out air from their lungs. Most of the studies didn't show much difference between the different methods for clearing lungs over short periods. But longer studies weren't sure if one method worked better than another.

They also looked at how often people got sick with breathing problems. They found that people who used PEP (a special breathing machine) with a mask for at least a year got sick less often than those who used other methods. One study found that people who used PEP with a mouthpiece didn't get sick less often. People preferred PEP over other methods in most studies that lasted at least a month.

The studies sometimes had problems being fair, like not always making sure who got which treatment. But overall, the evidence shows that PEP might help people with a lung disease called Cystic Fibrosis. The review suggests that doctors should choose the best way to clear people's lungs based on their age, what they like, and how well their lungs work.

This study looked at a type of help called Intensive Case Management (ICM) for people who have serious mental health problems. They reviewed 40 studies that included over 7500 people. The studies compared ICM to regular care and to another kind of support that isn't as intensive.

When ICM was compared to regular care, it seemed to help people stay out of the hospital for shorter periods of time. It also helped more people stay in the program longer. But it didn't seem to make much difference in helping people feel better mentally or in their ability to work.

When ICM was compared to other less intensive forms of support, it didn't seem to make much difference in helping people stay out of the hospital or in their ability to work. However, when ICM was done well according to its rules, it did seem to help people stay out of the hospital for shorter times.

The studies weren't perfect because some of them might have shown only good results. Also, it's hard to know if ICM really helps people's mental health or quality of life because the studies didn't look at those things directly.

Overall, ICM seems to be helpful for people who need a lot of help staying out of the hospital. But it's not clear if it helps more than just doing a simpler form of support. More studies are needed to compare ICM to regular care and to other types of support.

This research looked at whether using creams on the skin during pregnancy might affect babies. They reviewed 14 studies that followed many pregnant women and their babies. Most of these studies didn't find that using any strength of cream during pregnancy had a big effect on things like how the baby was born, if the baby would have birth defects, if the baby was born early, or if the baby died in the womb. 

For some things like low birth weight, the studies weren't sure if there was a link. But some studies suggested that using stronger creams might make it more likely for the baby to be born early. There was also a small chance that using stronger creams might slightly increase the risk of the baby dying in the womb.

The studies found that using weaker creams during pregnancy seemed to help reduce the risk of the baby dying in the womb. However, they couldn't be completely sure about this because the studies weren't perfect. 

Overall, the research suggests that using any type of cream during pregnancy doesn't seem to cause major problems for the baby. But there might be a small increased risk of low birth weight for women who use stronger creams, especially if they use them a lot. More research is needed to confirm this. Using weaker creams during pregnancy seems to be safe and might even help protect the baby from dying in the womb.

In this review, we looked at seven new studies about a type of medicine called morphine. We found that six studies didn't fit our criteria, and one is still being done, so we didn't include them. Altogether, we looked at 62 studies with 4241 people in them. Most of the studies used a method where they gave the medicine to some people first and then switched to another kind, usually for a week or less. But the way they did this wasn't very good.

The studies mostly looked at how well morphine works to help people feel better when they're in pain. They compared different types of morphine, like regular morphine and special forms that last longer. Some studies also compared morphine to other medicines that work on pain.

Overall, most of the studies showed that morphine helps people feel much better, with about 80% of people saying their pain was no worse than a little bit. But sometimes, even though people took the medicine, they still felt a lot of pain. About 6% of people stopped taking the medicine because they couldn't stand the side effects.

The studies we looked at aren't perfect. They're old and not very big, and they weren't always set up to compare different kinds of morphine fairly. But the overall idea that morphine works well for pain hasn't changed. It's been shown to work for a long time, but there aren't many studies that look at all the different ways morphine might work. Most of the studies only had a few hundred people in them, which isn't enough to really know if one kind of morphine is better than another. However, the studies do show that morphine works well for most people, and that it can be taken in different ways to get the right amount of medicine.

This research looked at five different studies involving 162 people to see if taking antibiotics could help with a type of skin condition called psoriasis. Three of these studies happened in a special place where doctors treat skin problems. Some of the studies got money from companies that make medicine. The people in the studies were between 12 and 77 years old, but most were older than 15. Before starting the studies, some people had a lot of psoriasis, while others had just a little bit.

The studies didn't measure how quickly the psoriasis went away or if it came back later. They also didn't look at whether the people taking the medicine felt better overall. The researchers think the results might not be very reliable because the studies weren't perfect. They're not sure if the medicine works well or if it has bad side effects.

There were only a few studies looking at different ways to use antibiotics. One study found that a type of antibiotic called azithromycin helped more people get their psoriasis to go away completely over a year. Another study found that removing the tonsils (the part of your mouth that swells when you have strep throat) helped some people get their psoriasis to go away completely too. But other studies didn't measure these things.

Overall, the evidence isn't strong enough to know if these medicines work well or if they cause problems. More studies are needed to find out if these treatments are safe and effective for people with psoriasis.

This study looked at different treatments for a type of cancer called Hodgkin lymphoma (HL) in adults. They checked 1796 records and found 5 studies that fit their criteria. These studies involved 3427 people. Some studies were done in Germany, some in Italy, and one in Belgium. The studies mostly showed good results, but there were some problems with how they were done, like not always being able to keep things secret so people wouldn't know which treatment they got.

The studies showed that a treatment called BEACOPP escalated helped people live longer and stay healthy longer than another treatment called ABVD. For every 100 people who took ABVD, about 120 would die after 5 years, while about 90 people who took BEACOPP escalated would die after 5 years. Also, fewer people in the BEACOPP escalated group had their cancer get worse or return after 5 years.

BEACOPP escalated didn't seem to cause more deaths, but it did make some people's blood count go down more. It also seemed to slightly increase the chance of getting another kind of blood problem called AML or MDS, but this wasn't clear because the studies weren't long enough to see if this happened often.

There wasn't enough information to tell if BEACOPP escalated caused more infertility, especially since not many women were studied. The studies also didn't look at whether BEACOPP escalated made men less fertile.

Overall, the studies suggest that BEACOPP escalated helps people with HL live longer and feel better, but it might make some people feel sicker. More research is needed to understand the long-term effects, especially about infertility and second cancers.

In a study looking at 130 research papers involving 8341 people, doctors gave some people a medicine called ketamine before and after certain surgeries. The medicine was used in surgeries like removing wisdom teeth, repairing knees, and fixing broken hips. Some people got a special kind of ketamine, while others got a sugar pill instead. 

The study found that people who got ketamine needed less pain medicine after their surgery. They needed about 8 less units of a common painkiller over 24 hours compared to those who didn't get ketamine. This was true whether they had minor or major surgeries. People also felt less pain at rest and when moving around after their surgery. 

Ketamine made it take longer for people to ask for more pain relief after their surgery, but this wasn't a big deal. It also helped reduce swelling in the body after surgery. However, some people did have side effects like feeling confused, but these were rare. 

Overall, using ketamine before and after surgery seems to help people feel less pain and need less pain medicine afterward. But it doesn't seem to make much difference in how often people feel sick after surgery.

This research looked at studies about adding a vitamin called folic acid to flour to help prevent some birth problems. They studied different types of flour and where the studies were done. Some studies used special groups of people to see if the flour helped, while others just followed large groups over time.

The studies didn't find that adding folic acid to flour stopped all kinds of birth problems, like spina bifida or anencephaly. But they did find that adding folic acid to flour made it easier for mommies-to-be to have enough of something called folate in their blood. This helps keep them healthy during pregnancy.

Some studies also found that adding folic acid to flour made it easier for mommies-to-be to have more red blood cells in their blood, which can help prevent something called anaemia.

However, the studies weren't perfect. There weren't many of them, and some parts of the studies weren't clear. So we don't know for sure if adding folic acid to flour will definitely help prevent birth problems or make mommies-to-be healthier. We also don't know if it might cause any bad side effects. More studies would be needed to learn more.

output:
This research looked at whether certain medicines called antibiotics could help children who are at higher risk of getting lung infections. They studied 10 studies that included children with different health problems like HIV, cystic fibrosis, sickle cell disease, cancer, and babies born very early. The studies lasted from a few days to several years.

For children with HIV, taking a medicine called isoniazid didn't seem to stop them from getting a serious lung infection called TB. But it didn't seem to make their chances of dying any better. One study found that giving these children another medicine called co-trimoxazole might actually lower their chance of dying.

For children with cystic fibrosis, taking a medicine called co-trimoxazole seemed to keep them from needing to go to the hospital as much. Taking another medicine called azithromycin also helped them have fewer times when their lungs got really sick.

The studies showed that these medicines didn't cause many bad side effects. But they weren't sure if the medicines made it harder for germs to become stronger over time.

For children with sickle cell disease, taking a different medicine called penicillin V didn't seem to help prevent lung infections. And for children with cancer, taking a medicine called trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole seemed to help prevent a lung infection called Pneumocystis carinii pneumonia.

Overall, the research suggests that these medicines might help some children at higher risk of lung infections, but more studies are needed to know for sure. Doctors think that studying these medicines in children with other types of health problems, like those born very early or with heart problems, would be helpful.

output:
In a recent study, researchers looked at how often different health problems happen in people who had cancer treatments. They checked 61 studies that included over 13,000 people. These studies looked at things like whether people's kidneys got weaker (called renal dysfunction), whether they had too much salt in their urine (proteinuria), and whether they had low levels of calcium or magnesium in their blood (hypophosphataemia and hypomagnesaemia).

The studies found that the chances of having weak kidneys varied a lot. Some studies said about 2% of people had weak kidneys, while others said up to 84% might have them. Other issues like high blood pressure also varied widely.

Some studies found that certain medicines or treatments seemed to make people more likely to have weak kidneys. For example, some people who got a type of radiation called total body irradiation (TBI) along with certain medicines had their kidneys get weaker. Also, people who had surgery to remove part of their kidney (nephrectomy) or took very strong medicine called ifosfamide were more likely to have weak kidneys.

However, many of the studies didn't agree on exactly what caused these problems. Some studies found that taking certain medicines for a long time might make kidneys weaker, while others didn't see this happening.

Because the studies were different in so many ways, it was hard to know for sure what causes these problems. Researchers think that future studies should use better methods to compare the results and look at more people to get clearer answers.

For now, doctors should keep an eye on people who had cancer treatments to check their kidneys and blood pressure. More research is needed to understand these issues better.

output: This study looked at 36 different studies involving 2,999 people who had a condition called pulmonary hypertension. The studies lasted anywhere from 14 weeks to up to 12 months. Some studies included children, but most did not. The researchers found that people taking medicines called PDE5 inhibitors improved their breathing ability and were less likely to die during the study period. They could walk a little farther too. However, these medicines caused some side effects like headaches, upset stomachs, flushing, and muscle aches. The studies showed that PDE5 inhibitors helped people with pulmonary hypertension better than a sugar pill, but they weren't sure if it helped everyone. For people whose pulmonary hypertension was caused by problems in the left side of their heart, the medicines seemed to help them walk a bit farther. But for people whose pulmonary hypertension was caused by lung disease or blood clots in the lungs, the medicines didn't seem to help much. The studies about people with lung disease were not very strong because there wasn't enough information. More research is needed to understand why some people might benefit from these medicines and which types of heart problems might respond well to them.

We looked at 881 studies about programs that try to get people to eat less salt. These programs involved more than 260,000 people, but mostly in richer countries. Most of these programs didn't have a control group to compare them to, which makes it hard to know if the changes happened because of the program or something else. 

Out of the 10 programs that had enough information, some helped people eat less salt, while others made people eat more salt. In general, the programs seemed to work better for men than for women. But we don't know if they worked differently for people based on where they live or their education level.

None of the programs caused any bad side effects. But there weren't enough programs to really tell if they worked for everyone. The programs usually had lots of people in them, but they still couldn't be sure why some worked and others didn't. 

The main idea is that these kinds of programs might help people eat less salt overall, especially if they include things like changing food products to have less salt and making rules about where food can be sold. But we need more studies to figure out exactly how well they work and why some don't.

The study compared two groups: one group got a special fluid put into their cervix through the vagina, while the other group didn't get this fluid. Both groups also got other treatments like medicine and monitoring.

The study found that getting the fluid did not seem to help prevent infections in the mother or baby. It also did not seem to cause more problems. However, the women in the fluid group had slightly lower body temperatures when they gave birth, which might be good for the baby.

Because the study was small and some important details weren't clearly reported, we don't have enough information to know if this fluid helps or hurts. More studies are needed to find out if it's safe and effective. These studies would need to compare the fluid to not using it and look at many different outcomes, such as whether the baby has long-term health problems.

This study looked at different ways to help people with a lung condition called cystic fibrosis breathe better. They tried out several methods, including using special machines to help them breathe while they sleep, and other ways to clear their lungs. 

In seven studies, they found that using a machine to help people breathe while they sleep might make it easier for them to clear their lungs. Some people also said they liked using these machines. But the studies weren't always done in a way that makes us really sure they're fair, so we can't be totally sure about that.

Three studies looked at using a machine to help people breathe while they sleep. They found that this helped people feel better during the night and made their breathing better. But it didn't seem to help them do more exercises during the day.

One study found that using a special mask to help people breathe while sleeping might help them do better exercises. But another study found that some people couldn't use the mask because it was too hard on their breathing muscles.

Overall, the studies suggest that using a machine to help people breathe while they sleep might be helpful, especially for people with cystic fibrosis who have trouble clearing their lungs. But we don't know if it helps them get better over time or if it stops their lungs from getting worse. More studies are needed to learn more about this.

This research looked at two studies in Iran that compared two different types of eye surgeries for people with a condition called keratoconus. Both studies had about 111 people in them, but one had fewer participants. Before the surgeries, all the people had moderate to severe keratoconus. Each person had only one eye operated on. 

The studies lasted from 6.8 to 36.4 months after the surgery. One study had 12 months of follow-up data for everyone. The other study had to stop four surgeries because they couldn't do them properly. They didn't measure the vision improvement or how well the new corneas worked in those four eyes.

In the end, there wasn't much difference between the two types of surgery. One type of surgery, called DALK, had a lower chance of the new cornea being rejected by the body. But the studies weren't big enough to know for sure if one type of surgery was better overall. Some people had problems like blurry vision or swelling after the surgery, but most of these could be fixed.

Overall, the evidence isn't strong enough to say which type of surgery works best. More studies are needed to compare these two types of surgery and find out which might work better for people with keratoconus.

This research looked at three studies involving 45 children with Down syndrome who were between 29 months and six years old. The studies compared different ways parents worked with their children to improve language skills. Some studies had parents do activities alone, while others had both parents and doctors help. The studies lasted from 12 weeks to six months.

One study had nine group meetings and four home visits over 13 weeks. Another had weekly visits to the doctor or at home for 6 months. The last study had one big meeting and then smaller meetings twice a week at home for 12 weeks.

The researchers couldn't combine the studies because they used different ways to measure if the children improved. They thought the studies might not be very fair because some things weren't explained clearly. Also, the studies were too small to show if the improvements lasted long.

Some studies showed that kids in the new program could use more specific words after the program started. But these benefits didn't last for a year. One study found that kids in the new program did better on tests measuring all their language skills right after the program ended. 

However, other studies didn't see much difference in how well the kids spoke or how stressed their parents were. All the studies said the parents talked differently to their kids after the program started, but it wasn't clear if these changes lasted.

Because the studies were small and not very good, the researchers think there isn't enough proof to know if these programs work. They suggest doing more studies with bigger groups and using better ways to measure if the programs help. These studies should look at how well the parents follow the program outside of the meetings and if it helps families in other ways.

output:
In a study looking at different ways to help people feel better when they have long-lasting problems, researchers looked at 21 studies with 2658 people. These studies mostly looked at talking therapies like Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) and behavior therapies. They compared these therapies to regular care or waiting lists. The studies lasted from a few days to almost a year, and the people in the studies had their problems for many years before starting the therapy.

The studies found that the talking therapies helped people feel less bad during the time they were getting the therapy. But, it wasn't very strong. About 7 out of every 100 people dropped out of the therapy instead of continuing. Most of the studies didn't tell us if the therapies caused any bad side effects.

When comparing CBT specifically to regular care, it seemed to work a little bit better. But, it's not clear if it works better than other types of therapies. Overall, the evidence isn't very strong because many studies had problems that made them less reliable.

Only CBT has been studied enough to suggest it might be helpful in practice. CBT helps with physical symptoms, but the effects are small. The benefits last for about a year.

Compared to getting extra help or following a special plan, the talking therapies didn't seem to work better. CBT didn't work better than extra help either.

Overall, the evidence is not very strong, so we can't be sure if these therapies really work. More studies are needed, especially ones that look at different types of therapies and involve people of all ages. Also, it's important to make sure the people doing the therapy and checking if they're better don't know which type of therapy someone is getting.

output:
In a study looking at 159 clinical trials, researchers found that among 95,286 participants, those who took vitamin D had slightly fewer deaths overall compared to those who didn't take it. This happened in 56 trials that provided clear information. The studies involved mostly older women, with most participants being over 70 years old. Vitamin D was given for about 4.4 years on average. About half of the trials had little chance of having gotten the results wrong. The studies were mostly done in rich countries.

Vitamin D helped reduce deaths in all 56 trials combined. However, when they looked at different types of vitamin D, only vitamin D3 seemed to help lower death rates. Vitamin D3 reduced deaths by about 3% compared to those who didn’t get it. But some studies showed that vitamin D2 might actually increase deaths, though this isn’t very clear because there weren’t many studies showing this.

Vitamin D3 also seemed to help reduce cancer deaths. It didn’t cause more kidney stones or make people’s calcium levels too high. Vitamin D3 mixed with calcium made more people have kidney stones, and both vitamin D2 and calcitriol made people’s calcium levels go up too much.

Because some people dropped out of the studies, and not all studies told us about every death, we need more studies to be sure if vitamin D really helps or not. These new studies should use a placebo instead of vitamin D to see if the benefits are real.

output: In a review of fourteen studies involving 1260 participants, researchers looked at different ways to treat trigger fingers. The studies compared open surgery to steroid injections, which is the older and more common treatment, with steroid injections alone, which is less invasive and often used first. The studies showed that open surgery might help prevent the trigger finger from coming back less often, but it also hurts more. About 385 out of every 1000 people who got steroid shots had their trigger finger come back, while only 65 out of 1000 who had open surgery had it come back. This means open surgery helped keep the trigger finger from coming back in about 60% fewer people. However, right after the treatment, more people who had open surgery said their hands hurt a lot. It's not clear if open surgery helps make the hand work better or if it makes the hand feel better. There wasn't enough information to know if open surgery caused more problems like infections or injuries. Some people didn't finish the studies, so we don't know how well it worked for them. Overall, open surgery seems to be better at stopping the trigger finger from coming back, but it causes more pain right away. We're not sure if it helps the hand move better or if it causes more problems.

This research looked at a program called PIP, which helps parents with their children. They studied 846 mothers who had different issues like being sad after having a baby, feeling scared about their babies, or having been hurt by others. They compared PIP to regular care or other programs.

The study found that PIP didn't make moms feel less sad, but it helped more babies be more secure with their moms. This means the babies were happier and more trusting. PIP also seemed to help reduce some types of attachment problems in babies, like being too distant or confused.

However, PIP didn't seem to help moms feel better or improve how they interacted with their babies. It also didn't work better than other ways of helping parents and babies. The results weren't very strong because there weren't many people in the studies and the findings varied a bit.

The researchers think PIP might be helpful for making babies more secure, but more research is needed to know if it works for other things too. They also want to learn more about how PIP affects mommies's feelings and how they play with their babies.

This research looked at 19 studies that tested different treatments for kids who have problems with their stomachs. These studies involved 1453 children, mostly from clinics where doctors help kids with digestive issues. The studies lasted from one to five months, and they included kids aged 4 to 18 years old. Most of the studies focused on kids with symptoms like irritable bowel syndrome, which affects their digestion.

The studies tested different things like special bacteria called probiotics, fiber, and diets low in certain sugars. Researchers found that kids who took probiotics felt less pain in their bellies compared to those who didn't take them. They also found that kids who took probiotics were more likely to feel better overall. For example, out of every 8 kids taking probiotics, 1 kid felt much better. But the researchers weren't completely sure about this because some parts of the studies weren't clear or had too few kids in them.

They also looked at fiber and sugar-free diets but didn't find strong evidence that these helped kids feel better. More studies are needed to learn more about these treatments and to see if they work over a longer time.

Overall, the research suggests that probiotics might help kids with stomach problems feel less pain. Doctors might want to try giving probiotics to their patients. But more research is needed to know if probiotics really work and how best to use them. Future studies should look at whether probiotics help kids with different types of stomach problems and if they're safe.

In a review of 22 studies with over 2300 people who had ulcers, researchers looked at different ways to treat them with medicine applied directly to the skin. They found that using special bandages with medicine seemed to help more wounds heal compared to regular bandages. However, they weren't very sure if this was true because the studies were small and didn’t always follow people long enough. 

They also looked at whether putting medicine on the skin worked better than taking it inside the body. This wasn’t clear either, as some studies showed it might help, while others didn’t. 

The review suggests that using special bandages might help heal more ulcers, but it’s not very certain. It also says that taking medicine inside the body or applying it to the skin doesn’t seem to make much difference in how many ulcers heal or in how many bad things happen to people. 

Because there aren’t many good studies, doctors should try to do bigger, better-designed studies to learn more about which treatments work best for ulcers. This will help them decide which ones are safest and most effective.
